FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/dynamic_mcp_invocation.py
==============================================================================
"""DynamicMcpInvocationStage — `uses_tool` for a reader (1.3a.1.2).

Run order: 14 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4: no pre-1.3 row. ADR-0010's channel has two halves by now — 1.3a
emits `source → reader` for every catalogue read, 1.3a.1 emits the write
side (`mcp_server → writes_to → source` before B.3b-mcp-catalogue,
`mcp_server → writes_to → store → reads_from → source` since) — and
neither says *which tools the reader can call*. The reader's call is
`client.call_tool(name)`, and `name` is a runtime value: no static edge
exists from the agent to any tool, so a chain that starts at the
catalogue dies at the agent and `find_chain_groups` stays empty on the
one corpus that has the shape (measured: FinBot, 1.3a.1's report).

This stage closes that hop with the only evidence available: **the agent
that reads a catalogue can invoke every tool the catalogue describes.**
The analysis cannot know which one it will pick, so it links all of
them. That is the same trade-off `provides_tool` already makes — "can
call" is the candidate attack path until runtime monitoring can
separate it from "does call" (ADR-0015 decision 5, ADR-0009) — applied
one hop further out.

**Why `uses_tool`, and no new edge kind.** `uses_tool` already means
"an agent calls a tool" (ADR-0013). The invocation is real; only the
resolution is coarse. A new kind would have to mean something different,
and it would need a `find_chains` rule of its own.

**Position.** After `untrusted_source_writers` (11), because it walks
the `writes_to` edges that stage emits, and after `flow_kind` (12), for
the reason the three resolvers after it run there: they construct
control edges and pass `CONTROL_FLOW`, so the kind is named in one place
and this stage names no `flow_kind` of its own (ADR-0016).

Side effects: none. It reads the delta only — the agent nodes and the
three edge kinds — and creates no nodes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Edge
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import CONTROL_FLOW, edge_id

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


# The capability that makes a node a catalogue reader. The gate is on
# the reader, not on the source: 1.3a credits `reads_untrusted` on the
# component whose body makes the call (ADR-0009), and the source itself
# carries no capabilities by design.
READS_UNTRUSTED: str = "reads_untrusted"


# The source families whose reader can invoke what the source describes.
# One entry, deliberately: a tool catalogue names callable tools, and
# nothing else in ADR-0010's table does. Widening this set needs a rule
# for what the reader can invoke, not just for what it reads.
INVOCABLE_SOURCE_TYPES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"mcp_tool_description"})


class DynamicMcpInvocationStage:
    """`agent → uses_tool → tool` for a catalogue the agent reads."""

    name = "dynamic_mcp_invocation"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        agents = [
            node for node in delta.nodes
            if node.kind == "agent" and READS_UNTRUSTED in node.capabilities
        ]
        if not agents:
            return delta
        agent_ids = {node.id for node in agents}

        catalogues = {
            node.id for node in delta.nodes
            if node.kind == "untrusted_source"
            and node.attributes.get("source_type")
            in INVOCABLE_SOURCE_TYPES
        }
        if not catalogues:
            return delta

        read_by = _readers_of_catalogues(delta, catalogues, agent_ids)
        writers = _writers_of_catalogues(delta, catalogues)
        tools_by_server = _tools_by_server(delta)

        emitted = {edge.id for edge in delta.edges}
        for agent in sorted(agents, key=lambda node: node.id):
            targets = _invocable_tools(
                agent.id, read_by, writers, tools_by_server
            )
            for tool_id in sorted(targets):
                edge = _invocation_edge(agent.id, tool_id, ctx)
                if edge.id in emitted:
                    continue
                emitted.add(edge.id)
                delta.edges.append(edge)
        return delta


def _readers_of_catalogues(
    delta: "GraphDelta",
    catalogues: set[str],
    agent_ids: set[str],
) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """`catalogue id → [agent id]`, from 1.3a's read edges.

    The read edge is `has_access_to` with the source at the tail and the
    reader at the head, and it is the only statement the graph makes
    about *this agent reads this catalogue*. An agent whose capability
    says it reads untrusted data but whose read resolves to no node
    (a plain helper function has none) is not in this index, and gets no
    invocation edge: the catalogue would be a different agent's.
    """
    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for edge in delta.edges:
        if edge.kind != "has_access_to":
            continue
        if edge.source_id not in catalogues:
            continue
        if edge.target_id not in agent_ids:
            continue
        index.setdefault(edge.source_id, []).append(edge.target_id)
    return index


def _writers_of_catalogues(
    delta: "GraphDelta",
    catalogues: set[str],
) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """`catalogue id → [server id]`, from the write side of the channel.

    Two shapes, because the graph has two (ADR-0021 §2). Since
    B.3b-mcp-catalogue a server writes the *store* the catalogue reads
    from — `server --writes_to--> store`, `store --reads_from-->
    catalogue` — and before it the server wrote the catalogue itself
    (`server --writes_to--> catalogue`). Both are read, so a scanned
    delta in the new shape and a hand-built one in the old shape both
    resolve; the store hop is the graph's, not a lookup, and the
    `reads_from` target is what ties a store to *this* catalogue.
    """
    stores_by_catalogue = _stores_by_catalogue(delta, catalogues)
    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for edge in delta.edges:
        if edge.kind != "writes_to":
            continue
        if edge.target_id in catalogues:
            index.setdefault(edge.target_id, []).append(edge.source_id)
            continue
        for catalogue_id in stores_by_catalogue.get(edge.target_id, ()):
            index.setdefault(catalogue_id, []).append(edge.source_id)
    return index


def _stores_by_catalogue(
    delta: "GraphDelta",
    catalogues: set[str],
) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """`store id → [catalogue id]`, from the `reads_from` edges (§3)."""
    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for edge in delta.edges:
        if edge.kind != "reads_from":
            continue
        if edge.target_id not in catalogues:
            continue
        index.setdefault(edge.source_id, []).append(edge.target_id)
    return index


def _tools_by_server(delta: "GraphDelta") -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """`server id → [tool id]`, from the `provides_tool` edges."""
    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for edge in delta.edges:
        if edge.kind != "provides_tool":
            continue
        index.setdefault(edge.source_id, []).append(edge.target_id)
    return index


def _invocable_tools(
    agent_id: str,
    read_by: dict[str, list[str]],
    writers: dict[str, list[str]],
    tools_by_server: dict[str, list[str]],
) -> set[str]:
    """Every tool of every server that writes a catalogue this agent reads.

    Two hops and a set union, in the direction the graph stores: the
    agent's own read edge names the catalogue, the write side names the
    server (through the catalogue's store since B.3b-mcp-catalogue, or
    directly before it), and the server's `provides_tool` edges name the
    tools. A catalogue no server writes contributes nothing (no writer
    evidence exists for it), and a server that exposes no tool
    contributes nothing — both are absences, not failures.
    """
    tools: set[str] = set()
    for source_id, readers in read_by.items():
        if agent_id not in readers:
            continue
        for server_id in writers.get(source_id, ()):
            tools.update(tools_by_server.get(server_id, ()))
    return tools


def _invocation_edge(
    agent_id: str,
    tool_id: str,
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> Edge:
    """`uses_tool` from the agent to a tool its catalogue declares.

    `control` via `CONTROL_FLOW`, the same attributes `provides_tool`
    carries and for the same reason: the edge is an access path, and no
    value was traced (ADR-0016, decision 3). No
    `data_flow_confirmed` is written — the column is Layer 2's.
    """
    return Edge(
        id=edge_id(agent_id, tool_id, "uses_tool"),
        source_id=agent_id,
        target_id=tool_id,
        kind="uses_tool",
        host_id=ctx.host_id,
        **CONTROL_FLOW,
    )


__all__ = [
    "DynamicMcpInvocationStage",
    "INVOCABLE_SOURCE_TYPES",
    "READS_UNTRUSTED",
]


==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/entry_points.py
==============================================================================
"""EntryPointStage — `entry_point` nodes.

Run order: 6 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4: "**Entry point nodes** — from the entry points detector, including
HTTP, CLI, and Streamlit."

The id derivation differs per method because the identity differs: an
HTTP route is `(file, method, path)` — or `(file, method, handler)` when
the route has no path, which is every Django route, whose pattern lives
in `urls.py` (`normalizer_helpers.entry_point_id` states it) — a CLI entry
is the file itself (one per script), and a Streamlit entry is
`(file, call)`. The `entry_kind` attribute records which, so downstream
consumers can tell an MCP entry from a CLI one without re-deriving it.

A path-less route's **name** is `"<METHOD> <handler>"` for the same
reason: `"POST "` names nothing, and a Django route is named by the view
that handles it, not by a path the AST never held.

Side effects: fills `ctx.entry_node_by_handler` (handler → node id),
which the delegation and reachability stages read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Node
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import (
    HOST_ID,
    cli_entry_point_id,
    entry_point_id,
    streamlit_entry_point_id,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class EntryPointStage:
    """One node per detected entry point."""

    name = "entry_points"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        for ep in ctx.entry_points.entry_points:
            if ep.method == "CLI":
                node_id = cli_entry_point_id(ep.file_path)
                attrs = {
                    "source_file": ep.file_path,
                    "line_start": ep.line,
                    "method": "CLI",
                    "entry_kind": "cli",
                    "path": ep.path,
                }
                name = f"CLI:{ep.file_path}"
            elif ep.method == "STREAMLIT":
                node_id = streamlit_entry_point_id(ep.file_path, ep.path)
                attrs = {
                    "source_file": ep.file_path,
                    "line_start": ep.line,
                    "method": "STREAMLIT",
                    "entry_kind": "streamlit",
                    "path": ep.path,
                }
                name = f"Streamlit:{ep.file_path}:{ep.path}"
            else:
                node_id = entry_point_id(ep)
                attrs = {
                    "source_file": ep.file_path,
                    "line_start": ep.line,
                    "method": ep.method,
                    "path": ep.path,
                    "handler": ep.handler,
                }
                name = f"{ep.method} {ep.path or ep.handler}"

            ctx.entry_node_by_handler[ep.handler] = node_id
            delta.nodes.append(Node(
                id=node_id,
                kind="entry_point",
                name=name,
                host_id=HOST_ID,
                attributes=attrs,
            ))
        return delta

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/entry_to_sink.py
==============================================================================
"""EntryToSinkStage — entry point to same-file sink reachability.

Run order: 10 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4 lists this resolver as step 13 of the normalizer — after the detector
merge. The code it was split from called it *before* the merge, and that
is where it still runs, because the merge invalidates the ids it uses:
the resolver reads the TSA-side `sinks_by_file` index, so an edge built
after the merge points at a node the merge removed. On dvmcp that is six
dangling edges and a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` at write time.
Before the merge, the merge's own id remap re-points those edges to the
detector nodes. C4's order is the one that is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Edge, Node
from ..entry_points import EntryPointOutput
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import CONTROL_FLOW, HOST_ID, edge_id

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class EntryToSinkStage:
    """Link each entry point to the sinks its handler can reach."""

    name = "entry_to_sink"

    def apply(self, delta: GraphDelta, ctx: NormalizeContext) -> GraphDelta:
        delta.edges.extend(link_entry_points_to_sinks(
            entry_points=ctx.entry_points,
            sinks_by_file=ctx.sinks_by_file,
            entry_node_by_handler=ctx.entry_node_by_handler,
            imports_by_file=ctx.entry_points.imports,
        ))
        return delta


def link_entry_points_to_sinks(
    entry_points: EntryPointOutput,
    sinks_by_file: dict[str, list[Node]],
    entry_node_by_handler: dict[str, str],
    imports_by_file: dict[str, list[str]],
) -> list[Edge]:
    """Resolve entry_point → sink edges via same-file call reachability.

    For HTTP routes and Streamlit entries: BFS from the handler (or
    module for module-level entries) through the file's call graph.

    For CLI entries: the handler is the module itself. BFS starts at
    every top-level function and every name imported from another
    module, so a CLI script that calls `run()` imported from a
    helper module can reach sinks in that helper.

    Control-flow reachability, not dataflow. False positives accepted
    (ADR-0009).
    """
    edges: list[Edge] = []

    for ep in entry_points.entry_points:
        entry_id = entry_node_by_handler.get(ep.handler)
        if entry_id is None:
            continue

        sinks_here = sinks_by_file.get(ep.file_path, [])
        if not sinks_here:
            continue

        # Determine BFS start nodes.
        if ep.method in ("CLI", "STREAMLIT"):
            # Module-level entry: start from every function defined
            # in the file and every imported name that could resolve
            # to a function in another module.
            starts: set[str] = set(entry_points.call_graph.keys())
            for module in imports_by_file.get(ep.file_path, []):
                # Imported module name; functions called via
                # `module.func(...)` are recorded by their last segment
                # in the call graph. Add the module's last segment too,
                # in case the call graph recorded it as a Name call.
                starts.add(module.split(".")[-1])
        else:
            starts = {ep.handler}

        reachable: set[str] = set()
        for start in starts:
            reachable |= reachable_functions(
                start=start,
                call_graph=entry_points.call_graph,
            )

        for sink_node in sinks_here:
            if sink_node.name in reachable:
                edges.append(Edge(
                    id=edge_id(entry_id, sink_node.id, "has_access_to"),
                    source_id=entry_id,
                    target_id=sink_node.id,
                    kind="has_access_to",
                    host_id=HOST_ID,
                    # Control-flow reachability, not dataflow (ADR-0015):
                    # the call graph is name-based, so nothing is known
                    # about what data reaches the sink.
                    **CONTROL_FLOW,
                ))
    # Fallback for CLI and Streamlit entries with no same-file sinks:
    # link to all sinks in the project. The rationale is the same as
    # for the orphan-entry resolver: a CLI script can call into any
    # module, and we do not track cross-file calls here. False
    # positives are accepted (ADR-0009).
    all_sinks: list[Node] = []
    for sinks in sinks_by_file.values():
        all_sinks.extend(sinks)

    if all_sinks:
        for ep in entry_points.entry_points:
            if ep.method not in ("CLI", "STREAMLIT"):
                continue
            entry_id = entry_node_by_handler.get(ep.handler)
            if entry_id is None:
                continue
            # Only add fallback edges if this entry has no outgoing
            # has_access_to edge yet.
            has_edge = any(
                e.source_id == entry_id and e.kind == "has_access_to"
                for e in edges
            )
            if has_edge:
                continue
            for sink_node in all_sinks:
                edges.append(Edge(
                    id=edge_id(entry_id, sink_node.id, "has_access_to"),
                    source_id=entry_id,
                    target_id=sink_node.id,
                    kind="has_access_to",
                    host_id=HOST_ID,
                    attributes={"resolved_via": "cli_fallback"},
                    **CONTROL_FLOW,
                ))
    return edges


def reachable_functions(
    start: str,
    call_graph: dict[str, set[str]],
) -> set[str]:
    """BFS from `start` through the call graph, including `start` itself.

    The call graph is a name-keyed mapping: function name → set of
    called function names. Only `ast.Name` calls are recorded (see
    `entry_points._collect_call_names`), so attribute calls like
    `self._helper()` are not followed.
    """
    visited: set[str] = set()
    queue: list[str] = [start]
    while queue:
        current = queue.pop()
        if current in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(current)
        for next_name in call_graph.get(current, ()):
            if next_name not in visited:
                queue.append(next_name)
    return visited

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/flow_kind.py
==============================================================================
"""FlowKindStage — `flow_kind` on every AST edge (ADR-0016).

Run order: 13 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

Every edge the AST layer produces is a *control* edge. The AST knows
that one symbol reaches another; it does not know whether data moves
along that path, and after ADR-0016 it does not pretend to:

    flow_kind = "control"   on every edge this stage sees

`data_flow_confirmed` is neither read nor written here. It stays `NULL`
on AST edges and is populated only by Layer 2, which runs the `flow/`
analyzers against a `(tool_func, sink_call)` pair that runtime observed
(ADR-0016, decision 3). `flow.decision.flow_kind_for` remains the single
implementation of the value → kind mapping, and on Layer 1a nothing
calls it: the kind is `control` unconditionally.

A structural edge (`guards`) is a declaration, not a path, and is left
alone (ADR-0015, decision 5). `guardrail_edges` (stage 19) emits one,
already `structural`, and this stage skips it because `guards` is in
`STRUCTURAL_EDGE_KINDS`. A guardrail edge that arrives here must not be
downgraded to control.

Every other resolver that runs after this stage also constructs control
edges, and none of them writes `data_flow_confirmed`, so the whole AST
graph is `control` with a `NULL` flow confirmation, except for structural
edges.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...patterns import STRUCTURAL_EDGE_KINDS
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class FlowKindStage:
    """Set `flow_kind = "control"` on every AST edge (ADR-0016)."""

    name = "flow_kind"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        for edge in delta.edges:
            if edge.kind in STRUCTURAL_EDGE_KINDS:
                # A declaration, not a path (ADR-0015, decision 5).
                # `guardrail_edges` (stage 19) emits one, already
                # `structural`; skipping it here is what keeps it from
                # being downgraded to control.
                continue
            edge.flow_kind = "control"
        return delta

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/guardrail_capability.py
==============================================================================
"""GuardrailCapabilityStage — the `validates_input` capability (B.4-gap-1).

Run order: 2 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`) — before
`class_nodes` and `method_nodes`, which read the map this stage writes.

ADR-0024 §2 decides the first of three `guardrail` producers, and it is a
**negative capability**: `validates_input` is credited on a function or
method that

  - is **called from** the body of an agent, a tool or an entry point —
    a caller whose own capabilities include `calls_llm`,
    `invokes_mcp_tool` or `reads_untrusted` (`CALLER_CAPABILITIES`), and
  - carries **none of** `SINK_CAPABILITIES`, `AGENT_CAPABILITIES`,
    `LLM_ENDPOINT_CAPABILITIES`, `TOOL_CAPABILITIES`
    (`CLASSIFYING_CAPABILITIES`).

`classification.classify_method` yields `guardrail` from the capability
and `MethodNodeStage` builds the node, whose `observed_by` stays the
`Node` default `["ast"]` — the provenance ADR-0024 §1 assigns to a
capability-derived guardrail. This stage emits no node and no edge: it
writes one capability into `ctx.capabilities`, the per-symbol map
`capability_extractor` fills, and the node stages read it afterwards.
B.4a's `guardrail_edges` (stage 21) then links the node to the component
that calls it, by the same call graph this stage read.

**The caller's kind is read from capabilities, not from nodes.** Stage
2a runs before `class_nodes` (3), `method_nodes` (4) and `entry_points`
(5) have produced anything, so there is no `agent` / `tool` /
`entry_point` node to ask. The caller is a component because its
capabilities say so: `calls_llm` is an agent, `invokes_mcp_tool` is a
tool, `reads_untrusted` is a handler that reads untrusted input. That
union is this stage's reading of ADR-0024 §2's "called from the body of
a node with kind agent, tool, or entry_point" — the deterministic
capability is the node's kind, one stage early. A caller that is a tool
by *layout* only (a public method of an MCP server with no capability of
its own) is therefore not a caller here: the layout rule is
`classify_method`'s, and this stage does not read paths. That is a known
false negative, accepted with the others below.

**The false positives are the ADR's.** A capability-free helper called
from an agent body is a `validates_input` candidate; ADR-0024 §2 names
`logger.info(text)` and `print(text)` as the examples. The capability is
weak by design (ADR-0024 §6), the payload's `guardrails` section is a
signal the model weighs rather than a filter (ADR-0019 §2), and the
alternative — a table of names like `validate_input` — is ADR-0016
decision 7's removal and stays removed. One of the ADR's two examples
cannot be reached as written: `logger.info(text)` is an `ast.Attribute`
call, and the call graph holds `ast.Name` targets only, so that call is
invisible here — the same limitation that makes B.4a miss
`self.pii.check(x)`. The bare-name helper is what this stage credits.

**The call graph is flat, and its collisions are pre-existing.**
`ctx.entry_points.call_graph` is keyed by function name with no file
scope (`entry_points._collect_call_names` records `ast.Name` calls
only), so a call name is matched project-wide and a caller's
capabilities are looked up by name across every file. Two functions of
the same name in two files therefore collide: an agent calling
`validate_input` credits *every* symbol of that name the scan saw, and a
caller named `run` in a non-agent file counts as an agent caller if some
other file's `run` calls an LLM. This is the shape `guardrail_edges`
(B.4a) and `entry_to_sink` already read; narrowing the call graph to a
file or a scope is a separate item, and it is not this step's.

**A class is never a guardrail.** The capability is credited on a
function or a method, so a class symbol is not credited — and
`classify_class` has no guardrail branch, so a class would not become a
`guardrail` node if it were. The method is the node; the class keeps
whatever its own body yields.

**Determinism.** The symbols are walked in `tsa_output.symbols` order,
the two tests are set membership, and the credited pairs are returned
sorted, so the same scan credits the same symbols in the same order.

**The LLM classifier runs before this stage, not after.**
`run_scan.py` runs it before `normalize()`, on the map as the extractor
left it, so the classifier is never asked about a symbol this stage
credited. Precedence between the producers is ADR-0024 §1's and is
resolved by `DetectorMergeStage` (11), which replaces a capability-derived
node with a detector node at the same `(name, source_file)`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...patterns import (
    AGENT_CAPABILITIES,
    CLASSIFYING_CAPABILITIES,
)
from ..capability_extractor import FileCapabilities, SymbolCapabilities
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import caps_for_symbol

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta
    from ..models import TSASymbol


log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# The one capability this stage credits (ADR-0024 §2). The classification
# reads `patterns.GUARDRAIL_CAPABILITIES` — the set, not this name — and
# this constant must stay a member of it.
CREDITED_CAPABILITY = "validates_input"

# The capabilities that make a caller a component whose call on a
# capability-free symbol is evidence of a guardrail (ADR-0024 §2): an
# agent (`calls_llm`), a tool (`invokes_mcp_tool`), and an entry point —
# a handler that reads untrusted input (`reads_untrusted`), which is the
# capability the extractor credits on the read the request arrives in.
CALLER_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = AGENT_CAPABILITIES | frozenset({
    "reads_untrusted",
})


class GuardrailCapabilityStage:
    """`validates_input` on the symbols ADR-0024 §2's rule names."""

    name = "guardrail_capability"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        credited = credit_validates_input(ctx)
        if credited:
            log.debug(
                "guardrail_capability: %s credited on %d symbol(s)",
                CREDITED_CAPABILITY,
                len(credited),
            )
        return delta


def credit_validates_input(
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Credit `validates_input`; return the `(file_path, name)` pairs.

    The one entry point of the rule, so a caller that wants to know what
    the stage did does not have to diff the capability map. The pairs are
    sorted, which is what makes the answer stable across runs.

    Returns `[]` — and touches nothing — when no caller in the call graph
    is a component: a scan with no agent, tool or untrusted reader has no
    symbol this rule can be about, and the map is left exactly as the
    extractor wrote it.
    """
    callers = _component_callers(ctx)
    if not callers:
        return []

    callers_by_callee = _callers_by_callee(ctx.entry_points.call_graph)
    credited: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for symbol in ctx.tsa_output.symbols:
        if symbol.kind == "class":
            # A guardrail is a function or a method (ADR-0024 §2). A class
            # is not credited, and `classify_class` has no guardrail
            # branch to read the capability if it were: the method is the
            # node.
            continue
        if _is_a_component(ctx, symbol):
            continue
        if not callers_by_callee.get(symbol.name, frozenset()) & callers:
            continue
        _credit(ctx, symbol)
        credited.append((symbol.file_path, symbol.name))
    # A file may define the same name twice (two `run` methods in two
    # classes); the capability is one entry per `(file, name)` — the same
    # key `caps_for_symbol` reads — so the answer is deduplicated.
    return sorted(set(credited))


def _is_a_component(ctx: NormalizeContext, symbol: "TSASymbol") -> bool:
    """True when the symbol's own capabilities make it a component.

    The negative half of the rule (ADR-0024 §2): a symbol carrying a
    sink, agent, llm_endpoint or tool capability is that kind, and the
    classification's own branches say so. It is not a guardrail, and
    crediting it would only add a capability no branch reads.
    """
    own = caps_for_symbol(ctx.capabilities, symbol.file_path, symbol.name)
    return bool(set(own) & CLASSIFYING_CAPABILITIES)


def _component_callers(ctx: NormalizeContext) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Symbol names whose capabilities make them an agent, tool or entry.

    Read from `ctx.capabilities` across every file, and by name: the call
    graph this stage matches against is flat, so the caller is resolved
    the same way, and a name that is a component in one file is a
    component caller here (the documented collision in the module
    docstring).
    """
    callers: set[str] = set()
    for file_caps in ctx.capabilities.values():
        for symbol_caps in file_caps.symbols:
            if symbol_caps.capabilities & CALLER_CAPABILITIES:
                callers.add(symbol_caps.symbol_name)
    return frozenset(callers)


def _callers_by_callee(
    call_graph: dict[str, set[str]],
) -> dict[str, frozenset[str]]:
    """`callee name` → the callers that call it, from the flat graph.

    Built once per scan rather than scanned per symbol, and it is the
    same relation `guardrail_edges` (B.4a) tests one pair at a time:
    membership, not reachability — a symbol one hop away in a *chain*
    was not called by the component, so it is not evidence.
    """
    index: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for caller, callees in call_graph.items():
        for callee in callees:
            index.setdefault(callee, set()).add(caller)
    return {
        callee: frozenset(names) for callee, names in index.items()
    }


def _credit(ctx: NormalizeContext, symbol: "TSASymbol") -> None:
    """Write the capability into the symbol's map entry.

    The entry is matched the way `caps_for_symbol` matches — by file and
    symbol name — so the set the classifier reads is the set written
    here. A symbol with no capability of its own has no entry at all
    (`capability_extractor` records one only for a body that produced
    something), which is the ordinary case for the symbols this stage
    credits: the entry is created rather than looked up.
    """
    file_caps = ctx.capabilities.get(symbol.file_path)
    if file_caps is None:
        file_caps = FileCapabilities(file_path=symbol.file_path)
        ctx.capabilities[symbol.file_path] = file_caps
    for symbol_caps in file_caps.symbols:
        if symbol_caps.symbol_name == symbol.name:
            symbol_caps.capabilities.add(CREDITED_CAPABILITY)
            return
    file_caps.symbols.append(SymbolCapabilities(
        symbol_name=symbol.name,
        file_path=symbol.file_path,
        capabilities={CREDITED_CAPABILITY},
    ))

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/guardrail_edges.py
==============================================================================
"""GuardrailEdgeStage — `guards` (guardrail → component) from source evidence.

Run order: 21 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`) — last.

ADR-0019 §1 (emission). A `guards` edge is emitted only when the
source-level evidence establishes a protection relationship, and B.4a
recognizes two forms of it:

  - **Call site.** The component's body calls a function that is a
    `guardrail` node, recorded in the name-keyed call graph
    (`ctx.entry_points.call_graph`, the same one `entry_to_sink` and
    `delegation_edges` read). A *direct* call, not reachability: a
    component calls its guardrail, it does not reach it through a chain,
    so the test is membership and not the BFS `reachable_functions`
    runs.
  - **Decorator.** The component carries a decorator whose last dotted
    segment is the literal name `guardrail` — `@guardrail`,
    `@guardrail(...)`, `@mcp.guardrail(...)` — the same literal-name
    rule by which `framework_detectors/langchain.py` recognizes `@tool`.

Three forms are deliberately **not** evidence, and emit nothing
(ADR-0019 §1, "not emitted, deliberately"):

  - **Co-location.** A guardrail and a component in the same file are a
    file layout, not a defensive relationship. Emitting on co-location
    would be a false claim about protection — and, once B.4b weighs
    guardrails into confidence, a false claim that lowers confidence on
    chains no guardrail protects.
  - **A `guardrail` node with no call site and no decorator.** One wired
    in by dependency injection, a framework hook or an import side
    effect is a false negative, and it is accepted: a false negative
    leaves confidence where it was; a false positive moves it down for a
    reason the code does not support.
  - **`self.`-prefixed calls.** `self.pii.check(x)` is not in the call
    graph, which records `ast.Name` calls only
    (`entry_points._collect_call_names`). Widening the call graph is a
    separate item and a precondition for a second pass over ADR-0019.

The direction is `guardrail → component` — the guardrail is the actor,
the component is the object (ADR-0019 §1). The edge is `structural`
(`STRUCTURAL_FLOW`, ADR-0015 decision 5): a declaration, not a step in
an attack path, so `find_chains` never traverses it and this stage
cannot change what is enumerated. `observed_by` keeps the `Edge`
default (`["ast"]`) and `data_flow_confirmed` keeps its schema default
(`NULL`) — a guardrail's presence is not a statement about whether any
value reached it (ADR-0016).

Why its own stage, and why the last slot: the only ordering constraint
is the detector merge (stage 10) — a framework detector or the LLM
classifier can produce the `guardrail` node this resolver links from,
and the merge is what puts it in the delta. `lethal_trifecta` shares
that constraint and nothing else, and this stage shares it too, so it
takes the end of the pipeline, where the node set is final. Running last
also keeps it out of the way of the stages that already carry ordering
tests. `flow_kind` (stage 12) is *not* a constraint either way: it skips
`STRUCTURAL_EDGE_KINDS`, and this stage runs after it regardless.

**A known gap in what this stage can see.** No deterministic classifier
in the tree produces a `guardrail` node today: `classification.py`
answers `sink` / `agent` / `llm_endpoint` from capabilities and nothing
else (ADR-0016 decision 7 removed the name-and-path rule that used to
emit `guardrail`). The nodes this resolver links from arrive through
`ctx.framework_detection` — the LLM classifier's `DetectionResult`
(D.2) can name `guardrail` as a kind — and are merged into the delta by
`detector_merge`. The resolver reads them from `delta.nodes`, not from a
per-file index, for the same reason `cross_file_resolution` reads its
tools and sinks from the delta: the merge can replace a node, and the
replacement is what the graph keeps. Which is also why this stage cannot
run before stage 10.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Edge, Node
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import (
    STRUCTURAL_FLOW,
    edge_id,
    node_line_start,
    resolve_definition,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


# The kinds a guardrail protects. ADR-0007 describes the edge as
# "guardrail → component" and its table says "Guardrail protects an
# agent or a tool"; a `mcp_server` is the container those tools live in,
# not a body a guardrail is called from.
COMPONENT_KINDS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"agent", "tool"})

GUARDRAIL_KIND = "guardrail"

# The one decorator name B.4a recognizes, by its last dotted segment,
# and the name a `guardrail` node has to carry for the edge to point
# somewhere. Mirrors `framework_detectors/langchain.py::_decorator_name`,
# which recognizes `@tool` by the literal name `tool`: a project whose
# guardrail decorator is called something else (`@pii_guard`) is not
# emitted. That is a known false negative, consistent with ADR-0016's
# "no name tables" posture (ADR-0019 §1).
GUARDRAIL_DECORATOR_NAME = "guardrail"


class GuardrailEdgeStage:
    """`guards` (guardrail → component) from a call site or a decorator."""

    name = "guardrail_edges"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        delta.edges.extend(link_guardrails_to_components(delta, ctx))
        return delta


def link_guardrails_to_components(
    delta: "GraphDelta",
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> list[Edge]:
    """Every `(guardrail, component)` pair the source evidence supports.

    One edge per pair, id-deduplicated: a pair the delta already links
    keeps the edge it has. The guardrail and component nodes are read
    from `delta.nodes` — the stage runs after the merge, and the delta is
    what the graph keeps. A node with no `source_file`, or one whose
    definition is not in its file, contributes no evidence: the resolver
    does not guess.
    """
    guardrails = [n for n in delta.nodes if n.kind == GUARDRAIL_KIND]
    components = [n for n in delta.nodes if n.kind in COMPONENT_KINDS]
    if not guardrails or not components:
        return []

    existing = {edge.id for edge in delta.edges}
    edges: list[Edge] = []
    for guardrail in guardrails:
        for component in components:
            evidence = _evidence(guardrail, component, ctx)
            if not evidence:
                continue
            guard_edge = Edge(
                id=edge_id(guardrail.id, component.id, "guards"),
                source_id=guardrail.id,
                target_id=component.id,
                kind="guards",
                host_id=ctx.host_id,
                # Which forms of evidence resolved the pair —
                # `delegation_edges` carries `resolved_via` for the same
                # reason. Sorted, so the value is deterministic.
                attributes={"resolved_via": ",".join(sorted(evidence))},
                # A declaration, not a path (ADR-0015, decision 5). No
                # data-flow claim either (ADR-0016): spreading
                # `STRUCTURAL_FLOW` leaves `data_flow_confirmed` at its
                # schema default.
                **STRUCTURAL_FLOW,
            )
            if guard_edge.id in existing:
                continue
            existing.add(guard_edge.id)
            edges.append(guard_edge)
    return edges


def _evidence(
    guardrail: Node,
    component: Node,
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> set[str]:
    """The forms of evidence tying `guardrail` to `component`, if any."""
    definition = _definition_for(component, ctx)
    evidence: set[str] = set()
    if _calls_guardrail(guardrail, component, definition, ctx):
        evidence.add("call_graph")
    if _decorated_by_guardrail(guardrail, definition):
        evidence.add("decorator")
    return evidence


def _definition_for(
    component: Node,
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> ast.AST | None:
    """The class or function definition behind a component node, or None.

    A `tool` node is a function or method; an `agent` node is a class.
    Resolution goes through `resolve_definition` with the node's
    `line_start`, the same way `body_attributes` finds the body a node
    came from — a file may define the same name twice.

    Returns None when the node carries no `source_file`, or when the file
    does not define the name at all (a detector-created node in a file
    the manifest does not hold, or a name the TSA index and the file
    index disagree about).
    """
    file_path = _source_file(component)
    if file_path is None:
        return None
    line_start = node_line_start(component)
    if component.kind == "agent":
        return resolve_definition(
            ctx.classes_for(file_path), component.name, line_start
        )
    return resolve_definition(
        ctx.functions_for(file_path), component.name, line_start
    )


def _body_call_names(
    component: Node,
    definition: ast.AST | None,
) -> frozenset[str]:
    """The call-graph keys whose call set is the component's own body.

    A `tool` node is a function, so its own name is the key
    (`entry_points` records `call_graph[func.name]` per definition). An
    `agent` node is a class: its body is its methods, and the call graph
    keys those by method name, so every method the class defines
    directly is a key. An agent node whose class definition is not
    visible contributes none — the resolver does not fall back to the
    file, because a call anywhere in the file is co-location, not
    evidence about this component.
    """
    if component.kind != "agent":
        return frozenset({component.name})
    if not isinstance(definition, ast.ClassDef):
        return frozenset()
    return frozenset(
        item.name
        for item in definition.body
        if isinstance(item, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
    )


def _calls_guardrail(
    guardrail: Node,
    component: Node,
    definition: ast.AST | None,
    ctx: NormalizeContext,
) -> bool:
    """True when the component's body calls the guardrail by bare name.

    Membership, not reachability: the call graph maps a function name to
    the names it calls, so a guardrail one hop away in a *chain* does not
    count — only a call in the component's own body does. Only
    `ast.Name` call targets are recorded, which is what makes
    `self.pii.check(x)` invisible (the accepted false negative of
    ADR-0019 §1).
    """
    call_graph = ctx.entry_points.call_graph
    for key in _body_call_names(component, definition):
        if guardrail.name in call_graph.get(key, ()):
            return True
    return False


def _decorated_by_guardrail(
    guardrail: Node,
    definition: ast.AST | None,
) -> bool:
    """True when the component carries the literal `@guardrail` decorator.

    Two conditions, both required: the decorator's last dotted segment is
    `guardrail`, and a `guardrail` node carries that name — the second is
    what makes the edge point at a node rather than at a string. A
    decorator named anything else emits nothing, even when a `guardrail`
    node shares its name (ADR-0019 §1).
    """
    if guardrail.name != GUARDRAIL_DECORATOR_NAME:
        return False
    for decorator in _decorators(definition):
        if _decorator_name(decorator) == GUARDRAIL_DECORATOR_NAME:
            return True
    return False


def _decorators(definition: ast.AST | None) -> tuple[ast.expr, ...]:
    """The decorator expressions of a class or function definition."""
    if definition is None:
        return ()
    return tuple(getattr(definition, "decorator_list", ()))


def _decorator_name(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
    """The last dotted segment of a decorator name, or None.

    Mirrors `framework_detectors/langchain.py::_decorator_name`:
    `@guardrail`, `@guardrail(...)`, `@mcp.guardrail` and
    `@mcp.guardrail(...)` all answer `guardrail`. Any other expression
    (a subscript, a lambda) answers None.
    """
    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
        node = node.func
    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
        return node.id
    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
        return node.attr
    return None


def _source_file(node: Node) -> str | None:
    """The relative path a node was found in, when it carries one."""
    value = node.attributes.get("source_file")
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/intra_file_edges.py
==============================================================================
"""IntraFileEdgeStage — `provides_tool` and same-file `has_access_to`.

Run order: 5 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4: "**Intra-file edges** — `provides_tool` (MCP server to tool),
`has_access_to` (tool to sink)."

Both edges are candidates, not calls: every tool in a file is linked to
every sink in the same file. Neither edge claims data flow. After
ADR-0016 this stage no longer runs the Flow Analyzer on the
`(tool_func, sink_call)` pair it can see: its result does not land on an
AST edge. Layer 2 runs the analyzer against a pair that runtime observed.
Every edge here is `flow_kind = "control"` with `data_flow_confirmed`
left at its schema default (`NULL`); `FlowKindStage` pins the kind.

A framework detector may still record a tool's signature result on the
tool *node* (`tool_data_flow`, 1.2a.2). Nothing copies it onto an edge
any more: an AST edge does not carry a data-flow claim (ADR-0016,
decision 3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Edge
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import (
    CONTROL_FLOW,
    edge_id,
    server_name_for_file,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class IntraFileEdgeStage:
    """`provides_tool` (server → tool) and `has_access_to` (tool → sink)."""

    name = "intra_file_edges"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        _provides_tool(delta, ctx)
        _has_access_to(delta, ctx)
        return delta


def _provides_tool(delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext) -> None:
    """One `provides_tool` edge per tool, when the file is an MCP server."""
    for file_path, tools in ctx.tools_by_file.items():
        server_name = server_name_for_file(file_path)
        if server_name is None:
            continue
        server_id = ctx.mcp_servers.get(server_name)
        if server_id is None:
            continue
        for tool_node in tools:
            delta.edges.append(Edge(
                id=edge_id(server_id, tool_node.id, "provides_tool"),
                source_id=server_id,
                target_id=tool_node.id,
                kind="provides_tool",
                host_id=ctx.host_id,
                # Access path, not a declaration (ADR-0015, decision 5):
                # "the agent can call the tool" is the candidate attack
                # path until runtime monitoring separates the two.
                # Control, and no data-flow claim: the edge leaves
                # `data_flow_confirmed` at its schema default (ADR-0016,
                # decision 3).
                **CONTROL_FLOW,
            ))


def _has_access_to(delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext) -> None:
    """Every tool in a file to every sink in the same file.

    Reachability, not dataflow (ADR-0016, decision 3): the edge records
    that the tool and the sink share a file. Whether the tool body calls
    the sink — and whether an argument reaches it — is a question the
    AST layer does not answer and does not store.
    """
    for file_path, tools in ctx.tools_by_file.items():
        sinks = ctx.sinks_by_file.get(file_path, [])
        if not sinks:
            continue
        for tool_node in tools:
            for sink_node in sinks:
                delta.edges.append(Edge(
                    id=edge_id(
                        tool_node.id, sink_node.id, "has_access_to"
                    ),
                    source_id=tool_node.id,
                    target_id=sink_node.id,
                    kind="has_access_to",
                    host_id=ctx.host_id,
                ))

FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/lethal_trifecta.py
==============================================================================
"""LethalTrifectaStage — the `lethal_trifecta` node attribute (1.3d).

Run order: 19 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`) — second to last.

One node fact, derived from the node's own capabilities: does this node
read untrusted input, can it read secrets, and can it get data out?
That is ADR-0009's lethal trifecta, spelled by the three sets in
`patterns.py`, and it is what ADR-0012 scores +5 for. Until 1.3d the
combination was computed inside `graph/query.py`'s scorer and nowhere
else, which made the fact a property of one score rather than something
the prompt (1.3e), the report, or any other consumer could read off the
node. The stage writes it down once per scan.

Why its own stage rather than a branch inside `body_attributes`:

  - the two answer different questions about different inputs.
    `body_attributes` reads *source* — it resolves the function or class
    behind a tool or sink node and parses its body — and it is scoped to
    those two kinds. This stage reads *capabilities*, which every node
    kind can carry, and touches no file. Folding it in would make a
    stage named for bodies the authority on a capability combination,
    and would leave the question "which node kinds does it visit?"
    answered differently in two halves of one loop.
  - every other concern in the pipeline has its own stage and its own
    test file; this one is ~10 lines and reads well on its own.

Why second to last, and why after `body_attributes`: the only ordering
constraint is the detector merge (stage 10), which can replace a node and
the replacement is what the graph keeps — the same reason
`body_attributes` runs late. This stage has no constraint relative to
`body_attributes`, so it sits at the end of the pipeline, where the node
set is final. `guardrail_edges` (B.4a, stage 19) takes the very last
slot, and it shares this stage's one constraint and no other, so the two
do not read what the other writes and their order is not load-bearing —
see `normalizer_stages.guardrail_edges`.

The attribute is written on **every** node, `True` or `False`, and the
stage is its only producer, so it recomputes rather than guarding: a
node that no longer satisfies the combination loses a flag it had. The
`body_attributes` "leave an existing attribute alone" guard exists
because a detector can arrive with a better answer for that attribute;
nothing produces this one, and a stale flag would be worse than a
recomputed one.

Storing `False` rather than omitting it is deliberate, and it is the
`body_attributes` posture read closely: that stage *does* store its
negative (`returns_data = False`, `sink_data_flow = "unknown"` — see
`tests/test_ast_normalizer.py`), and its attributes may be absent only
because they are node-kind specific. This attribute is not kind
specific — any node can read untrusted input and hold secrets — so
absence cannot mean "not applicable". It means "not computed", which is
what `graph/query.py`'s scorer needs to tell apart from a computed
`False` in order to fall back to the capability walk on a graph written
before 1.3d.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...patterns import lethal_trifecta_caps
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class LethalTrifectaStage:
    """Record ADR-0009's lethal trifecta as a node attribute."""

    name = "lethal_trifecta"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        for node in delta.nodes:
            node.attributes["lethal_trifecta"] = bool(
                lethal_trifecta_caps(node.capabilities)
            )
        return delta

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/llm_endpoints.py
==============================================================================
"""LlmEndpointStage — `llm_endpoint` nodes from LLM configs.

Run order: 8 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4: "**LLM endpoint nodes** — from the LLM extractor."

The extractor reads config files (`.env`, `.py`, `.yaml`, ...), so
several files may describe the same endpoint; `deduplicated()` collapses
them before a node is built. The id is a hash of provider + model +
base_url, so two configs for the same model produce one node.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Node
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import (
    HOST_ID,
    llm_endpoint_id,
    llm_endpoint_name,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class LlmEndpointStage:
    """One node per distinct configured LLM endpoint."""

    name = "llm_endpoints"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        for llm_ep in ctx.llm_output.deduplicated():
            delta.nodes.append(Node(
                id=llm_endpoint_id(llm_ep),
                kind="llm_endpoint",
                name=llm_endpoint_name(llm_ep),
                host_id=HOST_ID,
                attributes={
                    "source_file": llm_ep.source_file,
                    "provider": llm_ep.provider,
                    "model": llm_ep.model or "",
                    "base_url": llm_ep.base_url or "",
                },
            ))
        return delta

==============================================================================
FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/mcp_entry_synthesis.py
==============================================================================
"""McpEntrySynthesisStage — virtual MCP entry (Resolver 3).

Run order: 16 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Edge, Node
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import (
    CONTROL_FLOW,
    HOST_ID,
    edge_id,
    mcp_entry_point_id,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class McpEntrySynthesisStage:
    """Synthesize one entry point per framework-detected MCP server."""

    name = "mcp_entry_synthesis"

    def apply(self, delta: GraphDelta, ctx: NormalizeContext) -> GraphDelta:
        delta.edges.extend(link_mcp_entries_to_tools(delta=delta))
        return delta


def link_mcp_entries_to_tools(delta: GraphDelta) -> list[Edge]:
    """Create virtual entry points for framework-detected MCP servers
    and link them to the tools they expose.

    Side effects: appends the new entry_point nodes to `delta.nodes`.
    Returns only the new edges (the caller appends them).
    """
    edges: list[Edge] = []

    # Index tools by parent_server, only those with framework provenance.
    tools_by_parent: dict[str, list[Node]] = {}
    for node in delta.nodes:
        if node.kind != "tool":
            continue
        parent = node.attributes.get("parent_server")
        if parent:
            tools_by_parent.setdefault(parent, []).append(node)

    for mcp_node in delta.nodes:
        if mcp_node.kind != "mcp_server":
            continue
        framework = mcp_node.attributes.get("framework")
        if not framework:
            continue

        entry_id = mcp_entry_point_id(mcp_node.name)

        delta.nodes.append(Node(
            id=entry_id,
            kind="entry_point",
            name=f"MCP:{mcp_node.name}",
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            attributes={
                "source_file": mcp_node.attributes.get("source_file", ""),
                "mcp_server_name": mcp_node.name,
                "framework": framework,
                "entry_kind": "mcp",
            },
        ))

        for tool_node in tools_by_parent.get(mcp_node.name, []):
            edges.append(Edge(
                id=edge_id(entry_id, tool_node.id, "delegates_to"),
                source_id=entry_id,
                target_id=tool_node.id,
                kind="delegates_to",
                host_id=HOST_ID,
                attributes={"resolved_via": "mcp_entry"},
                # The MCP client → tool path is the protocol channel.
                # Control, and no data-flow claim: a detector may have
                # recorded whether the tool takes arguments (1.2a.2),
                # but that result stays on the node — it does not land
                # on the edge (ADR-0016, decision 3).
                **CONTROL_FLOW,
            ))

    return edges

FILE: src/aicorellator/parsing/normalizer_stages/mcp_server_nodes.py

"""McpServerNodeStage — `mcp_server` nodes from file paths.

Run order: 1 of 21 (see `normalizer_stages.STAGES`).

C4: "**MCP server nodes** — from file paths under `mcp/servers/`." The
detector-discovered servers (`FastMCP(...)`, `Server(...)`) arrive with
the detector merge instead; this stage covers the convention-based
layout, where the directory name is the server name.

Side effects: fills `ctx.mcp_servers` (server name → node id), which the
`provides_tool` edges and the agent → server edges read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from ...graph.models import Node
from ..classification import classify_file
from ..normalizer_context import NormalizeContext
from ..normalizer_helpers import HOST_ID, mcp_server_id

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from ..ast_normalizer import GraphDelta


class McpServerNodeStage:
    """One `mcp_server` node per `mcp/servers/<name>/server.py` path."""

    name = "mcp_server_nodes"

    def apply(
        self, delta: "GraphDelta", ctx: NormalizeContext
    ) -> "GraphDelta":
        for file_entry in ctx.manifest.files:
            c = classify_file(file_entry.path)
            if c is None:
                continue
            server_name = c.attributes["server_name"]
            if server_name in ctx.mcp_servers:
                continue
            node_id = mcp_server_id(server_name)
            ctx.mcp_servers[server_name] = node_id
            delta.nodes.append(Node(
                id=node_id,
                kind="mcp_server",
                name=server_name,
                host_id=HOST_ID,
                attributes={"server_name": server_name},
                content_hash=None,
            ))
        return delta
