def test_sink_self_attribute_from_parameter_is_data() -> None:
    """`self.q = q; self.db.delete(self.q)` is a data flow (1.2a.3g).

    The sink stores its own parameter on the instance and hands it to
    the dangerous call. Values are not followed, but the name is: the
    attribute is parameter-derived because this body assigned it from a
    parameter.
    """
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q = q
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_self_attribute_from_a_local_var_is_data() -> None:
    """A local variable on the right-hand side is enough (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        path = os.path.join("/tmp", q)
        self.q = path
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_self_attribute_chain_is_data() -> None:
    """`self.q = q; self.r = self.q; ... self.r` follows the chain.

    The "right-hand side is another derived attribute" rule is applied
    until nothing changes, so a chain of any length is followed
    (1.2a.3g).
    """
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q = q
        self.r = self.q
        self.s = self.r
        self.db.delete(self.s)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_self_attribute_from_a_literal_is_unknown() -> None:
    """`self.q = "literal"` is not parameter-derived (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q = "literal"
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_sink_self_attribute_from_a_call_is_unknown() -> None:
    """A call result on the right-hand side is not a name (ADR-0001)."""
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q = fetch(q)
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_sink_self_attribute_not_assigned_here_is_unknown() -> None:
    """An attribute on `self` that this body never assigns (1.2a.3g).

    `self.q` may hold anything the rest of the class put there — an
    assignment in another method is not visible, because each body is
    analyzed on its own (1.2a.5).
    """
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_sink_attribute_of_another_object_is_unknown() -> None:
    """`other.attr` where `other` is a global is not `self.attr`.

    Changed by 1.2a.3j: when `other` is a *parameter* the attribute is
    parameter-derived and the value is `parameter_match` — 1.2a.3j
    extended the rule from `self.X` to `param.X`. What this test keeps
    pinning is the part that did not change: an attribute whose base is
    neither `self`, nor a parameter, nor a local variable is someone
    else's state, and the body has no evidence about it.
    """
    src = """
    def delete(self):
        self.db.delete(other.attr)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_sink_self_attribute_annotated_and_augmented_is_data() -> None:
    """`self.q: str = q` and `self.q += q` are assignments too (1.2a.3g)."""
    annotated = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q: str = q
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    augmented = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q += q
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(annotated).kind == "parameter_match"
    assert _sink_body(augmented).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_fstring_with_parameter_is_data() -> None:
    """An f-string built from the sink's parameter reaches the call.

    This is the dvmcp `VulnerableChatAssistant` shape: the URL is
    formatted at the call site (1.2a.3g).
    """
    src = """
    def fetch(self, q):
        requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/{q}")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_fstring_without_a_parameter_is_unknown() -> None:
    """No parameter-derived interpolation → no evidence (1.2a.3g).

    An f-string is never `literal_only`: it is evaluated at runtime even
    when every interpolation is a constant.
    """
    src = """
    def fetch(self, q):
        requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/tags")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_sink_fstring_with_a_derived_attribute_is_data() -> None:
    """`self.base = base` then `f"{self.base}/tags"` is data (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    def fetch(self, base):
        self.base = base
        requests.get(f"{self.base}/api/tags")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_dict_with_parameter_value_is_data() -> None:
    """`requests.post(url, json={"q": q})` carries the parameter.

    The dict is the payload; the values are what the sink consumes
    (1.2a.3g).
    """
    src = """
    def post(self, q):
        requests.post(URL, json={"q": q})
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_dict_with_local_var_value_is_data() -> None:
    """The dvmcp shape: a local list built from the parameter.

    `messages` is a local variable, and the body under analysis is the
    one that built it (1.2a.3g).
    """
    src = """
    def chat(self, user_message):
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_message}]
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/chat",
            json={"model": MODEL, "messages": messages},
        )
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_dict_all_literals_is_literal_only() -> None:
    """A dict of constants stays `literal_only` (1.2a.4)."""
    src = """
    def post(self, q):
        requests.post("https://example.com/api", json={"a": 1, "b": "x"})
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_sink_list_with_parameter_is_data() -> None:
    """A command list with the parameter in it is a data flow (1.2a.3g).

    Changed by 1.2a.3g: `[param, "a"]` used to be `unknown` (1.2a.4).
    """
    src = """
    def convert(self, q):
        subprocess.run(["docker", q])
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_tuple_with_parameter_is_data() -> None:
    """Tuples follow the same rule as lists (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    def convert(self, q):
        subprocess.run(("docker", q))
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_orm_delete_with_parameter() -> None:
    """The FinBot `delete_file` shape: the sink parameter reaches the
    ORM delete call (1.2a.3)."""
    src = """
    def delete_file(self, f):
        self.db.delete(f)
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_orm_delete_with_local_var() -> None:
    """A local variable derived from the sink parameter is still data."""
    src = """
    def delete_file(self, file_id):
        record = self.db.query(file_id).first()
        self.db.delete(record)
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_orm_delete_with_literal() -> None:
    """Only a constant reaches the ORM delete call → literal_only."""
    src = """
    def purge(self):
        self.db.delete("literal-id")
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "literal_only"


# ============================================================
# Commit exception (1.2a.3c)
# ============================================================

def test_commit_call_is_recognized_by_qualifier() -> None:
    """Every documented qualifier is a commit call (1.2a.3c)."""
    for qualifier in (
        "db", "session", "repository", "repo",
        "transaction", "connection", "conn",
    ):
        src = f"""
        def flush(self, oid):
            {qualifier}.commit()
        """
        call = _sink_call(_func(src), "commit")
        assert _is_commit_call(call), qualifier


def test_commit_call_requires_a_qualifier() -> None:
    """A bare `commit()` is not a commit call: no qualifier, no match."""
    for body in ("commit()", "commit_all()", "flush()", "commit_now()"):
        src = f"""
        def flush(self, oid):
            self.{body}
        """
        call = _sink_call(_func(src), body.split("(")[0])
        assert not _is_commit_call(call), body


def test_commit_only_body_with_parameter_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """The FinBot `toggle_admin` shape: the body's only dangerous call is
    a bare `db.commit()`, which persists the session (1.2a.3c)."""
    src = """
    def toggle_admin(self, user_id):
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_commit_only_body_on_session_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """`session.commit()` gets the same treatment as `db.commit()`."""
    src = """
    def update_status(self, order_id):
        session.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_commit_after_a_write_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """The write already supplied `parameter_match`; the commit adds the
    same value — the strongest result is unchanged."""
    src = """
    def mark_as_read(self, email_id):
        self.db.add(email_id)
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_commit_exception_does_not_apply_to_subprocess() -> None:
    """`subprocess.run()` with no arguments is not a commit → unknown."""
    src = """
    def run_task(self, cmd):
        subprocess.run()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_commit_exception_does_not_apply_to_os_system() -> None:
    """`os.system()` with no arguments is not a commit → unknown."""
    src = """
    def shell_out(self, cmd):
        os.system()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_commit_contributes_while_subprocess_run_does_not() -> None:
    """The commit carries the result even when a bare shell call sits in
    the same body."""
    src = """
    def toggle(self, user_id):
        self.db.commit()
        subprocess.run()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_commit_only_body_without_parameters_is_unknown() -> None:
    """Edge case (1.2a.3c): a sink with no parameters has nothing
    parameter-derived to persist, so `parameter_match` would claim
    evidence that does not exist — the commit contributes nothing."""
    src = """
    def flush(self):
        self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_commit_without_a_write_promotes_a_literal_only_body() -> None:
    """Accepted consequence of the rule: the commit is treated as a
    parameter-derived persistence step, so a body whose only write is a
    constant still reports `parameter_match`."""
    src = """
    def update_status(self, order_id):
        cursor.execute("UPDATE orders SET status = 'done'")
        self.conn.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_commit_of_a_qualifier_outside_the_capabilities_counts() -> None:
    """`conn.commit` is not a sink capability, but the commit exception
    still recognizes it (the sink comes from the `execute` call)."""
    src = """
    def set_flag(self, flag):
        self.session.execute("UPDATE configs SET flag = 1")
        self.conn.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"

# --- Private qualifiers (1.2a.3e) ---

def test_commit_call_accepts_a_private_qualifier() -> None:
    """`_conn.commit` is `conn.commit` on a private connection — the
    spelling mcploitable uses throughout (1.2a.3e)."""
    src = """
    def seed(self):
        self._conn.commit()
    """
    call = _sink_call(_func(src), "commit")
    assert _is_commit_call(call)


def test_private_conn_commit_with_parameter_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """mcploitable's `create_ticket(customer, subject, body)` shape: the
    body's persistence step is a `_conn.commit()` the capability
    extractor does not treat as a write, so only the commit exception
    can carry the data — and it does once the underscore is ignored
    (1.2a.3e)."""
    src = """
    def create_ticket(self, customer, body):
        self._conn.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_private_conn_commit_without_parameters_is_unknown() -> None:
    """The 1.2a.3c edge-case rule is unaffected by the normalization: a
    parameterless sink has no parameter-derived state to persist."""
    src = """
    def flush(self):
        self._conn.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_private_commit_does_not_outrank_a_literal_only_body() -> None:
    """`self._db.add("literal")` + `self._conn.commit()` — the write is a
    constant, the commit still counts (the accepted 1.2a.3c
    consequence), now also for a private qualifier."""
    src = """
    def seed(self, tag):
        self._db.add("literal")
        self._conn.commit()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"




def test_subprocess_run_with_empty_string_stays_literal_only() -> None:
    """A commit-shaped exception must not widen literal calls (1.2a.3c)."""
    src = """
    def run_task(self):
        subprocess.run("")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "literal_only"


# ============================================================
# Class-body sink analyzer (1.2a.5)
# ============================================================

def _class(source: str) -> ast.ClassDef:
    """Parse `source` and return its first class definition."""
    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
            return node
    raise AssertionError("no class found in source")


def _class_sink(source: str) -> FlowDecision:
    """Analyze the first class in `source` as a sink body."""
    return analyze_sink_class(_class(source))


def test_class_sink_init_parameter_reaches_dangerous_call() -> None:
    """A constructor parameter reaches the dangerous call (1.2a.5).

    The same case spelled as a stored attribute — `self.db.delete(self.q)`
    — is also `parameter_match` since 1.2a.3g; see
    `test_class_sink_self_attribute_argument_is_parameter_match`.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.db.delete(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_call_parameter_reaches_dangerous_call() -> None:
    """`__call__`'s parameter reaches `os.remove`: the class is invoked."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def __call__(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_async_call_is_analyzed() -> None:
    """`async def __call__` is the same scope (AsyncFunctionDef)."""
    src = """
    class X:
        async def __call__(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_literal_only_init() -> None:
    """A constructor whose dangerous call takes a constant only."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_class_sink_without_dangerous_call_is_unknown() -> None:
    """`self.q = q` alone is no flow evidence."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.q = q
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_commit_only_init_with_parameter_is_data() -> None:
    """The commit exception applies at class level too (1.2a.3c).

    The constructor declares a parameter, so `self.db.commit()` persists
    the class's data and the class is `parameter_match`. The preceding
    `self.db.delete(self.q)` is `parameter_match` on its own as well
    (1.2a.3g), so the commit is not what decides this value.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.q = q
            self.db.delete(self.q)
            self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_commit_only_init_without_parameter_is_unknown() -> None:
    """The parameterless rule holds for class bodies as well.

    A constructor with no parameters has no parameter-derived state to
    persist, so a bare commit contributes nothing.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self):
            self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_self_attribute_argument_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """`self.db.delete(self.q)` is data when the body stored `q`.

    Changed by 1.2a.3g: the stored attribute used to be `unknown` (the
    1.2a.5 sketch called it a known limitation). The class body is the
    scope, and `self.q` is assigned from the constructor's parameter.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.q = q
            self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_self_attribute_from_a_literal_is_unknown() -> None:
    """`self.q = "literal"` then `self.q` in the call is `unknown`."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.q = "literal"
            self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_attribute_from_another_method_is_unknown() -> None:
    """Each method is its own scope: `__init__` does not help `delete`.

    1.2a.5 analyzes every method separately, so an attribute stored in
    one is not visible in another (1.2a.3g).
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.q = q
        def delete(self):
            self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_fstring_argument_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """The dvmcp shape, at class level: a formatted URL with the sink's
    parameter (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def fetch(self, q):
            requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/{q}")
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_dict_argument_with_local_var_is_parameter_match() -> None:
    """The `VulnerableChatAssistant` shape: `messages` is a local built
    from the parameter and handed to the sink in a dict (1.2a.3g)."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def chat(self, user_message):
            messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_message}]
            requests.post(BASE_URL, json={"messages": messages})
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_strongest_scope_wins() -> None:
    """Any `parameter_match` beats a `literal_only`, in either order."""
    literal_then_parameter = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
        def __call__(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    parameter_then_literal = """
    class X:
        def __init__(self, q):
            self.db.delete(q)
        def __call__(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
    """
    assert _class_sink(literal_then_parameter).kind == "parameter_match"
    assert _class_sink(parameter_then_literal).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_plain_method_is_analyzed() -> None:
    """Every method counts, not only `__init__`/`__call__` (1.2a.5).

    A class-kind sink is a container of callable entry points; the
    caller invokes `delete(q)` and `q` reaches the dangerous call there.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def delete(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_repository_style_add_and_commit_is_data() -> None:
    """`claim_username`-style method: the parameter is written and
    committed through the session (FinBot `UserProfileRepository`).
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def claim_username(self, user_id, username):
            profile = self.db.query(Profile).filter_by(username=username)
            profile.user_id = user_id
            profile.username = username
            self.db.add(profile)
            self.db.commit()
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_execute_method_parameter_reaches_subprocess() -> None:
    """`execute_mcp_tool`-style method: the parameter is the command
    (dvmcp `DVMCPClient`).
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def execute(self, tool_name, params):
            subprocess.run(params, shell=True)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_method_literal_only() -> None:
    """A method whose dangerous call takes a constant only
    (mcploitable `Handler.do_GET`-style, literal URL).
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        def do_GET(self):
            urllib.request.urlopen("http://example.com/")
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_class_sink_methods_without_dangerous_call_is_unknown() -> None:
    """Methods that never call anything dangerous → unknown."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def get(self, q):
            return q
        def put(self, q):
            self.q = q
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_async_method_is_analyzed() -> None:
    """`async def handle` is a method like any other (AsyncFunctionDef)."""
    src = """
    class X:
        async def handle(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_strongest_method_wins() -> None:
    """Any method's `parameter_match` beats another's `literal_only`."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def ping(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
        def purge(self, q):
            os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_class_sink_methods_only_literal_only_is_literal_only() -> None:
    """All methods literal → `literal_only`, not `unknown`."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def ping(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
        def pong(self):
            self.db.delete("other")
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_class_sink_class_level_dangerous_call_counts() -> None:
    """A class with no methods: `class X: db = SomeClient();
    db.delete("scratch")` runs at definition time, so the class-level
    scope still contributes its argument.
    """
    src = """
    class X:
        db = SomeClient()
        db.delete("scratch")
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_class_sink_class_level_name_argument_is_unknown() -> None:
    """A class with no methods whose only dangerous call is class level
    and takes no parameter → unknown. There are no parameters at class
    level, so a bare name is a global and contributes no evidence
    (ADR-0001)."""
    src = """
    class X:
        db = SomeClient()
        db.delete(CONFIG_PATH)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_nested_class_is_not_analyzed() -> None:
    """A nested class is a scope of its own — its `__call__` body is not
    this class's data flow. Counting it here would double-count the call
    when the nested class is itself a sink node."""
    src = """
    class X:
        class Inner:
            def __call__(self, q):
                os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_class_sink_nested_class_method_is_not_analyzed() -> None:
    """A nested class's ordinary method is excluded the same way: the
    dangerous call belongs to `Inner`, not to `X`."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def ping(self):
            self.db.delete("literal")
        class Inner:
            def delete(self, q):
                os.remove(q)
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_class_sink_nested_function_inside_method_counts() -> None:
    """A function nested inside a method is not separated: the method
    body is walked whole, as everywhere else in this module."""
    src = """
    class X:
        def handle(self, q):
            def inner():
                os.remove(q)
            inner()
    """
    assert _class_sink(src).kind == "parameter_match"


# ============================================================
# Cursor fetch reads (1.2a.3h)
# ============================================================
# A fetch gives `reads_db` (patterns.CAPABILITY_ORM_READS_DB), and
# `reads_db` is deliberately not in `SINK_CAPABILITIES`: a fetch is
# read evidence, not sink evidence. So a fetch never makes a body
# dangerous, and these tests pin that the analyzer stays honest.

def test_fetch_only_body_has_no_sink_evidence() -> None:
    """`cursor.fetchall()` alone is not a dangerous call → `unknown`.

    Such a body is not a sink node at all, so this path is unreachable
    in a scan; the test pins the analyzer's logic, not a corpus shape.
    """
    src = """
    def list_rows(self):
        return cursor.fetchall()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_fetch_after_a_read_statement_has_no_sink_evidence() -> None:
    """The realistic shape: `execute("SELECT ...")` + `fetchall()`.
    Both are reads, so neither is a dangerous call."""
    src = """
    def list_rows(self):
        cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM rows")
        return cursor.fetchall()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


def test_fetch_does_not_change_a_write_sinks_data_flow() -> None:
    """On a real sink the fetch sits next to the write: it adds
    `reads_db` to the node's capabilities but contributes no argument
    evidence, so the value is still the write's `parameter_match`."""
    src = """
    def insert_and_read(self, rows):
        self.db.add(rows)
        return cursor.fetchall()
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_self_attribute_is_still_data_in_a_sink_body() -> None:
    """Unchanged from 1.2a.3g: `self.q = q` then `self.q` is data.

    The `self` case is one level and needs the assignment as evidence
    (`self_attrs`); 1.2a.3j added the parameter/local case and left this
    one alone.
    """
    src = """
    def delete(self, q):
        self.q = q
        self.db.delete(self.q)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_body_with_a_parameter_attribute_is_data() -> None:
    """The node value: FinBot `create_vendor_file`, as the sink sees it."""
    src = """
    def write_file(self, file_data):
        open(file_data.filename, "w")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_body_with_a_nested_parameter_attribute_is_data() -> None:
    """`session_context.current_user.id` reaches the node too."""
    src = """
    def write_file(self, session_context):
        open(session_context.current_user.id, "w")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_body_with_a_local_attribute_is_data() -> None:
    """`cfg = session_context.config` then `cfg.path` is the sink's data."""
    src = """
    def write_file(self, session_context):
        cfg = session_context.config
        open(cfg.path, "w")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_body_with_an_attribute_of_a_global_is_unknown() -> None:
    """The negative case: a global's attribute is not the sink's data."""
    src = """
    def write_file(self):
        open(config.path, "w")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"


# ============================================================
# Adapter wrapper calls (1.2a.3i)
# ============================================================
# `self.adapter.execute(...)` and `self.client.post(...)` are dangerous
# calls in their own right (patterns.CAPABILITY_EXECUTES_CODE and
# CAPABILITY_HTTP_EGRESS), so a body whose only dangerous call is a
# wrapper call now has an argument value at all. Before this item the
# call matched nothing, `_dangerous_calls` was empty and the body was
# read as `unknown` — even though the wrapper is exactly the shape that
# carries the caller's data. The argument classification is unchanged:
# these tests pin what the newly visible call contributes, not a new
# rule for arguments.

def test_sink_body_with_an_adapter_execute_is_data() -> None:
    """The 1.2a.3g example: `self.adapter.execute(cmd)`, `cmd` a param."""
    src = """
    def run_command(self, cmd):
        self.adapter.execute(cmd)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "parameter_match"


def test_sink_body_with_a_client_post_of_a_literal_is_literal_only() -> None:
    """`self.client.post(url)` with a literal URL — egress, no data."""
    src = """
    def notify(self):
        self.client.post("https://api.example.com/notify")
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "literal_only"


def test_sink_body_with_a_client_get_has_no_evidence() -> None:
    """`client.get` is not a dangerous call (1.2a.3i decision).

    Such a body is not a sink node at all; the test pins the analyzer's
    logic, not a corpus shape.
    """
    src = """
    def fetch(self, url):
        return self.client.get(url)
    """
    assert _sink_body(src).kind == "unknown"

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_flow_tool_analyzer.py
==============================================================================
"""Unit tests for `flow.tool_analyzer` — the tool question (1.2a.1).

A tool that returns (or yields) data can carry the agent's data onward,
so the answer is a `bool` published as the node's `returns_data`. The
analyzer is pure: these tests build AST nodes from source strings and
assert the boolean. No filesystem, no TSA subprocess.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import textwrap

from aicorellator.parsing.flow.arguments import FunctionNode
from aicorellator.parsing.flow.tool_analyzer import analyze_tool_returns


# ============================================================
# Helpers
# ============================================================

def _func(source: str) -> FunctionNode:
    """Parse `source` and return its first function definition."""
    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            return node
    raise AssertionError("no function found in source")


# ============================================================
# Tool return analyzer (1.2a.1)
# ============================================================

def _returns(source: str) -> bool:
    """Analyze the first function in `source` as a tool body."""
    return analyze_tool_returns(_func(source))


def test_tool_returns_data() -> None:
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        return search(query)
    """
    assert _returns(src) is True


def test_tool_returns_none_is_false() -> None:
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        log(query)
        return None
    """
    assert _returns(src) is False


def test_tool_bare_return_is_false() -> None:
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        log(query)
        return
    """
    assert _returns(src) is False


def test_tool_without_return_is_false() -> None:
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        log(query)
    """
    assert _returns(src) is False


def test_tool_yield_is_true() -> None:
    """A generator hands data to its caller."""
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        yield query
    """
    assert _returns(src) is True


def test_tool_yield_from_is_true() -> None:
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        yield from query
    """
    assert _returns(src) is True


def test_tool_conditional_return_with_data_is_true() -> None:
    """One data return is enough, even when another branch returns None."""
    src = """
    def read_file(query):
        if query:
            return search(query)
        return None
    """
    assert _returns(src) is True


def test_tool_async_return_is_true() -> None:
    src = """
    async def read_file(query):
        return await search(query)
    """
    assert _returns(src) is True

"""Unit tests for the FastMCP detector."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.fastmcp import FastMCPDetector


def _detect(code: str):
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return FastMCPDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def test_no_fastmcp_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("x = 1\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_detect_fastmcp_server() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("my-server")
""")
    servers = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"]
    assert len(servers) == 1
    assert servers[0].name == "my-server"
    assert servers[0].attributes["framework"] == "fastmcp"
    assert servers[0].attributes["server_variable"] == "mcp"


def test_detect_fastmcp_server_name_keyword() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP(name="ops-orchestrator", description="x")
""")
    servers = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"]
    assert len(servers) == 1
    assert servers[0].name == "ops-orchestrator"


def test_detect_fastmcp_no_name_falls_back() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP()
""")
    servers = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"]
    assert len(servers) == 1
    assert servers[0].name == "unnamed_mcp_server"


def test_detect_tool_with_parens() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool()
def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].name == "search"
    assert tools[0].attributes["parent_server"] == "srv"


def test_detect_tool_without_parens() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool
def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].name == "search"


def test_detect_tool_with_description() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool(description="A search tool")
def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].name == "search"


def test_tool_capabilities_extracted() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
import subprocess
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool()
def run_cmd(cmd: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True).stdout.decode()
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    caps = tools[0].capabilities
    assert "executes_code" in caps
    assert "executes_shell" in caps


def test_multiple_servers_in_one_file() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
a = FastMCP("alpha")
b = FastMCP("beta")

@a.tool()
def alpha_tool() -> str:
    return "a"

@b.tool()
def beta_tool() -> str:
    return "b"
""")
    servers = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"}
    assert servers == {"alpha", "beta"}
    tools = {n.name: n.attributes["parent_server"] for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"}
    assert tools == {"alpha_tool": "alpha", "beta_tool": "beta"}


def test_unrelated_decorator_ignored() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@other.tool()
def not_our_tool() -> str:
    return "x"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert tools == []


def test_provenance_in_attributes() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool()
def t() -> str:
    return "x"
""")
    for node in result.nodes:
        assert node.attributes.get("framework") == "fastmcp"


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.2a.2 — tool_data_flow for the normalizer's server → tool edge
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def test_tool_with_parameters_records_parameter_match() -> None:
    """A tool with a parameter receives the client's data (MCP channel)."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool()
def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "parameter_match"
    # The detector emits no edges; the normalizer copies the attribute
    # onto the edge it builds.
    assert result.edges == []


def test_tool_without_parameters_records_no_args() -> None:
    """A parameterless tool has nothing to receive."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

@mcp.tool()
def health() -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "no_args"


def test_tool_method_ignores_self() -> None:
    """`self` is not a client-supplied argument."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")

class Tools:
    @mcp.tool()
    def ping(self) -> str:
        return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "no_args"

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_framework_fastmcp_middleware.py
==============================================================================
"""Unit tests for the FastMCP middleware detector (B.4-gap-5).

ADR-0024 §3 decides the SDK detectors; this is the fourth and last. The
shape is the SDK's own **base class** — a `Middleware` subclass — and the
node it produces is a `guardrail` with
`observed_by=["ast", "framework:fastmcp_middleware"]` (ADR-0024 §1: the
detector's provenance, distinguishable from the capability's `["ast"]`).

S1–S6 are the shapes, P1/P2 the provenance, E1/E3 the empty edge list, R1
and R2 the registry, and the rest are the decisions the module docstring
states and the brief left open: the two-part fast path, all subclasses
accepted (a hook name is never read), every base read rather than one, the
registration (`@mcp.middleware(...)`, `mcp.add_middleware(...)`) as no
second node, the grandchild and the alias (both false negatives), and the
id collision of two same-name classes in one file.

The merge (M1) and B.4a's behaviour on a detector node (X1) need a
`NormalizeContext` and the file-backed `project` fixture, which lives in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/conftest.py`; they are in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_fastmcp_middleware_detector.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.fastmcp_middleware import (
    FastMCPMiddlewareDetector,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
    all_names,
    resolve,
)

IMPORT = "from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware\n"

# A middleware built where a project builds one: the SDK's base, the hook
# the SDK calls, the project's own work in the body.
MIDDLEWARE_SOURCE = """\
from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware


class AuditMiddleware(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context, call_next):
        audit(context)
        return await call_next(context)
"""


def _detect(code: str):
    """One detector run over `code`, as the runner calls it."""
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return FastMCPMiddlewareDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def _names(result) -> list[str]:
    return [node.name for node in result.nodes]


# ============================================================
# The fast path
# ============================================================

def test_no_fastmcp_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    """No import, no detection — even when the shape is present.

    A project that subclasses `Middleware` without importing `fastmcp`
    is subclassing its own name, not the SDK's.
    """
    result = _detect(
        "class AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n    pass\n"
    )
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_a_fastmcp_import_without_the_base_returns_empty() -> None:
    """FastMCP, but no middleware: the second half of the fast path.

    A project that registers tools on a `FastMCP` server and declares no
    middleware has none; the file is skipped without a walk.
    """
    source = (
        "from fastmcp import FastMCP\n"
        "\n"
        'mcp = FastMCP("audit")\n'
        "\n"
        "\n"
        '@mcp.tool\n'
        "def search(query):\n"
        "    return query\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# S1, S2 — the shapes that are nodes
# ============================================================

def test_a_middleware_subclass_is_a_node() -> None:
    """S1: `class AuditMiddleware(Middleware)` → one `guardrail` node.

    The hook the class overrides is the body; the base is the shape. A
    subclass that overrides nothing is a node too (see below).
    """
    result = _detect(MIDDLEWARE_SOURCE)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditMiddleware"]
    node = result.nodes[0]
    assert node.kind == "guardrail"
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "fastmcp_middleware"
    assert node.attributes["source_file"] == "test.py"


def test_a_subclass_that_overrides_nothing_is_still_a_node() -> None:
    """The base is the trigger, not the methods (the module docstring).

    An empty subclass is a middleware the SDK calls; the detector does
    not rank subclasses by what their bodies do.
    """
    source = IMPORT + "\n\nclass MetricsMiddleware(Middleware):\n    pass\n"
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["MetricsMiddleware"]


def test_a_dotted_base_is_a_node() -> None:
    """S2: `fastmcp.server.middleware.Middleware` is the same base."""
    source = (
        "import fastmcp.server.middleware\n"
        "\n"
        "\n"
        "class AuditMiddleware(fastmcp.server.middleware.Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["AuditMiddleware"]


def test_a_mixin_alongside_the_base_does_not_hide_it() -> None:
    """Every base is read, not one: `(Middleware, ABC)` is a subclass."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "from abc import ABC\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware, ABC):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["AuditMiddleware"]


# ============================================================
# S3–S6 — the shapes that are not nodes
# ============================================================

def test_a_class_named_middleware_but_not_subclassing_it_is_not_a_node(
) -> None:
    """S3: the name is not read (ADR-0016 decision 7).

    `AuditMiddleware` ending in `Middleware` grants nothing; the base is
    the SDK's own convention and that is what the detector reads.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(SomeOtherBase):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _detect(source).nodes == []


def test_an_annotation_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """S4: `mw: Middleware` is a type, not a subclass."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\ndef configure(mw: Middleware):\n"
        "    return mw\n"
    )
    assert _detect(source).nodes == []


def test_a_grandchild_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """S5: a false negative, documented and pinned.

    The detector is per-file (ADR-0011) and does not resolve the chain:
    `AuditMiddleware` is a project name here, not the SDK's base.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Child(AuditMiddleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["AuditMiddleware"]


def test_a_bare_instance_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """`Middleware()` with no class statement is not a subclass."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nMIDDLEWARE = Middleware()\n"
    )
    assert _detect(source).nodes == []


def test_a_middleware_decorator_is_not_a_second_node() -> None:
    """S6: `@mcp.middleware(...)` registers a factory; the class is the node.

    The decorator names the server the middleware is added to. It is not
    a class statement and not a second thing the middleware is, so the
    detector emits one node — the subclass — and nothing for the
    decorator.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "from fastmcp import FastMCP\n"
        "\n\nmcp = FastMCP(\"audit\")\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\n@mcp.middleware\n"
        "def middleware_factory():\n"
        "    return AuditMiddleware()\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditMiddleware"]


def test_the_registration_is_not_a_second_node() -> None:
    """S6: the class is the node; the registration names the server.

    `mcp.add_middleware(AuditMiddleware())` registers the class on a
    server — the server is B.4a's business, and the detector emits the
    class and nothing else.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "from fastmcp import FastMCP\n"
        "\n\nmcp = FastMCP(\"audit\")\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nmcp.add_middleware(AuditMiddleware())\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditMiddleware"]


# ============================================================
# P1, P2, E1, E3 — provenance and the empty edge list
# ============================================================

def test_the_provenance_is_the_detector() -> None:
    """P1: ADR-0024 §1 — `["ast", "framework:<name>"]`."""
    node = _detect(MIDDLEWARE_SOURCE).nodes[0]
    assert node.observed_by == ["ast", "framework:fastmcp_middleware"]


def test_the_framework_attribute_is_the_registry_name() -> None:
    """P2: `framework="fastmcp_middleware"`, lowercase, and the line."""
    node = _detect(MIDDLEWARE_SOURCE).nodes[0]
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "fastmcp_middleware"
    assert node.attributes["line_start"] == 4


def test_the_provenance_list_is_fresh_per_node() -> None:
    """Two nodes, two lists — a shared list is one mutation away."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass One(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Two(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    first, second = _detect(source).nodes
    assert first.observed_by == second.observed_by
    assert first.observed_by is not second.observed_by


def test_the_detector_emits_no_edges() -> None:
    """E1/E3: node-only. B.4a emits the `guards` edge, not the detector."""
    result = _detect(MIDDLEWARE_SOURCE)
    assert result.edges == []
    assert result.framework == "fastmcp_middleware"


# ============================================================
# R1, R2 — registration
# ============================================================

def test_all_names_includes_fastmcp_middleware() -> None:
    assert "fastmcp_middleware" in all_names()
    assert all_names() == sorted(all_names())


def test_resolve_returns_an_instance() -> None:
    resolved = resolve(["fastmcp_middleware"])
    assert len(resolved) == 1
    assert isinstance(resolved[0], FastMCPMiddlewareDetector)
    assert resolved[0].name == "fastmcp_middleware"


def test_the_registry_class_is_the_detector() -> None:
    from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
        KNOWN_DETECTORS,
    )
    assert KNOWN_DETECTORS["fastmcp_middleware"] is FastMCPMiddlewareDetector


# ============================================================
# The boundaries the module docstring states
# ============================================================

def test_an_aliased_import_is_not_matched() -> None:
    """`Middleware as MW` is a false negative, pinned.

    The detector matches the base's name; an ADR-0011 per-file detector
    does not carry an alias table. The import is still the fast path: the
    file mentions the base, and the shape then declines to match.
    """
    source = (
        "from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware as MW\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(MW):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_string_base_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`class AuditMiddleware("Middleware")` — a forward reference."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + '\n\nclass AuditMiddleware("Middleware"):\n'
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _detect(source).nodes == []


def test_a_subscript_base_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`Middleware[int]` is a subscript, not the base."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware[int]):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _detect(source).nodes == []


def test_two_subclasses_are_two_nodes_with_distinct_ids() -> None:
    """Two classes, two ids — the id hashes the class name."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass MetricsMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditMiddleware", "MetricsMiddleware"]
    first, second = result.nodes
    assert first.id != second.id
    assert first.id.startswith("guardrail:")
    assert first.kind == second.kind == "guardrail"


def test_two_same_name_classes_in_one_file_collide_on_one_id() -> None:
    """The id hashes the name, not the line: one row, two lines.

    The accepted false negative of the sibling detectors. `line_start`
    is in `attributes`, so the definition each node came from is still
    visible; the second node's id repeats the first's.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditMiddleware", "AuditMiddleware"]
    assert result.nodes[0].id == result.nodes[1].id
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == 4
    assert result.nodes[1].attributes["line_start"] == 8


def test_the_nodes_are_in_source_order() -> None:
    """A breadth-first walk, one source-ordered result.

    `ast.walk` is breadth-first, so it reaches the module's second class
    before a class nested in a function body above it; the detector sorts
    by `(lineno, col_offset)`.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass First(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\ndef build():\n"
        "    class Nested(Middleware):\n"
        "        pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Second(Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["First", "Nested", "Second"]


def test_a_module_alias_prefix_is_matched() -> None:
    """`import fastmcp.server.middleware` — the fast path is the prefix.

    The SDK's middleware module imports as `fastmcp.server.middleware`,
    and the detector reads the base's last dotted segment, so the
    module-level import is enough for the fast path and the qualified
    base is the shape.
    """
    source = (
        "import fastmcp.server.middleware as fw\n"
        "\n\nclass AuditMiddleware(fw.Middleware):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert _names(_detect(source)) == ["AuditMiddleware"]

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_framework_guardrails_ai.py
==============================================================================
"""Unit tests for the Guardrails AI detector (B.4-gap-2).

ADR-0024 §3 decides the SDK detectors; this is the first. The shape is
the SDK's own **class-level construction** — `Guard(...)` and
`Guard.<factory>(...)` — and the node it produces is a `guardrail` with
`observed_by=["ast", "framework:guardrails_ai"]` (ADR-0024 §1: the
detector's provenance, distinguishable from the capability's `["ast"]`).

S1–S5 are the shapes, P1/P2 the provenance, E1 the empty edge list, R1/R2
the registry, and the rest are the decisions the module docstring states
and the brief left open: the fast path, the id collision of two unnamed
constructions, the class-level/dotted forms, the decorator, and the
fallback name.

The merge (M1) and B.4a's behaviour on a detector node (X1) need a
`NormalizeContext` and the file-backed `project` fixture, which lives in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/conftest.py`; they are in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_guardrails_ai_detector.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.guardrails_ai import (
    GuardrailsAIDetector,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
    all_names,
    resolve,
)

IMPORT = "from guardrails import Guard\n"


def _detect(code: str):
    """One detector run over `code`, as the runner calls it."""
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return GuardrailsAIDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def _names(result) -> list[str]:
    return [node.name for node in result.nodes]


# ============================================================
# The fast path
# ============================================================

def test_no_guardrails_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    """No import, no detection — even when the shape is present.

    A project that calls `Guard(...)` without importing `guardrails` is
    calling its own name, not the SDK's.
    """
    result = _detect("guard = Guard()\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_an_unrelated_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("import json\n\nguard = Guard()\n")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_each_import_form_of_the_sdk_is_the_fast_path() -> None:
    """`import guardrails` / `from guardrails import ...` / `.hub`.

    `_has_import_prefix` is the base helper every detector uses; the
    SDK's distribution imports as `guardrails` and its validators live
    under `guardrails.hub`.
    """
    for header in (
        "import guardrails",
        "import guardrails.hub",
        "from guardrails import Guard",
        "from guardrails.hub import Guard",
    ):
        result = _detect(f"{header}\n\nguard = Guard()\n")
        assert len(result.nodes) == 1, header


# ============================================================
# S1 — Guard(...)
# ============================================================

def test_guard_assigned_names_the_node_after_the_variable() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]
    node = result.nodes[0]
    assert node.kind == "guardrail"
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "guardrails_ai"
    assert node.attributes["source_file"] == "test.py"
    assert node.attributes["line_start"] == 3


def test_guard_unassigned_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    """A bare-expression construction has no name of its own."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nGuard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


def test_a_guard_inside_a_call_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    """`setup(Guard())` — the call is not an assignment value."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nsetup(Guard())\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


def test_a_guard_inside_a_list_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguards = [Guard(), Guard()]\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard", "Guard"]


def test_a_guard_inside_a_method_body_counts() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` reaches the whole tree; the line is the call's own."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
class Service:
    def build(self, text):
        guard = Guard()
        return guard
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == 5


def test_a_self_attribute_target_names_the_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
class Service:
    def __init__(self):
        self.guard = Guard()
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


# ============================================================
# S2–S4 — Guard.<factory>(...)
# ============================================================

def test_from_pydantic_is_a_construction() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Invoice(BaseModel):
    total: float


guard = Guard.from_pydantic(Invoice)
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["framework"] == "guardrails_ai"


def test_for_string_is_a_construction() -> None:
    result = _detect("""\
from guardrails import Guard

guard = Guard.for_string(validators=[], description="x")
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_for_rail_is_a_construction() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard.for_rail(\"pii.rail\")\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_any_class_level_factory_is_a_construction() -> None:
    """The set of factories is the SDK's, not the detector's.

    ADR-0016 decision 7 forbids a table that grants a kind from a name;
    the detector reads the class (`Guard.<attr>(...)`), so a factory the
    SDK adds later is covered without a line here.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard.from_yaml(\"config.yaml\")\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_a_dotted_construction_is_a_construction() -> None:
    """`import guardrails` + `guardrails.Guard.for_string(...)`."""
    result = _detect(
        "import guardrails\n"
        "\nguard = guardrails.Guard.for_string(validators=[])\n"
    )
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_an_unassigned_factory_call_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nGuard.for_rail(\"pii.rail\")\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


# ============================================================
# S5 — an instance method is not a construction
# ============================================================

def test_an_instance_method_call_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """`guard.parse` / `guard.validate` use a guard, they do not build one.

    One construction, one node — the two calls add nothing. The base of
    the attribute is `guard` (the value), not `Guard` (the class).
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
guard = Guard()

guard.parse("text")
guard.validate("text")
guard("text")
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_a_construction_that_is_used_is_still_one_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
guard = Guard.for_pydantic(Invoice)
result = guard.parse(text)
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


# ============================================================
# The assignment forms
# ============================================================

def test_an_annotated_assignment_names_the_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(
        IMPORT + "\nguard: Guard = Guard.for_rail(\"pii.rail\")\n"
    )
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


def test_a_multiple_target_assignment_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    """`first = second = Guard()` — two names, one value: no name wins."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nfirst = second = Guard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


def test_a_tuple_target_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    """`left, right = Guard()` — one target, and it is a tuple."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nleft, right = Guard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


def test_a_tuple_value_goes_through_the_call_sites() -> None:
    """`left, right = Guard(), Guard(...)` — the value is not a call.

    Neither construction is an assignment *value* (`node.value` is the
    tuple), so both are found the second way: as call sites named after
    the class.
    """
    result = _detect(
        IMPORT + "\nleft, right = Guard(), Guard.for_rail(\"x\")\n"
    )
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard", "Guard"]


def test_a_subscript_target_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguards[0] = Guard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]


# ============================================================
# Names that are not the SDK's class
# ============================================================

def test_a_similarly_named_class_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """`MyGuard(...)` is the project's class, not the SDK's."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = MyGuard()\n")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_lowercase_base_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """`guard.Guard(...)` — an attribute of an instance, not the class."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
guard = Guard()

other = guard.Guard()
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["guard"]


# ============================================================
# The decorator
# ============================================================

def test_the_bare_decorator_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """ADR-0024 §3 names `@guard`; the node here is the construction.

    `@guard` is a `Name`, not a call, so there is nothing to build a
    node from — a separate shape, not detected in B.4-gap-2.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
from guardrails import guard


@guard
def answer(text):
    return text
""")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_class_level_call_as_a_decorator_is_a_call_site() -> None:
    """`@Guard.for_string(...)` applies a guard this detector cannot name.

    It is a `Guard` class-level call in the tree, so the rule that
    "a class-level call is a construction" emits a node — named after
    the class, because a decorator binds nothing.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """

@Guard.for_string(validators=[], description="x")
def answer(text):
    return text
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard"]

def test_the_node_names_the_detector_and_the_ast() -> None:
    """ADR-0024 §1: a detector-derived guardrail says who saw it.

    `["ast", "framework:guardrails_ai"]`, which is what distinguishes it
    from a capability-derived `guardrail` (`["ast"]`) and from the LLM
    classifier's (`["ast", "static_llm:<model>"]`).

    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n")
    assert result.nodes[0].observed_by == [
        "ast", "framework:guardrails_ai",

    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["framework"] == "guardrails_ai"


def test_the_provenance_is_a_fresh_list() -> None:
    """Two nodes must not share one mutable list."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\ng1 = Guard()\ng2 = Guard.for_rail(\"x\")\n")
    assert result.nodes[0].observed_by is not result.nodes[1].observed_by


def test_the_detection_result_names_the_framework() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n")
    assert result.framework == "guardrails_ai"
    assert result.detected_version is None

    """No version is inferable from an import line (ADR-0011)."""
    assert GuardrailsAIDetector.supported_versions == "*"

def test_the_detector_returns_no_edges() -> None:
    """Node-only. A `Guard` wraps an LLM call; the AST links nothing.

    B.4a's `guardrail_edges` decides what a `guards` edge needs, and it
    runs on this node like on any other `guardrail` node.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n\nguard.parse(\"x\")\n")
    assert result.nodes != []
    assert result.edges == []


# ============================================================
# The id — two unnamed constructions collide
# ============================================================

def test_two_named_constructions_are_two_nodes_with_two_ids() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\ng1 = Guard()\ng2 = Guard.for_rail(\"x\")\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["g1", "g2"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 2


def test_two_unnamed_constructions_share_one_id() -> None:
    """The id hashes the name, not the line: an accepted false negative.

    The detector emits one node per call site; the id is
    `framework + kind + file + name + host` (the existing detectors'
    rule), so two `Guard()` calls with no binding produce the same id and
    the graph keeps one row. `line_start` distinguishes them for a reader.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nGuard()\nGuard()\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["Guard", "Guard"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 1
    assert [n.attributes["line_start"] for n in result.nodes] == [3, 4]


def test_the_id_does_not_depend_on_the_line() -> None:
    """The same construction at two lines is the same id, not two."""
    one = _detect(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n")
    two = _detect(IMPORT + "\n\n\n\nguard = Guard()\n")
    assert one.nodes[0].id == two.nodes[0].id


def test_the_id_depends_on_the_file() -> None:
    """Per-file and per-host, like the other detectors (ADR-0011)."""
    detector = GuardrailsAIDetector()
    tree = ast.parse(IMPORT + "\nguard = Guard()\n")
    here = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "")
    there = detector.detect("b.py", tree, "")
    other_host = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "", host_id="other")
    assert here.nodes[0].id != there.nodes[0].id
    assert here.nodes[0].id != other_host.nodes[0].id


# ============================================================
# Order
# ============================================================

def test_the_nodes_are_in_source_order() -> None:
    """Two passes over the tree, one ordered result."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
first = Guard()
Guard.for_rail("x")
second = Guard.for_pydantic(Invoice)
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["first", "Guard", "second"]

# ============================================================

def test_all_names_includes_guardrails_ai() -> None:
    assert "guardrails_ai" in all_names()
    assert all_names() == sorted(all_names())


def test_resolve_returns_an_instance() -> None:
    resolved = resolve(["guardrails_ai"])
    assert len(resolved) == 1
    assert isinstance(resolved[0], GuardrailsAIDetector)
    assert resolved[0].name == "guardrails_ai"

    from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
        KNOWN_DETECTORS,
    )
    assert KNOWN_DETECTORS["guardrails_ai"] is GuardrailsAIDetector
