"""Unit tests for LangChain detector."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.langchain import LangChainDetector


def _detect(code: str):
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return LangChainDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def test_no_langchain_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("x = 1\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_detect_agent_executor() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor, initialize_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")
agent = AgentExecutor(agent=..., tools=[], llm=llm)
""")
    kinds = {n.kind for n in result.nodes}
    assert "agent" in kinds
    assert "llm_endpoint" in kinds
    agent_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "agent"}
    assert "AgentExecutor" in agent_names
    llm_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "llm_endpoint"}
    assert "ChatOpenAI" in llm_names


def test_detect_initialize_agent() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import initialize_agent
agent = initialize_agent(tools=[], llm=None)
""")
    agent_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "agent"}
    assert "initialize_agent" in agent_names


def test_detect_tool_decorator() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def search(query: str) -> str:
    return ""
""")
    tool_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"}
    assert "search" in tool_names


def test_detect_tool_instance() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.tools import Tool, StructuredTool

t = Tool(name="my_tool", func=lambda x: x, description="...")
s = StructuredTool.from_function(my_function)
""")
    tool_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"}
    assert "my_tool" in tool_names
    assert "my_function" in tool_names


def test_detect_llm_providers() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
from langchain_community.llms import Ollama

a = ChatAnthropic(model="claude")
o = Ollama(model="llama")
""")
    providers = {
        n.attributes.get("provider")
        for n in result.nodes
        if n.kind == "llm_endpoint"
    }
    assert "anthropic" in providers
    assert "ollama" in providers


def test_provenance_in_attributes() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor
a = AgentExecutor(agent=..., tools=[])
""")
    for node in result.nodes:
        assert node.attributes.get("framework") == "langchain"

def test_uses_model_from_local_assignment() -> None:
    """LLM assigned inside a function is resolved."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama

def get_agent(role):
    llm = ChatOllama(model="llama3")
    return create_agent(model=llm, tools=[])
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert len(uses_model) == 1
    # The model was configured with a literal name. The detector knows
    # that, but the AST edge records only the control relationship
    # (ADR-0016, decision 3).
    assert uses_model[0].flow_kind == "control"
    assert uses_model[0].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_tool_from_local_assignment() -> None:
    """Tool list assigned inside a function is resolved."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def search(q: str) -> str:
    return ""

def get_agent():
    tools = [search]
    return create_agent(tools=tools, model=None)
""")
    uses_tool = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_tool"]
    assert len(uses_tool) == 1
    # ADR-0015: control flow. ADR-0016: no data-flow verdict.
    assert uses_tool[0].flow_kind == "control"
    assert uses_tool[0].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_assignment_later_wins() -> None:
    """When two assignments share a name, the later one is used."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama

llm = ChatOllama(model="first")
llm = ChatOllama(model="second")
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=[])
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert len(uses_model) == 1

def test_resolve_tool_names_cycle_safe() -> None:
    """Cyclic assignments do not cause infinite recursion."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent

X = Y
Y = X
agent = create_agent(tools=X, model=None)
""")
    # No crash; no edges because X/Y are not resolvable to tools.
    uses_tool = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_tool"]
    assert uses_tool == []


def test_resolve_llm_names_cycle_safe() -> None:
    """Cyclic LLM assignment does not cause infinite recursion."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent

A = B
B = A
agent = create_agent(model=A, tools=[])
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert uses_model == []


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ADR-0016 — the detector reads the source, the edge stays control
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each case below is a question the detector answers with confidence —
# "the prompt names this tool", "the model name is a literal", "the model
# name is a caller-supplied parameter". The answer is framework knowledge
# for Layer 2; none of it is written to an AST edge, so every edge here
# is `control` with `data_flow_confirmed = NULL`.

def _tool_edges(result):
    """Map the uses_tool edges by target tool name."""
    names = {n.id: n.name for n in result.nodes}
    return {
        names[e.target_id]: e
        for e in result.edges
        if e.kind == "uses_tool"
    }


def test_uses_tool_named_in_system_prompt_is_still_control() -> None:
    """The prompt names `a` — and neither edge claims data flow.

    This is the detector's strongest reading of the source: the system
    prompt mentions one of the two tools. It still is not a data-flow
    confirmation, because nothing ran (ADR-0016, decision 3).
    """
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def a(x: str) -> str:
    return x

@tool
def b(x: str) -> str:
    return x

agent = create_agent(tools=[a, b], system_prompt="Use a for X")
""")
    edges = _tool_edges(result)
    assert edges["a"].flow_kind == "control"
    assert edges["a"].data_flow_confirmed is None
    assert edges["b"].flow_kind == "control"
    assert edges["b"].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_tool_without_system_prompt_stays_control() -> None:
    """No prompt is no evidence."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def a(x: str) -> str:
    return x

agent = create_agent(tools=[a])
""")
    edges = _tool_edges(result)
    assert edges["a"].flow_kind == "control"
    assert edges["a"].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_tool_unrelated_system_prompt_stays_control() -> None:
    """A prompt that does not name the tool stays control."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def a(x: str) -> str:
    return x

agent = create_agent(tools=[a], system_prompt="Do something unrelated")
""")
    edges = _tool_edges(result)
    assert edges["a"].flow_kind == "control"
    assert edges["a"].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_model_literal_is_literal_only() -> None:
    """`ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")` is a constant configuration."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")
agent = AgentExecutor(agent=..., tools=[], llm=llm)
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert len(uses_model) == 1
    assert uses_model[0].flow_kind == "control"
    assert uses_model[0].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_model_resolved_module_assignment_is_literal_only() -> None:
    """`model=model_var` where `model_var = "gpt-4"` resolves to a literal."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

model_var = "gpt-4"
llm = ChatOpenAI(model=model_var)
agent = create_agent(model=llm, tools=[])
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert len(uses_model) == 1
    assert uses_model[0].flow_kind == "control"
    assert uses_model[0].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_uses_model_from_function_parameter_stays_control() -> None:
    """A caller-supplied model name is the tempting `parameter_match`.

    Same shape as the Flow Analyzer's data case — the value arrives from
    outside — but the AST layer did not see it arrive, so the edge stays
    control with no verdict (ADR-0016, decision 3).
    """
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama

def get_agent(model_name):
    llm = ChatOllama(model=model_name)
    return create_agent(model=llm, tools=[])
""")
    uses_model = [e for e in result.edges if e.kind == "uses_model"]
    assert len(uses_model) == 1
    assert uses_model[0].flow_kind == "control"
    assert uses_model[0].data_flow_confirmed is None


def test_tool_node_records_signature_data_flow() -> None:
    """Tool nodes carry the signature result for the normalizer."""
    result = _detect("""
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def with_args(x: str) -> str:
    return x

@tool
def without_args() -> str:
    return "x"
""")
    tools = {n.name: n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"}
    assert tools["with_args"].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "parameter_match"
    assert tools["without_args"].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "no_args"

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_framework_langchain_callback.py
==============================================================================
"""Unit tests for the LangChain callbacks detector (B.4-gap-4).

ADR-0024 §3 decides the SDK detectors; this is the third. The shape is
the SDK's own **base class** — a `BaseCallbackHandler` subclass — and the
node it produces is a `guardrail` with
`observed_by=["ast", "framework:langchain_callback"]` (ADR-0024 §1: the
detector's provenance, distinguishable from the capability's `["ast"]`).

S1–S6 are the shapes, P1/P2 the provenance, E1 the empty edge list, R1/R2
the registry, and the rest are the decisions the module docstring states
and the brief left open: the two-part fast path, all subclasses accepted
(a hook name is never read), every base read rather than one, the
grandchild and the alias (both false negatives), and the id collision of
two same-name classes in one file.

The merge (M1) and B.4a's behaviour on a detector node (X1) need a
`NormalizeContext` and the file-backed `project` fixture, which lives in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/conftest.py`; they are in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_langchain_callback_detector.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.langchain_callback import (
    LangChainCallbackDetector,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
    all_names,
    resolve,
)

IMPORT = "from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\n"

# A handler built where a project builds one: the SDK's base, the hook
# the SDK calls, the project's own work in the body.
HANDLER_SOURCE = """\
from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler


class AuditHook(BaseCallbackHandler):
    def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs):
        audit(prompts)
"""


def _detect(code: str):
    """One detector run over `code`, as the runner calls it."""
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return LangChainCallbackDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def _names(result) -> list[str]:
    return [node.name for node in result.nodes]


# ============================================================
# The fast path
# ============================================================

def test_no_langchain_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    """No import, no detection — even when the shape is present.

    A project that subclasses `BaseCallbackHandler` without importing
    `langchain` is subclassing its own name, not the SDK's.
    """
    result = _detect(
        "class MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n    pass\n"
    )
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_a_langchain_import_without_the_base_returns_empty() -> None:
    """LangChain, but no callbacks: the second half of the fast path.

    A project using `AgentExecutor` and no handler has no callback; the
    file is skipped without a walk.
    """
    source = (
        "from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor\n"
        "\n"
        "\n"
        "class MyHandler(SomeOtherBase):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_each_import_form_of_the_sdk_is_the_fast_path() -> None:
    """`import langchain` / `langchain_core` / the callback modules.

    `_has_import_prefix` is the base helper every detector uses; the
    SDK's distributions import as `langchain` and `langchain_core`, and
    the base class lives under `.callbacks`.
    """
    for header in (
        "import langchain",
        "import langchain_core.callbacks",
        "from langchain.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler",
        "from langchain.callbacks.base import BaseCallbackHandler",
        "from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler",
    ):
        code = (
            f"{header}\n"
            "\n\nclass MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
            "    pass\n"
        )
        result = _detect(code)
        assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler"], header


# ============================================================
# S1 — a BaseCallbackHandler subclass
# ============================================================

def test_a_subclass_is_one_guardrail_node_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    assert _names(result) == ["AuditHook"]
    node = result.nodes[0]
    assert node.kind == "guardrail"
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "langchain_callback"
    assert node.attributes["source_file"] == "test.py"


def test_a_subclass_that_overrides_no_hook_is_still_a_node() -> None:
    """The base is the trigger; the methods are not read.

    A callback that overrides nothing is a hook with a default
    behaviour — a weak guardrail, and ADR-0024 §2 accepts it. There is
    no hook-name table and no "does it override" test.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass Noop(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["Noop"]


def test_a_hook_method_without_the_base_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """A class that *looks* like a handler but is not one.

    `on_llm_start` on a class that does not subclass the SDK's base is
    the project's own method. The method names are the SDK's (ADR-0024
    §3) and are deliberately not read (ADR-0016 decision 7).
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass Logger:\n"
        "    def on_llm_start(self, serialized, prompts, **kwargs):\n"
        "        audit(prompts)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# S2 — a dotted base
# ============================================================

def test_a_dotted_base_is_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`class MyHandler(langchain.callbacks.base.BaseCallbackHandler)`.

    The rule is the base's last dotted segment, so the fully qualified
    form is the same base (ADR-0024 §3 reads the SDK's own convention).
    """
    source = (
        "import langchain.callbacks.base\n"
        "\n\n"
        "class MyHandler("
        "langchain.callbacks.base.BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler"]


def test_a_module_alias_prefix_is_the_same_base() -> None:
    source = (
        "import langchain_core.callbacks as callbacks\n"
        "\n\n"
        "class MyHandler(callbacks.BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler"]


# ============================================================
# S3 — a Handler-shaped class that is not a subclass
# ============================================================

def test_a_handler_shaped_class_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """The name is not read — ADR-0016 decision 7.

    A `*Handler` class whose base is something else is not a LangChain
    callback, whatever it is called. `BaseCallbackHandlerLike` is the
    near miss worth pinning: the same prefix, not the same class.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass NotAHandler(SomeOtherBase):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass BaseCallbackHandlerLike(BaseCallback):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Plain:\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# S4 — an annotation
# ============================================================

def test_an_annotation_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`handler: BaseCallbackHandler` is a type, not a base.

    The file names the base — so the fast path passes — and no class
    statement subclasses it.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nhandler: BaseCallbackHandler = build_handler()\n"
        "\n\ndef register(h: BaseCallbackHandler) -> None:\n"
        "    handlers.append(h)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# S5 — a grandchild
# ============================================================

def test_a_grandchild_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """A false negative, documented and pinned.

    `class Child(MyHandler)` where `MyHandler` subclasses the SDK's base
    is not a node: the base the child names is a project class, and a
    per-file detector (ADR-0011) does not resolve the chain. Resolving
    it is a separate mechanism, and this test is the pin that says so.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Child(MyHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler"]


# ============================================================
# S6 — a bare instance
# ============================================================

def test_a_bare_instance_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`BaseCallbackHandler()` with no subclass: no hook, no node.

    A false negative — a handler built from the base itself overrides
    no hook, which is unusual enough to leave unmodelled.
    """
    source = IMPORT + "\nhandler = BaseCallbackHandler()\n"
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# The bases the rule reads
# ============================================================

def test_a_mixin_alongside_the_base_does_not_hide_it() -> None:
    """Every base is read, not one (ADR-0020's rule is a different one)."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass MyHandler(abc.ABC, BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass OtherHandler(BaseCallbackHandler, AbcMixin):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler", "OtherHandler"]


def test_a_subscripted_base_is_not_read() -> None:
    """`class X(BaseCallbackHandler[T])` — a false negative, pinned.

    `_last_segment` answers Name and Attribute, and None for anything
    else, the same posture as the sibling detectors' helper of the same
    name.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler[AuditEvent]):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# Nesting
# ============================================================

def test_a_class_nested_in_a_function_or_a_class_counts() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` reaches the whole tree, the sibling detectors' rule."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\ndef build():\n"
        "    class Inner(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "        pass\n"
        "    return Inner\n"
        "\n\nclass Outer:\n"
        "    class Nested(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "        pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["Inner", "Nested"]


# ============================================================
# P1, P2 — provenance
# ============================================================

def test_the_node_names_the_detector_and_the_ast() -> None:
    """P1 — ADR-0024 §1's value for a detector-derived guardrail."""
    result = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    assert result.nodes[0].observed_by == [
        "ast", "framework:langchain_callback",
    ]


def test_the_provenance_is_a_fresh_list() -> None:
    """Two nodes must not share one list instance.

    `Node.observed_by` defaults to a new list per node; assigning the
    same object twice would let one node's provenance be edited through
    another's.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass First(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Second(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes[0].observed_by is not result.nodes[1].observed_by
    result.nodes[0].observed_by.append("scratch")
    assert result.nodes[1].observed_by == [
        "ast", "framework:langchain_callback",
    ]


def test_the_framework_attribute_is_the_registry_name() -> None:
    """P2 — the same string the registry and the provenance use."""
    result = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    node = result.nodes[0]
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "langchain_callback"
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == LangChainCallbackDetector.name


def test_the_attributes_carry_the_class_line_and_the_file() -> None:
    """`line_start` is the class statement's line, and informational."""
    result = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == 4
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["source_file"] == "test.py"


def test_the_detection_result_names_the_framework() -> None:
    assert _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE).framework == "langchain_callback"
    assert _detect("import json\n").framework == "langchain_callback"


def test_the_detector_declares_the_wildcard_version() -> None:
    """No version is inferable from an import line (ADR-0011)."""
    detector = LangChainCallbackDetector()
    assert detector.supported_versions == "*"
    assert detector.name == "langchain_callback"


# ============================================================
# E1 — no edges
# ============================================================

def test_the_detector_returns_no_edges() -> None:
    """Node-only. A callback is a hook, not a component a guard wraps.

    B.4a's `guardrail_edges` decides what a `guards` edge needs, and it
    runs on this node like on any other `guardrail` node.
    """
    result = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    assert result.nodes != []
    assert result.edges == []


# ============================================================
# The id
# ============================================================

def test_two_subclasses_are_two_nodes_with_two_ids() -> None:
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass First(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Second(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["First", "Second"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 2


def test_the_id_depends_on_the_file_and_on_the_host() -> None:
    """Per-file and per-host, like the other detectors (ADR-0011)."""
    detector = LangChainCallbackDetector()
    tree = ast.parse(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    here = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "")
    there = detector.detect("b.py", tree, "")
    other_host = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "", host_id="other")
    assert here.nodes[0].id != there.nodes[0].id
    assert here.nodes[0].id != other_host.nodes[0].id


def test_the_id_does_not_depend_on_the_line() -> None:
    """The same class at two lines is the same id, not two."""
    one = _detect(HANDLER_SOURCE)
    two = _detect(
        "from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler\n"
        "\n\n\n\nclass AuditHook(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    assert one.nodes[0].id == two.nodes[0].id


def test_two_classes_of_one_name_in_one_file_share_one_id() -> None:
    """The id hashes the name, not the line: an accepted false negative.

    Two definitions of one class name in one file — a shadowed
    redefinition, or a nested class named like a module-level one — are
    two nodes with one id, so the graph keeps one row. `line_start`
    distinguishes them for a reader.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\ndef build():\n"
        "    class MyHandler(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "        pass\n"
        "    return MyHandler\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["MyHandler", "MyHandler"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 1
    assert [n.attributes["line_start"] for n in result.nodes] == [4, 9]


# ============================================================
# Order
# ============================================================

def test_the_nodes_are_in_source_order() -> None:
    """A breadth-first walk, one source-ordered result.

    `ast.walk` is breadth-first, so it reaches the module's second class
    before a class nested in a function body above it; the detector
    sorts by `(lineno, col_offset)`.
    """
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + "\n\nclass First(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
        "\n\ndef build():\n"
        "    class Nested(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "        pass\n"
        "\n\nclass Second(BaseCallbackHandler):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["First", "Nested", "Second"]


# ============================================================
# The boundaries the module docstring states
# ============================================================

def test_an_aliased_import_is_not_matched() -> None:
    """`BaseCallbackHandler as BCH` is a false negative, pinned.

    The detector matches the base's name; an ADR-0011 per-file detector
    does not carry an alias table. The import is still the fast path:
    the file mentions the base, and the shape then declines to match.
    """
    source = (
        "from langchain_core.callbacks import BaseCallbackHandler as BCH\n"
        "\n\nclass MyHandler(BCH):\n"
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_string_base_is_not_a_subclass() -> None:
    """`class MyHandler("BaseCallbackHandler")` — a forward reference."""
    source = (
        IMPORT
        + '\n\nclass MyHandler("BaseCallbackHandler"):\n'
        "    pass\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# R1, R2 — registration
# ============================================================

def test_all_names_includes_langchain_callback() -> None:
    assert "langchain_callback" in all_names()
    assert all_names() == sorted(all_names())


def test_resolve_returns_an_instance() -> None:
    resolved = resolve(["langchain_callback"])
    assert len(resolved) == 1
    assert isinstance(resolved[0], LangChainCallbackDetector)
    assert resolved[0].name == "langchain_callback"


def test_the_registry_class_is_the_detector() -> None:
    from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
        KNOWN_DETECTORS,
    )
    assert KNOWN_DETECTORS["langchain_callback"] is LangChainCallbackDetector

"""Unit tests for LangGraph detector."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.langgraph import LangGraphDetector


def _detect(code: str):
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return LangGraphDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def test_no_langgraph_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("x = 1\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_detect_simple_graph() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", agent_fn)
graph.add_node("tools", tool_fn)
graph.add_edge("agent", "tools")
graph.add_edge("tools", "agent")
""")
    node_names = {n.name for n in result.nodes}
    assert "agent" in node_names
    assert "tools" in node_names

    edge_pairs = {(e.source_id, e.target_id) for e in result.edges}
    assert len(edge_pairs) == 2
    # ADR-0015: delegates_to is control flow. ADR-0016: no verdict.
    assert all(e.flow_kind == "control" for e in result.edges)
    assert all(e.data_flow_confirmed is None for e in result.edges)


def test_node_kinds_inferred() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", a)
graph.add_node("tools", t)
""")
    kinds = {n.name: n.kind for n in result.nodes}
    assert kinds["agent"] == "agent"
    assert kinds["tools"] == "tool"


def test_entry_point_marked() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", a)
graph.set_entry_point("agent")
""")
    agent_node = next(n for n in result.nodes if n.name == "agent")
    assert agent_node.attributes.get("entry_point") == "true"


def test_conditional_edges_list() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", a)
graph.add_node("tools", t)
graph.add_node("end", e)
graph.add_conditional_edges("agent", router, ["tools", "end"])
""")
    edge_pairs = {(e.source_id, e.target_id) for e in result.edges}
    assert len(edge_pairs) == 2


def test_conditional_edges_dict() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", a)
graph.add_node("tools", t)
graph.add_node("end", e)
graph.add_conditional_edges("agent", router, {"continue": "tools", "stop": "end"})
""")
    edge_pairs = {(e.source_id, e.target_id) for e in result.edges}
    assert len(edge_pairs) == 2


def test_provenance_in_attributes() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("agent", a)
""")
    for node in result.nodes:
        assert node.attributes.get("framework") == "langgraph"

"""Unit tests for the MCP Python SDK detector."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.mcp_python import MCPPythonDetector


def _detect(code: str):
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return MCPPythonDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def test_no_mcp_server_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("x = 1\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_fastmcp_import_not_matched() -> None:
    """The FastMCP import is handled by a different detector."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("srv")
""")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_detect_server_module_level() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server
server = Server("my-server")
""")
    servers = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"]
    assert len(servers) == 1
    assert servers[0].name == "my-server"
    assert servers[0].attributes["framework"] == "mcp_python"


def test_detect_server_as_self_attribute() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server

class MyServer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.server = Server("my-server")
""")
    servers = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "mcp_server"]
    assert len(servers) == 1
    assert servers[0].name == "my-server"
    assert servers[0].attributes["server_variable"] == "self.server"


def test_detect_tool_decorator_self_server() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server

class MyServer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.server = Server("srv")

    def setup(self):
        @self.server.call_tool()
        async def search(query: str) -> str:
            return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].name == "search"
    assert tools[0].attributes["parent_server"] == "srv"


def test_detect_tool_decorator_module_server() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server
server = Server("srv")

@server.call_tool()
async def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].name == "search"
    assert tools[0].attributes["parent_server"] == "srv"


def test_tool_capabilities_extracted() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
import subprocess
from mcp.server import Server

server = Server("srv")

@server.call_tool()
async def run_cmd(cmd: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True).stdout.decode()
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    caps = tools[0].capabilities
    assert "executes_code" in caps
    assert "executes_shell" in caps


def test_multiple_tools_on_one_server() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server

server = Server("srv")

@server.call_tool()
async def tool_a() -> str:
    return "a"

@server.call_tool()
async def tool_b() -> str:
    return "b"
""")
    tools = {n.name for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"}
    assert tools == {"tool_a", "tool_b"}


def test_unrelated_decorator_ignored() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server

server = Server("srv")

@other.call_tool()
async def not_a_tool() -> str:
    return "x"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert tools == []


def test_other_server_decorators_ignored() -> None:
    """list_resources, read_resource, etc. are not tools."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server

async def list_res():
    return []

@server.read_resource()

    return ""
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert tools == []


def test_provenance_in_attributes() -> None:
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server
server = Server("srv")

@server.call_tool()
async def t() -> str:
    return "x"
""")
    for node in result.nodes:
        assert node.attributes.get("framework") == "mcp_python"

def test_tool_with_parameters_records_parameter_match() -> None:
    """A tool with a parameter receives the client's data (MCP channel)."""
    result = _detect("""
from mcp.server import Server
server = Server("srv")

@server.call_tool()
async def search(query: str) -> str:
    return "ok"
""")
    tools = [n for n in result.nodes if n.kind == "tool"]
    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "parameter_match"
    # The detector emits no edges; the normalizer copies the attribute
    # onto the edge it builds.
    assert result.edges == []

""")

    assert len(tools) == 1
    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "no_args"

    """`self` is not a client-supplied argument."""
    result = _detect("""

    assert tools[0].attributes["tool_data_flow"] == "no_args"

FILE: tests/test_framework_nemo_guardrails.py

"""Unit tests for the NeMo Guardrails detector (B.4-gap-3).

ADR-0024 §3 decides the SDK detectors; this is the second. The shape is
the SDK's own **rails construction** — `LLMRails(config)` — and the node
it produces is a `guardrail` with
`observed_by=["ast", "framework:nemo_guardrails"]` (ADR-0024 §1: the
detector's provenance, distinguishable from the capability's `["ast"]`).

S1–S7 are the shapes, P1/P2 the provenance, E1 the empty edge list, R1/R2
the registry, and the rest are the decisions the module docstring states
and the brief left open: the fast path, the id collision of two unnamed
constructions, the qualified and keyword forms, the `@action` decorator,
and the alias.

The merge (M1) and B.4a's behaviour on a detector node (X1) need a
`NormalizeContext` and the file-backed `project` fixture, which lives in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/conftest.py`; they are in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_nemo_guardrails_detector.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.nemo_guardrails import (
    NeMoGuardrailsDetector,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
    all_names,
    resolve,
)

IMPORT = "from nemoguardrails import LLMRails\n"
CONFIG_IMPORT = "from nemoguardrails.rails import RailsConfig\n"

# A rails built where the SDK's own example builds one: inside the class
# that owns it, bound to an attribute.
METHOD_SOURCE = """\
from nemoguardrails import LLMRails


class Bot:
    def setup(self, config):
        self.rails = LLMRails(config)
"""


def _detect(code: str):
    """One detector run over `code`, as the runner calls it."""
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    return NeMoGuardrailsDetector().detect("test.py", tree, code)


def _names(result) -> list[str]:
    return [node.name for node in result.nodes]


# ============================================================
# The fast path
# ============================================================

def test_no_nemoguardrails_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    """No import, no detection — even when the shape is present.

    A project that calls `LLMRails(config)` without importing
    `nemoguardrails` is calling its own name, not the SDK's.
    """
    result = _detect("rails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.nodes == []
    assert result.edges == []


def test_an_unrelated_import_returns_empty() -> None:
    result = _detect("import json\n\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_each_import_form_of_the_sdk_is_the_fast_path() -> None:
    """`import nemoguardrails` / `from nemoguardrails...` / `.rails`.

    `_has_import_prefix` is the base helper every detector uses; the
    SDK's distribution imports as `nemoguardrails` and its rails class
    lives under `nemoguardrails.rails`.
    """
    for header in (
        "import nemoguardrails",
        "import nemoguardrails.rails",
        "from nemoguardrails import LLMRails",
        "from nemoguardrails.rails import LLMRails",
        "from nemoguardrails.rails.llm import LLMRails",
    ):
        result = _detect(f"{header}\n\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
        assert len(result.nodes) == 1, header


# ============================================================
# S1 — LLMRails(config)
# ============================================================

def test_llmrails_assigned_names_the_node_after_the_variable() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]
    node = result.nodes[0]
    assert node.kind == "guardrail"
    assert node.attributes["framework"] == "nemo_guardrails"
    assert node.attributes["source_file"] == "test.py"
    assert node.attributes["line_start"] == 3


def test_llmrails_unassigned_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    """A bare-expression construction has no name of its own."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nLLMRails(config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]
    assert result.nodes[0].kind == "guardrail"


def test_llmrails_inside_a_method_body_counts() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` reaches the whole tree; a method body is a call site.

    The construction is the rails the class wires up, and `source_file`
    plus `line_start` are the same treatment a module-level construction
    gets.
    """
    result = _detect(METHOD_SOURCE)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]
    line = METHOD_SOURCE.splitlines().index(
        "        self.rails = LLMRails(config)"
    ) + 1
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == line


def test_a_self_attribute_target_names_the_node() -> None:
    """`self.rails = LLMRails(...)` names the node after the attribute."""
    result = _detect(METHOD_SOURCE)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]


def test_an_annotated_assignment_names_the_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails: LLMRails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]


def test_a_multiple_target_assignment_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    """`a = b = LLMRails(...)` has two targets and no single name."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\na = b = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


def test_a_tuple_target_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails, other = LLMRails(config), None\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


def test_a_subscript_target_falls_back_to_the_class() -> None:
    """A list element is not a name."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails[0] = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


def test_a_construction_in_a_list_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = [LLMRails(config)]\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


def test_a_construction_passed_to_a_call_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nsetup(LLMRails(config))\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


def test_a_returned_construction_is_named_after_the_class() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """

def build(config):
    return LLMRails(config)
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]


# ============================================================
# S2 — the keyword form, and the arguments in general
# ============================================================

def test_the_keyword_form_is_a_construction() -> None:
    """`LLMRails(config=config)` — the SDK's own parameter name."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config=config)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]
    assert result.nodes[0].kind == "guardrail"


def test_the_arguments_are_not_read() -> None:
    """The shape is the call, not its argument list.

    An arity the SDK would reject at runtime is not the detector's call
    to make (module docstring): `LLMRails()` and
    `LLMRails(config, extra=1)` are the same construction to a reader of
    the AST.
    """
    for call in ("LLMRails()", 'LLMRails(config, extra=1)',
                 'LLMRails("config.yml")'):
        result = _detect(f"{IMPORT}\nrails = {call}\n")
        assert _names(result) == ["rails"], call


# ============================================================
# S3 — the qualified form
# ============================================================

def test_the_qualified_form_is_a_construction() -> None:
    """`nemoguardrails.rails.LLMRails(config)` — the rule is the name."""
    source = (
        "import nemoguardrails\n"
        "\n"
        "rails = nemoguardrails.rails.LLMRails(config)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]
    assert result.nodes[0].kind == "guardrail"


def test_a_module_alias_prefix_is_the_same_construction() -> None:
    """`import nemoguardrails as ng` then `ng.rails.LLMRails(...)`.

    The last dotted segment is `LLMRails` either way; the fast path
    matches the import, and the module alias is not needed to read the
    call.
    """
    source = (
        "import nemoguardrails as ng\n"
        "\n"
        "rails = ng.rails.LLMRails(config)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]


# ============================================================
# S4, S5 — RailsConfig is a config loader, not a guardrail
# ============================================================

def test_railsconfig_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """The config loader is not enforcement (module docstring).

    `RailsConfig(...)` builds the configuration value the rails is
    constructed from; the guardrail is the `LLMRails` instance.
    """
    result = _detect(CONFIG_IMPORT + "\nconfig = RailsConfig()\n")
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_railsconfig_from_path_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(
        CONFIG_IMPORT + '\nconfig = RailsConfig.from_path("config")\n'
    )
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_railsconfig_from_content_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    result = _detect(
        CONFIG_IMPORT + '\nconfig = RailsConfig.from_content(yaml="...")\n'
    )
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_railsconfig_argument_does_not_add_a_node() -> None:
    """The SDK's own three-line setup: exactly one node, the rails."""
    source = (
        "from nemoguardrails import LLMRails, RailsConfig\n"
        "\n"
        'config = RailsConfig.from_path("config")\n'
        "rails = LLMRails(config)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == 4


# ============================================================
# S6 — the instance methods are not constructions
# ============================================================

def test_the_instance_methods_are_not_constructions() -> None:
    """`rails.generate(...)` is an attribute call on an instance.

    The target's last segment is `generate`, not `LLMRails`: one node
    from the construction, none from the use. The whole SDK example is
    here — config, rails, generate — and the rails is the only node.
    """
    source = """\
from nemoguardrails import LLMRails, RailsConfig

config = RailsConfig.from_path("config")
rails = LLMRails(config)
result = rails.generate(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
async_result = rails.generate_async(messages=[])
"""
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["rails"]


def test_a_method_on_another_object_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """`bot.LLMRails`-free call sites are not this SDK's class."""
    result = _detect(
        IMPORT + "\nresult = client.generate_async(messages=[])\n"
    )
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# S7 — @action is custom logic, not the SDK's guardrail class
# ============================================================

def test_the_bare_action_decorator_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    """`@action` registers a project function in the rails runtime.

    What it does is the function's body, not the decorator's shape, and
    ADR-0024 §3 names the class construction.
    """
    source = IMPORT + """

@action
def check_input(text):
    return text
"""
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_the_qualified_action_decorator_is_not_a_node() -> None:
    source = (
        "from nemoguardrails import LLMRails\n"
        "from nemoguardrails.actions import action\n"
        "\n"
        "@action\n"
        "def check_input(text):\n"
        "    return text\n"
        "\n"
        '@nemoguardrails.action(name="check")\n'
        "def check_output(text):\n"
        "    return text\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_an_action_that_builds_rails_yields_only_the_rails() -> None:
    """The action is not a node; the construction inside it is."""
    source = """\
from nemoguardrails import LLMRails, RailsConfig
from nemoguardrails.actions import action


@action
def check_input(text):
    config = RailsConfig.from_path("config")
    return LLMRails(config)
"""
    result = _detect(source)
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails"]
    assert result.nodes[0].kind == "guardrail"



# ============================================================
# P1, P2 — provenance
# ============================================================

def test_the_node_names_the_detector_and_the_ast() -> None:
    """ADR-0024 §1: a detector-derived guardrail says so.

    `["ast", "framework:nemo_guardrails"]` is what keeps the three
    producers — capability, detector, LLM classifier — tellable apart
    in the graph.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.nodes[0].observed_by == [
        "ast", "framework:nemo_guardrails",
    ]


def test_the_framework_attribute_is_the_registry_name() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.nodes[0].attributes["framework"] == "nemo_guardrails"


def test_the_provenance_is_a_fresh_list() -> None:
    """Two nodes must not share one mutable `observed_by`."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nfirst = LLMRails(c)\nsecond = LLMRails(c)\n")
    first, second = result.nodes
    assert first.observed_by is not second.observed_by
    first.observed_by.append("x")
    assert second.observed_by == ["ast", "framework:nemo_guardrails"]


def test_the_detection_result_names_the_framework() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.framework == "nemo_guardrails"


def test_supported_versions_is_the_wildcard() -> None:
    """No version is inferable from an import line (ADR-0011)."""
    detector = NeMoGuardrailsDetector()
    assert detector.supported_versions == "*"
    assert detector.name == "nemo_guardrails"


# ============================================================
# E1 — no edges
# ============================================================

def test_the_detector_returns_no_edges() -> None:
    """Node-only. An `LLMRails` wraps a generation call at runtime.

    B.4a's `guardrail_edges` decides what a `guards` edge needs, and it
    runs on this node like on any other `guardrail` node.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert result.nodes != []
    assert result.edges == []


# ============================================================
# The id — two unnamed constructions collide
# ============================================================

def test_two_named_constructions_are_two_nodes_with_two_ids() -> None:
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nfirst = LLMRails(c)\nsecond = LLMRails(c)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["first", "second"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 2


def test_two_unnamed_constructions_share_one_id() -> None:
    """The id hashes the name, not the line: an accepted false negative.

    The detector emits one node per call site; the id is
    `framework + kind + file + name + host` (the existing detectors'
    rule), so two `LLMRails(config)` calls with no binding produce the
    same id and the graph keeps one row. `line_start` distinguishes them
    for a reader.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + "\nLLMRails(c)\nLLMRails(c)\n")
    assert _names(result) == ["LLMRails", "LLMRails"]
    assert len({node.id for node in result.nodes}) == 1
    assert [n.attributes["line_start"] for n in result.nodes] == [3, 4]


def test_the_id_does_not_depend_on_the_line() -> None:
    """The same construction at two lines is the same id, not two."""
    one = _detect(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    two = _detect(IMPORT + "\n\n\n\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    assert one.nodes[0].id == two.nodes[0].id


def test_the_id_depends_on_the_file() -> None:
    """Per-file and per-host, like the other detectors (ADR-0011)."""
    detector = NeMoGuardrailsDetector()
    tree = ast.parse(IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRails(config)\n")
    here = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "")
    there = detector.detect("b.py", tree, "")
    other_host = detector.detect("a.py", tree, "", host_id="other")
    assert here.nodes[0].id != there.nodes[0].id
    assert here.nodes[0].id != other_host.nodes[0].id


# ============================================================
# Order
# ============================================================

def test_the_nodes_are_in_source_order() -> None:
    """Two passes over the tree, one ordered result."""
    result = _detect(IMPORT + """
first = LLMRails(config)
LLMRails(config)
second = LLMRails(config)
""")
    assert _names(result) == ["first", "LLMRails", "second"]


# ============================================================
# The boundaries the module docstring states
# ============================================================

def test_an_aliased_import_is_not_matched() -> None:
    """`LLMRails as LR` is a false negative, documented and pinned.

    The detector matches the class name; an ADR-0011 per-file detector
    does not carry an alias table. The import is still the fast path.
    """
    source = (
        "from nemoguardrails import LLMRails as LR\n"
        "\n"
        "rails = LR(config)\n"
    )
    result = _detect(source)
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_class_level_factory_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """`LLMRails.from_config(...)` — a false negative, documented.

    `LLMRails` is a plain constructor; the SDK's factories live on
    `RailsConfig`, which is not a node. The rule is the target's last
    dotted segment, so a factory the SDK grows on `LLMRails` itself
    would need a one-line widening.
    """
    result = _detect(IMPORT + '\nrails = LLMRails.from_config("config")\n')
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_similarly_named_class_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    result = _detect(
        IMPORT + "\nrails = LLMRailsConfig(config)\nmy_rails = Rails(c)\n"
    )
    assert result.nodes == []


def test_a_call_returning_a_callable_is_not_a_construction() -> None:
    """A subscript or a call target is not a name: no node."""
    result = _detect(
        IMPORT + "\nrails = factories[0](config)\nother = make()(config)\n"
    )
    assert result.nodes == []


# ============================================================
# R1, R2 — registration
# ============================================================

def test_all_names_includes_nemo_guardrails() -> None:
    assert "nemo_guardrails" in all_names()
    assert all_names() == sorted(all_names())


def test_resolve_returns_an_instance() -> None:
    resolved = resolve(["nemo_guardrails"])
    assert len(resolved) == 1
    assert isinstance(resolved[0], NeMoGuardrailsDetector)
    assert resolved[0].name == "nemo_guardrails"


def test_the_registry_class_is_the_detector() -> None:
    from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors.registry import (
        KNOWN_DETECTORS,
    )
    assert KNOWN_DETECTORS["nemo_guardrails"] is NeMoGuardrailsDetector

# tests/test_llm_extractor.py
"""Unit tests for LLM extractor's config parsing."""

from __future__ import annotations

from aicorellator.parsing.llm_extractor import (
    _scan_toml,
    _scan_yaml,
    _walk_tree,
)


def test_yaml_simple() -> None:
    text = """
llm_provider: openai
llm_default_model: gpt-4o
"""
    result = _scan_yaml(text)
    assert result.get("LLM_PROVIDER") == "openai"
    assert result.get("LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL") == "gpt-4o"


def test_yaml_nested() -> None:
    """Nested YAML keys are flattened: services.llm.model."""
    text = """
services:
  llm:
    model: gpt-4o
    provider: openai
"""
    result = _scan_yaml(text)
    # Keys become SERVICES_LLM_MODEL etc.
    assert "SERVICES_LLM_MODEL" in result
    assert result["SERVICES_LLM_MODEL"] == "gpt-4o"


def test_yaml_docker_compose_style() -> None:
    """Docker-compose environment blocks are flattened."""
    text = """
services:
  app:
    environment:
      LLM_PROVIDER: openai
      OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://localhost:11434
"""
    result = _scan_yaml(text)
    assert result.get("SERVICES_APP_ENVIRONMENT_LLM_PROVIDER") == "openai"
    assert result.get("SERVICES_APP_ENVIRONMENT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL") == "http://localhost:11434"


def test_toml_simple() -> None:
    text = '''
[llm]
provider = "openai"
model = "gpt-4o"
'''
    result = _scan_toml(text)
    assert result.get("LLM_PROVIDER") == "openai"
    assert result.get("LLM_MODEL") == "gpt-4o"


def test_yaml_invalid_syntax() -> None:
    """Invalid YAML returns empty dict, does not crash."""
    assert _scan_yaml("this is : not : valid : yaml") == {}


def test_toml_invalid_syntax() -> None:
    assert _scan_toml("this is not = valid = toml") == {}


def test_walk_tree_filters_irrelevant_keys() -> None:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    _walk_tree({"database_url": "postgres://...", "llm_model": "gpt-4o"}, out)
    assert "LLM_MODEL" in out
    assert "DATABASE_URL" not in out

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_normalizer_stages/conftest.py
==============================================================================
"""Shared builders for the per-stage tests (step 4).

A stage takes a `GraphDelta` and a `NormalizeContext`. These fixtures
build both from a handful of keyword arguments — the files the stage may
read (written to `tmp_path`, because two stages parse source), the TSA
symbols, and whichever optional scan output the stage under test reads.

`Project.nodes(kind)` / `Project.edges(kind)` keep the assertions short
and readable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from aicorellator.ingestion.discovery import FileEntry, FileManifest
from aicorellator.ingestion.target import Target
from aicorellator.parsing.ast_normalizer import GraphDelta
from aicorellator.parsing.capability_extractor import FileCapabilities
from aicorellator.parsing.entry_points import EntryPointOutput
from aicorellator.parsing.framework_detectors import DetectionResult
from aicorellator.parsing.llm_extractor import LLMExtractorOutput
from aicorellator.parsing.models import TSASymbol, TSAOutput
from aicorellator.parsing.normalizer_context import (
    NormalizeContext,
    make_context,
)


@dataclass
class Project:
    """A context plus the delta a stage will fill."""

    ctx: NormalizeContext
    delta: GraphDelta = field(default_factory=GraphDelta)

    def nodes(self, kind: str) -> list:
        return [n for n in self.delta.nodes if n.kind == kind]

    def edges(self, kind: str) -> list:
        return [e for e in self.delta.edges if e.kind == kind]

    def named(self, name: str):
        return next(n for n in self.delta.nodes if n.name == name)


@pytest.fixture
def target(tmp_path: Path) -> Target:
    """A target pointing at an empty temp directory."""
    return Target(root=tmp_path, kind="folder")


@pytest.fixture
def project(target: Target):
    """Build a `Project` from a minimal scan input set."""

    def build(
        files: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        symbols: list[TSASymbol] | None = None,
        entry_points: EntryPointOutput | None = None,
        llm_output: LLMExtractorOutput | None = None,
        capabilities: dict[str, FileCapabilities] | None = None,
        detection: DetectionResult | None = None,
        host_id: str = "localhost",
    ) -> Project:
        manifest = FileManifest(target=target)
        for index, (path, source) in enumerate((files or {}).items()):
            abs_path = target.root / path
            abs_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            abs_path.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
            manifest.files.append(FileEntry(
                path=path,
                abs_path=abs_path,
                language="python",
                content_hash=f"h{index}",
                size=len(source),
            ))
        ctx = make_context(
            manifest,
            TSAOutput(symbols=symbols or []),
            entry_points=entry_points,
            llm_output=llm_output,
            capabilities=capabilities,
            framework_detection=detection,
            host_id=host_id,
        )
        return Project(ctx=ctx)

    return build

"""BodyAttributeStage: `returns_data` and `sink_data_flow` backfill."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.graph.models import Node
from aicorellator.parsing.normalizer_stages import BodyAttributeStage

SOURCE = '''\
import os


def read_file(query):
    return search(query)


def delete_file(file_id):
    os.remove(file_id)
'''


def _line_of(name: str) -> int:
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(SOURCE)):
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == name:
            return node.lineno
    raise AssertionError(name)


def _node(kind: str, name: str) -> Node:
    return Node(
        id=f"{kind}:{name}", kind=kind, name=name, host_id="localhost",
        attributes={"source_file": "server.py", "line_start": _line_of(name)},
    )


def test_tool_and_sink_get_their_body_attributes(project) -> None:
    """A tool records whether it returns data; a sink how it reaches a call."""
    p = project(files={"server.py": SOURCE})
    tool = _node("tool", "read_file")
    sink = _node("sink", "delete_file")
    p.delta.nodes.extend([tool, sink])

    delta = BodyAttributeStage().apply(p.delta, p.ctx)

    assert tool.attributes["returns_data"] is True
    assert sink.attributes["sink_data_flow"] == "parameter_match"
    assert delta.nodes == [tool, sink]


def test_existing_attributes_are_not_overwritten(project) -> None:
    """A detector-enriched node keeps what the detector decided."""
    p = project(files={"server.py": SOURCE})
    tool = _node("tool", "read_file")
    tool.attributes["returns_data"] = False
    p.delta.nodes.append(tool)

    BodyAttributeStage().apply(p.delta, p.ctx)

    assert tool.attributes["returns_data"] is False

FILE: tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_class_nodes.py

"""ClassNodeStage: a class symbol becomes a node of its classified kind.

The kind comes from the class body's capabilities (ADR-0009), not from
its name (ADR-0016, decision 7).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from aicorellator.parsing.capability_extractor import (
    FileCapabilities,
    SymbolCapabilities,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.models import TSASymbol
from aicorellator.parsing.normalizer_stages import ClassNodeStage

AGENTS = "agents/invoice.py"


def _caps(*pairs: tuple[str, str]) -> dict[str, FileCapabilities]:
    """Capabilities for named classes in `AGENTS` (ADR-0009)."""
    return {
        AGENTS: FileCapabilities(
            file_path=AGENTS,
            symbols=[
                SymbolCapabilities(
                    symbol_name=name,
                    file_path=AGENTS,
                    capabilities={capability},
                )
                for name, capability in pairs
            ],
        ),
    }


def _class_symbol(name: str) -> TSASymbol:
    return TSASymbol(
        name=name,
        kind="class",
        file_path=AGENTS,
        line_start=10,
        line_end=50,
    )


def test_class_symbol_becomes_an_agent_node(project) -> None:
    """A class whose body calls an LLM is an agent node."""
    p = project(
        files={AGENTS: ""},
        symbols=[_class_symbol("InvoiceAgent")],
        capabilities=_caps(("InvoiceAgent", "calls_llm")),
    )

    delta = ClassNodeStage().apply(p.delta, p.ctx)

    assert [(n.kind, n.name) for n in delta.nodes] == [
        ("agent", "InvoiceAgent"),
    ]
    assert delta.nodes[0].attributes["source_file"] == AGENTS
    assert delta.nodes[0].attributes["line_start"] == 10


def test_class_symbol_becomes_a_sink_node(project) -> None:
    """A class whose body writes is a sink, whatever it is called."""
    p = project(
        files={AGENTS: ""},
        symbols=[_class_symbol("RandomHelper")],
        capabilities=_caps(("RandomHelper", "writes_filesystem")),
    )

    delta = ClassNodeStage().apply(p.delta, p.ctx)

    assert [(n.kind, n.name) for n in delta.nodes] == [
        ("sink", "RandomHelper"),
    ]
    assert delta.nodes[0].attributes["category"] == "filesystem"


def test_agent_name_without_a_capability_is_not_a_node(project) -> None:
    """The class-A suffix rule is gone (ADR-0016, decision 7).

    `InvoiceAgent` used to be an agent because of its name. It is a node
    now only if its body says so, or if a framework detector saw it.
    """
    p = project(
        files={AGENTS: ""},
        symbols=[_class_symbol("InvoiceAgent")],
    )

    delta = ClassNodeStage().apply(p.delta, p.ctx)

    assert delta.nodes == []
