def _source_node(line: int = READ_LINE) -> Node:
    return Node(
        id="untrusted_source:1", kind="untrusted_source",
        name="user_upload:s3", host_id="localhost",
        attributes={
            "source_file": HANDLER,
            "source_type": "user_upload",
            "line_start": line,
        },
    )


def _resolve(built):
    """Resolve, and keep the edges the way `StoreResolverStage` does.

    The resolver returns the edges and puts its store *nodes* in the
    delta; the stage is what appends the edges. A test that only read
    the return value would leave the graph without them, so this does
    both — the same two lines the stage runs.
    """
    edges = StoreResolver([S3Family()]).resolve(built.delta, built.ctx)
    built.delta.edges.extend(edges)
    return edges


# ============================================================
# E1 — one write, one read, one literal
# ============================================================

def test_one_store_and_two_edges(scan) -> None:
    """The family's two sites become one store (§1) and two edges."""
    built = _scene(scan)
    edges = _resolve(built)

    stores = built.nodes("store")
    assert [store.name for store in stores] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert stores[0].attributes == {
        "family": "s3", "identity_hint": LITERAL,
    }
    assert stores[0].confidence == 1.0

    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to", "reads_from"]
    writes_to, reads_from = edges
    assert writes_to.source_id == "tool:handle"
    assert writes_to.target_id == stores[0].id
    assert reads_from.source_id == stores[0].id
    assert reads_from.target_id == "untrusted_source:1"


def test_the_confidence_is_the_signals_the_pair_earned(scan) -> None:
    """Equal literals (`0.6`) and the same module (`0.2`) over a base.

    The number is computed from `store.confidence`'s constants and not
    from prose: `combine_signals(BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL,
    CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE])` is the `0.776` §8's signals give the
    pair, and it is above the default threshold — the shape the whole
    mechanism exists for, one bucket and one key named twice.
    """
    expected = combine_signals(
        BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE]
    )
    assert round(expected, 4) == 0.776

    built = _scene(scan)
    edges = _resolve(built)
    assert [round(edge.identity_confidence, 4) for edge in edges] == [
        round(expected, 4), round(expected, 4),
    ]


def test_the_edges_are_structural(scan) -> None:
    """ADR-0021 §4, ADR-0015/0016: a declaration, with no data-flow claim."""
    built = _scene(scan)
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert {edge.flow_kind for edge in edges} == {"structural"}
    assert {edge.observed_by[0] for edge in edges} == {"ast"}
    assert {edge.data_flow_confirmed for edge in edges} == {None}


def test_the_familys_edges_are_a_chain_group(scan, store) -> None:
    """E1 — the two links meet at the store, and that is a group (§6).

    The chains around the store are hand-built, because the family
    produces the two *links* and not the paths they sit on:

        entry_point --has_access_to--> tool:handle --writes_to--> store
        store --reads_from--> source --has_access_to--> reader --> sink
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        nodes=[
            _writer_node(),
            _source_node(),
            Node(
                id="entry_point:1", kind="entry_point", name="POST /upload",
                host_id="localhost",
                attributes={"source_file": HANDLER, "line_start": DEF_LINE},
            ),
            Node(
                id="tool:reader", kind="tool", name="read_report",
                host_id="localhost",
                attributes={"source_file": HANDLER, "line_start": DEF_LINE},
            ),
            Node(
                id="sink:1", kind="sink", name="run_shell",
                host_id="localhost",
                attributes={"source_file": HANDLER, "line_start": DEF_LINE},
            ),
        ],
    )
    built.delta.edges.extend([
        _link("edge:1", "entry_point:1", "tool:handle"),
        _link("edge:2", "untrusted_source:1", "tool:reader"),
        _link("edge:3", "tool:reader", "sink:1"),
    ])
    _resolve(built)
    write_graph(store, built.delta)

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups()
    assert len(groups) == 1
    group = groups[0]
    assert group.store_id == built.nodes("store")[0].id
    assert group.store_name == f"s3:{LITERAL}"
    assert group.untrusted_source_id == "untrusted_source:1"
    assert group.weak is False
    assert round(group.store_confidence, 4) == 0.776


# ============================================================
# E2 — one side only, and E3 — a read with no source
# ============================================================

def test_a_write_with_no_read_is_a_store_with_one_edge(scan) -> None:
    """The store exists — the literal named it — and nothing reads it.

    §5 keeps the store the literal side named. The confidence is the
    literal alone, `1 − 0.7 × 0.4 = 0.72`: with no counterpart there is
    no code-context signal to add, and the literal is what named it.
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            f'    s3.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to"]
    assert round(edges[0].identity_confidence, 4) == round(
        combine_signals(BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL]), 4
    )


def test_a_read_with_no_write_is_a_store_with_one_edge(scan) -> None:
    """And the same from the other side."""
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle():\n"
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
        nodes=[_source_node(line=2)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["reads_from"]
    assert edges[0].target_id == "untrusted_source:1"


def test_a_read_the_graph_did_not_register_is_no_reads_from(scan) -> None:
    """E3 — a read points *from* a store; with no source there is no edge.

    A read's role is the graph's (`untrusted_source` nodes, 1.3a), and
    an S3 read is not one of the source types — `user_upload` is
    B.3b-user_upload. The store is still created: the literal named it,
    and the read is a fact about it even when the link has no target.
    """
    built = _scene(scan, nodes=[_writer_node()])
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to"]


# ============================================================
# The identity — two stores, and the containment branch
# ============================================================

def test_two_different_buckets_are_two_stores_and_no_cross_pair(
    scan,
) -> None:
    """Two buckets, two stores; neither side is claimed for the other's.

    The write names `docs` and the read `other`, in the same module: the
    code context agrees about everything and the literals do not. §8's
    rule is "no link", so the two edges that come out name the store
    their own site named.
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            f'    s3.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="other", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
        nodes=[_writer_node(), _source_node(line=3)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    stores = {store.name: store.id for store in built.nodes("store")}
    assert sorted(stores) == [f"s3:{LITERAL}", f"s3:other/{KEY}"]

    writes_to = [edge for edge in edges if edge.kind == "writes_to"]
    reads_from = [edge for edge in edges if edge.kind == "reads_from"]
    assert [edge.target_id for edge in writes_to] == [stores[f"s3:{LITERAL}"]]
    assert [edge.source_id for edge in reads_from] == [
        stores[f"s3:other/{KEY}"]
    ]


def test_a_bucket_and_a_bucket_with_a_key_are_two_stores(scan) -> None:
    """The containment branch, through the resolver (B.3b-fs-followup).

    A write naming `'docs/uploads/'` and a read naming
    `'docs/uploads/report.txt'` are two literals and two stores, and each
    site attaches to **both**: `literal_match` relates them on
    containment, and the resolver's attachment is the site's own literal
    plus every key that row relates to it. So each store earns one write
    and one read — the equal literal on one side and the prefix row on
    the other, `1 − 0.7 × 0.4 × 0.8 = 0.776` and `1 − 0.7 × 0.7 × 0.8 =
    0.608`. The branch itself is pinned in
    `tests/test_store_core/test_confidence.py`.
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            f'    s3.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="uploads/")\n'
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
        nodes=[_writer_node(), _source_node(line=3)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert literal_match("docs/uploads/", LITERAL) == LITERAL_PREFIX
    stores = {store.name: store.id for store in built.nodes("store")}
    assert sorted(stores) == ["s3:docs/uploads/", f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.target_id for edge in edges if edge.kind == "writes_to"] == [
        stores["s3:docs/uploads/"], stores[f"s3:{LITERAL}"],
    ]
    assert [edge.source_id for edge in edges if edge.kind == "reads_from"] == [
        stores["s3:docs/uploads/"], stores[f"s3:{LITERAL}"],
    ]
    equal = combine_signals(BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE])
    prefix = combine_signals(BASE, [LITERAL_PREFIX, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE])
    assert [round(edge.identity_confidence, 4) for edge in edges] == [
        round(equal, 4), round(prefix, 4),
        round(prefix, 4), round(equal, 4),
    ]


def test_an_unresolved_bucket_attaches_to_the_store_it_cannot_name(
    scan,
) -> None:
    """§5's wildcard: an unnamed site points at every store of its family.

    The write's bucket is a parameter, so its hint is `None` and §5
    keeps the store the *read* named, letting the write point at it.
    The write's literal signal is `LITERAL_ONE_SIDE` — it names no
    store of its own — while the read names the store exactly, so the
    two links differ: `1 − 0.7 × 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.552` for the write and
    the equal pair's `0.776` for the read.
    """
    from_unresolved = combine_signals(
        BASE, [LITERAL_ONE_SIDE, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE]
    )
    from_equal = combine_signals(
        BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE]
    )
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            "    s3.put_object(Bucket=payload['bucket'], "
            "Key=payload['key'])\n"
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to", "reads_from"]
    assert [round(edge.identity_confidence, 4) for edge in edges] == [
        round(from_unresolved, 4), round(from_equal, 4),
    ]


# ============================================================
# B.3b-s3-followup — three spellings, one store
# ============================================================

# `handle` binds a boto3 handle on line 2 and writes with it on line 3,
# then binds an `s3fs` handle on line 4 and reads `s3://...` with it on
# line 5. The two calls do not look alike and name the same store.
FOLLOWUP_SOURCE = f'''\
def handle(payload):
    s3_client = boto3.client("s3")
    s3_client.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}", Body=payload)
    fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()
    return fs.open("s3://{BUCKET}/{KEY}", "rb")
'''

FOLLOWUP_READ_LINE = 5


def test_a_tracked_handle_and_an_s3fs_path_are_one_store(scan) -> None:
    """The handle and the `s3://` path name the same identity hint.

    The family's half is pinned in `test_s3.py`; what this pins is that
    the *store* is one node and the pair is one group — `_identity_hint`
    is `bucket + "/" + key` whichever spelling produced it, so a boto3
    write and an `s3fs` read meet at `s3:docs/uploads/report.txt` with
    §8's equal-literal confidence.
    """
    expected = combine_signals(
        BASE, [LITERAL_EQUAL, CODE_CONTEXT_SAME_MODULE]
    )
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=FOLLOWUP_SOURCE,
        nodes=[_writer_node(), _source_node(line=FOLLOWUP_READ_LINE)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    stores = built.nodes("store")
    assert [store.name for store in stores] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert stores[0].attributes == {
        "family": "s3", "identity_hint": LITERAL,
    }
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to", "reads_from"]
    writes_to, reads_from = edges
    assert writes_to.source_id == "tool:handle"
    assert writes_to.target_id == stores[0].id
    assert reads_from.source_id == stores[0].id
    assert reads_from.target_id == "untrusted_source:1"
    assert [round(edge.identity_confidence, 4) for edge in edges] == [
        round(expected, 4), round(expected, 4),
    ]


def test_a_minio_write_and_a_boto3_read_are_one_store(scan) -> None:
    """MinIO's positional `(bucket, key)` names the same store.

    The write is `mc.put_object("docs", "uploads/report.txt", fileobj)`
    and the read is `s3.get_object(Bucket=..., Key=...)`: two argument
    layouts, one literal, so one store and the equal-literal pair.
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            "    mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
            f'    mc.put_object("{BUCKET}", "{KEY}", payload)\n'
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
        nodes=[_writer_node(), _source_node(line=4)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["writes_to", "reads_from"]


def test_an_untracked_receiver_leaves_the_store_unnamed(scan) -> None:
    """The follow-up's false negatives are false *negatives*, not noise.

    `c = get_client()` is not a handle, so line 3 is not a site and the
    write side contributes nothing: the read alone names the store, one
    edge, and no `writes_to`. A family that guessed would have produced
    a confident edge from a call it could not read.
    """
    built = _scene(
        scan,
        source=(
            "def handle(payload):\n"
            "    c = get_client()\n"
            f'    c.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}", Body=payload)\n'
            f'    return s3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")\n'
        ),
        nodes=[_writer_node(), _source_node(line=4)],
    )
    edges = _resolve(built)

    assert [store.name for store in built.nodes("store")] == [f"s3:{LITERAL}"]
    assert [edge.kind for edge in edges] == ["reads_from"]


# ============================================================
# Determinism
# ============================================================

def test_two_runs_over_one_scene_give_the_same_edges(scan) -> None:
    """The edges are a function of the code, not of the traversal.

    The store's id is content-derived (`store_node_id`) and the edges'
    are too, so the same scene resolved twice yields the same ids in the
    same order — which is what the pipeline depends on when it writes
    the delta.
    """
    first = _scene(scan)
    first_edges = _resolve(first)
    second = _scene(scan)
    again = _resolve(second)

    assert [edge.id for edge in again] == [edge.id for edge in first_edges]
    assert [store.name for store in second.nodes("store")] == [
        store.name for store in first.nodes("store")
    ]
    assert [store.name for store in second.nodes("store")] == [
        f"s3:{LITERAL}"
    ]


def _link(edge_id: str, source_id: str, target_id: str) -> Edge:
    """A control edge — the kind the chains around a store are made of."""
    return Edge(
        id=edge_id, source_id=source_id, target_id=target_id,
        kind="has_access_to", host_id="localhost", flow_kind="control",
    )

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_families/test_db.py
==============================================================================
"""The `db` family — call shapes, tables, and what it ignores.

ADR-0021 §12 gives a family one job: read a module's AST once, report the
call sites that write into and read from a store it recognizes, and say
what literal each site names the store with. For `db` the store is a
table, and the literal is the table name the SQL string carries.
Everything else — identity, confidence, nodes, edges — is
`StoreResolver`'s and is pinned in
`tests/test_store_core/test_db_resolver.py`. What is here is the family's
half:

  - **the write shapes** (W1–W6): `INSERT` / `UPDATE` / `DELETE` /
    `REPLACE` / `MERGE` through `execute`, `executemany`, and the
    `sql=` / `statement=` spellings;
  - **the read shapes** (R1–R4): `SELECT`, a CTE, `EXPLAIN` and
    `PRAGMA`;
  - **the table extraction**: quoting, the first `FROM` winning, and the
    regex's documented false negatives (a quoted identifier with a
    space, a `FROM` inside a CTE body);
  - **the non-sites**: the ORM methods, the fetches, the DDL keywords, a
    `text(...)` argument and a non-literal SQL string;
  - **the receivers**: the handle names that match, underscores and all;
  - **the registration**: importing `aicorellator.store` is enough for
    the resolver to see `db`.

The family is orthogonal to the sink rules — `cursor.execute("INSERT
INTO ...")` is a `writes_db` sink today — and nothing here asserts
anything about capabilities; `patterns.py` is not this step's.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.store import registry
from aicorellator.store.families.base import Family, ReadSite, WriteSite
from aicorellator.store.families.db import DbFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.fs import FsFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.s3 import S3Family

HANDLER = "app/handler.py"
TABLE = "documents"


def _writes(source: str) -> list[WriteSite]:
    return DbFamily().detect_writes(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _reads(source: str) -> list[ReadSite]:
    return DbFamily().detect_reads(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _hints(sites: list) -> list[str | None]:
    return [site.identity_hint for site in sites]


# ============================================================
# The write shapes (W1–W6)
# ============================================================

def test_insert_into_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W1 — `INSERT INTO <table>`, with the parameters ignored."""
    sites = _writes(
        f'cursor.execute("INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (?)", (1,))'
    )
    assert _hints(sites) == [TABLE]
    assert [site.file_path for site in sites] == [HANDLER]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]
    assert _reads(
        f'cursor.execute("INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (?)", (1,))'
    ) == []


def test_update_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W2 — `UPDATE <table> SET ...`; the table follows the keyword."""
    source = f"conn.execute('UPDATE {TABLE} SET x=1')"
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [TABLE]
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_delete_from_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W3 — `DELETE FROM <table>`; the `FROM` picks the table."""
    source = f"cur.execute('DELETE FROM {TABLE} WHERE id=1')"
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [TABLE]
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_executemany_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W4 — the row argument is not the store's identity."""
    source = (
        f"cur.executemany('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (?)', rows)"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [TABLE]
    # A write spelling, and only that (the module docstring's choice).
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_replace_and_merge_are_write_sites() -> None:
    """W5 — the other two write keywords the brief names."""
    for source in (
        f"cursor.execute('REPLACE INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('MERGE INTO {TABLE} USING src ON 1=1')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [TABLE], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_sql_keywords_are_read_too() -> None:
    """W6 — `sql=` and `statement=`, the spellings a call may name it."""
    assert _hints(
        _writes(f"cursor.execute(sql='INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (?)')")
    ) == [TABLE]
    assert _hints(
        _writes(f"cursor.execute(statement='UPDATE {TABLE} SET x=1')")
    ) == [TABLE]


# ============================================================
# The read shapes (R1–R4)
# ============================================================

def test_select_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R1 — `SELECT * FROM <table>`."""
    sites = _reads(f"cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')")
    assert _hints(sites) == [TABLE]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]
    # A read's role is the context's business, and this family has none.
    assert [site.source_type for site in sites] == [None]


def test_a_select_with_a_where_clause_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R2 — the first `FROM` is the table; the rest is ignored."""
    source = f"conn.execute('SELECT id FROM {TABLE} WHERE x=1')"
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [TABLE]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_a_cte_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R3 — `WITH` is a read, and the outer `FROM` names the store."""
    source = (
        f"cursor.execute('WITH cte AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')"
    )
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [TABLE]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_explain_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R4 — `EXPLAIN` prefixes a statement; the `FROM` still names it."""
    source = f"cursor.execute('EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')"
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [TABLE]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_pragma_is_a_read_site_with_no_table() -> None:
    """`PRAGMA` is a read keyword, and it names a table without a `FROM`.

    The keyword says the call reads; the regex, which reads a `FROM`,
    finds no table, so the hint is `None` — §5's wildcard, and not a
    guessed table.
    """
    source = "cursor.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON')"
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [None]
    assert _writes(source) == []


# ============================================================
# The direction is the SQL keyword, and the receiver is a name
# ============================================================

def test_each_statement_states_its_own_direction() -> None:
    """`execute` is both directions; only the SQL string can decide.

    Each source is checked in *both* lists, because a site in the wrong
    one would pair a reader with a reader. The arguments are the same on
    both sides, so only the keyword can decide.
    """
    writes = (
        f"cursor.execute('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('UPDATE {TABLE} SET x=1')",
        f"cursor.execute('DELETE FROM {TABLE}')",
        f"cursor.execute('REPLACE INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('MERGE INTO {TABLE} USING s ON 1=1')",
    )
    reads = (
        f"cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
        f"cursor.execute('SELECT id FROM {TABLE} WHERE x=1')",
        f"cursor.execute('EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
        f"cursor.execute('WITH c AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
    )
    for source in writes:
        assert _writes(source), source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source
    for source in reads:
        assert _reads(source), source
        assert _writes(source) == [], source


def test_the_keywords_are_matched_without_regard_to_case() -> None:
    """SQL keywords are case-insensitive, and the sink side uppercases.

    `capability_extractor` uppercases the string before comparing it
    with `SQL_WRITE_KEYWORDS`, so a lowercase statement is a `writes_db`
    sink; the store family reads the same string the same way.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes(f"cursor.execute('insert into {TABLE} (id) values (?)')")
    ) == [TABLE]
    assert _hints(
        _reads(f"cursor.execute('select * from {TABLE}')")
    ) == [TABLE]


def test_the_receiver_spellings_that_match() -> None:
    """The conventional handles for a connection, a cursor or a session.

    The last segment is what counts, so `self.cursor` and
    `db.session` match as well as the bare names; the leading
    underscore is stripped, so `self._cursor` and `_conn` name the
    same handles `cursor` and `conn` do (1.2a.3e).
    """
    for receiver in (
        "cursor", "cur", "conn", "connection", "db", "session", "engine",
        "self.cursor", "self._cursor", "self._conn", "self._session",
        "self.db.session", "self._db",
    ):
        source = f"{receiver}.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')"
        assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [TABLE], source


def test_a_bare_execute_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """No receiver, no store: the AST does not know the object.

    `execute(...)` is a method on a name the family cannot resolve, and
    §5 prefers "no store" to a guessed one.
    """
    for source in (
        f"execute('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_receiver_outside_the_set_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """The receiver set is the whole of what the AST can say.

    `self.adapter.execute(...)` is some other object's statement call —
    1.2a.3g's shell-adapter shape, and not a database handle — and a
    receiver that is an expression is not a name at all. Both are the
    false negatives the module docstring lists.
    """
    for source in (
        f"self.adapter.execute('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"obj.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
        f"cur_.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
        f"get_conn().execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_verb_is_not_normalized() -> None:
    """`cursor._execute(...)` is a private method, not `execute`."""
    source = f"cursor._execute('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')"
    assert _writes(source) == []


# ============================================================
# The table, out of the SQL string
# ============================================================

def test_the_table_comes_back_however_it_is_quoted() -> None:
    """A bare, a double-quoted and a backticked identifier are one table.

    The regex accepts the three spellings and returns the identifier
    without its wrapper, so the store's identity does not depend on how
    the statement spelled the table.
    """
    for source in (
        f"cursor.execute('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('INSERT INTO \"{TABLE}\" (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('INSERT INTO `{TABLE}` (id) VALUES (1)')",
        f"cursor.execute('INSERT INTO \"{TABLE}\"')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [TABLE], source


def test_the_write_regex_takes_the_keywords_first_match() -> None:
    """`INTO` comes first, so a nested `FROM` does not name the store.

    `INSERT INTO t SELECT ... FROM x` writes `t`: the scan is left to
    right and `INTO` precedes `FROM`. `DELETE FROM t WHERE id IN
    (SELECT id FROM u)` is the same rule with the other keyword.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes("cursor.execute('INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM x')")
    ) == ["t"]
    assert _hints(
        _writes(
            "cursor.execute('DELETE FROM t WHERE id IN "
            "(SELECT id FROM u)')"
        )
    ) == ["t"]


def test_a_joins_table_is_not_the_store() -> None:
    """The first `FROM` is the store; a `JOIN` is a second table.

    `FROM a, b` is the same rule: the comma-separated list starts at
    `a`, and the family does not read past it.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _reads(f"cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM {TABLE} JOIN other ON 1=1')")
    ) == [TABLE]
    assert _hints(
        _reads("cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM a, b WHERE a.id=b.id')")
    ) == ["a"]


def test_a_quoted_identifier_with_a_space_names_no_table() -> None:
    """The identifier is a word; `"my table"` fails the regex.

    A documented false negative: the table is unusual, and the AST is
    not asked to parse a quoted identifier. The site is still a write —
    the `INSERT` said so — with `None` as its hint, and the read side
    names none either.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes("cursor.execute('INSERT INTO \"my table\" (id) VALUES (1)')")
    ) == [None]
    assert _hints(
        _reads("cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM \"my table\"')")
    ) == [None]


def test_a_from_inside_a_cte_body_wins_when_it_comes_first() -> None:
    """The documented cost of the first-match rule, pinned.

    `WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM raw) SELECT * FROM documents` names `raw`
    here, because the match is the first `FROM` in the string and the
    family does not parse the CTE's nesting. The CTE form the brief
    names — a body with no `FROM` of its own — names the outer table.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _reads(
            f"cursor.execute('WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM raw) "
            f"SELECT * FROM {TABLE}')"
        )
    ) == ["raw"]


# ============================================================
# Unresolved SQL — §5's `None`, and no site
# ============================================================

def test_a_non_literal_sql_string_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """`cursor.execute(sql)` names no string, so no direction and no site.

    This is the one place the family is stricter than `fs` and `s3`: the
    direction lives in the same literal the table does, so a call whose
    SQL the AST cannot read can be neither a write nor a read. §5's
    answer is silence, not a guessed direction.
    """
    for source in (
        "cursor.execute(sql)",
        "cursor.execute(sql, params)",
        "cursor.execute(get_sql())",
        "cursor.execute(SQL_INSERT_DOCUMENTS)",
        "cursor.executemany(sql, rows)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_literal_prefix_names_the_direction_and_not_the_table() -> None:
    """`"INSERT INTO " + t` is a write site whose hint is `None`.

    The left side of the `+` is the literal the site names — the
    direction — and the table is on the other side, where the regex
    cannot see it. §5 keeps the store the *other* side names and lets
    this one point at it (the wildcard).
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("cursor.execute('INSERT INTO ' + t)")) == [None]
    assert _hints(
        _reads("cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM ' + t)")
    ) == [None]
    assert _writes("cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM ' + t)") == []


def test_an_fstring_names_the_constant_part_before_the_first_brace() -> None:
    """`f'INSERT INTO {t} ...'` names no table; a later brace is fine.

    When the placeholder comes before the table — the `INSERT INTO {t}`
    spelling — the prefix ends at `INTO`, so there is no table. When the
    table is literal and a *later* part is not — `f'INSERT INTO t
    ({col}) VALUES (?)'` — the prefix carries the table.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes("cursor.execute(f'INSERT INTO {t} (id) VALUES (?)')")
    ) == [None]
    assert _hints(
        _writes("cursor.execute(f'INSERT INTO t ({col}) VALUES (?)')")
    ) == ["t"]
    assert _hints(
        _reads("cursor.execute(f'SELECT * FROM {t}')")
    ) == [None]


# ============================================================
# `executemany`, and `WITH`
# ============================================================

def test_a_select_in_an_executemany_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """The choice the module docstring states, pinned.

    `executemany` is a write spelling: the read shape names `execute`.
    A read keyword in it is therefore neither a write (the keyword is
    not a write keyword) nor a read (the method is not `execute`), and
    the call is no site at all.
    """
    source = f"cursor.executemany('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}', rows)"
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_data_modifying_cte_is_read_as_a_read() -> None:
    """`WITH` is a read, and a `WITH ... INSERT` is the false negative.

    The outer statement of `WITH c AS (SELECT 1) INSERT INTO t SELECT *
    FROM c` is a write, and reaching `t` means parsing the CTE list,
    which this family does not do: the leading keyword is `WITH`, so the
    call is a read and the first `FROM` names `c`.
    """
    source = (
        "cursor.execute('WITH c AS (SELECT 1) INSERT INTO t "
        "SELECT * FROM c')"
    )
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["c"]


# ============================================================
# Not in `db`
# ============================================================

def test_the_fetches_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """A fetch collects the rows of an `execute` that already ran.

    The `execute` is the store operation, and the fetch is the
    `reads_db` sink half of it (`patterns.ORM_READS_RULE`); here it
    names no table and no statement.
    """
    for source in ("cursor.fetchone()", "cursor.fetchall()",
                   "cur.fetchmany(10)"):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_orm_methods_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """`db.add` / `db.delete` / `session.commit` name no table.

    They are `writes_db` sinks (`patterns.ORM_WRITES_RULE`) and they
    stay sinks; a store operation needs a table, and the call names
    none — the object it holds is the table, and the AST cannot see
    inside it.
    """
    for source in (
        "db.add(obj)",
        "db.add_all(objs)",
        "db.delete(obj)",
        "db.commit()",
        "session.add(obj)",
        "session.delete(obj)",
        "session.commit()",
        "session.flush()",
        "session.merge(obj)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_query_api_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """`session.query(Document)` names a mapped class, not a table.

    Turning `Document` into its table is type resolution, not a literal
    (§5: an identity the AST cannot resolve stays unresolved).
    """
    for source in (
        "session.query(Document)",
        "session.query(Document).all()",
        "session.query(Document).filter_by(id=1).first()",
        "db.get(Document, 1)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_ddl_keywords_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """A schema statement creates, drops or alters — it names no store.

    `patterns.SQL_WRITE_KEYWORDS` carries `DROP`, `CREATE`, `ALTER` and
    `TRUNCATE` for the sink side; the store family has no table to pair
    for them, so they are neither direction and not a site.
    """
    for source in (
        "cursor.execute('DROP TABLE documents')",
        "cursor.execute('CREATE TABLE documents (id int)')",
        "cursor.execute('ALTER TABLE documents ADD COLUMN x int')",
        "cursor.execute('TRUNCATE TABLE documents')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_text_wrapped_sql_string_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """`text(...)` hides the string one call down — a known miss.

    SQLAlchemy 2.0 spells statements `text("...")`, and the family reads
    a literal *argument*, not inside a call. Unwrapping `text(...)` is a
    separate step (the module docstring).
    """
    for source in (
        f"conn.execute(text('SELECT * FROM {TABLE}'))",
        f"session.execute(text('INSERT INTO {TABLE} (id) VALUES (1)'))",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_statement_whose_keyword_is_neither_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """No direction, no site: an empty string, a comment, a `BEGIN`."""
    for source in (
        "cursor.execute('')",
        "cursor.execute('   ')",
        "cursor.execute('-- a comment')",
        "cursor.execute('BEGIN')",
        "cursor.execute('VACUUM')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


# ============================================================
# Order, and the interface
# ============================================================

def test_the_sites_come_back_in_source_order() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` is breadth-first; the family reports source order.

    The nested write is first in the file and *second* in the walk, so
    this pins the sort rather than the traversal.
    """
    source = (
        "if flag:\n"
        "    cursor.execute('INSERT INTO a (x) VALUES (1)')\n"
        "cursor.execute('UPDATE b SET x=1')\n"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["a", "b"]
    assert [site.line for site in _writes(source)] == [2, 3]


def test_two_runs_over_one_module_report_the_same_order() -> None:
    """The report is a function of the code, not of the traversal."""
    source = (
        "cursor.execute('INSERT INTO a (x) VALUES (1)')\n"
        "cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM a')\n"
        "cur.executemany('INSERT INTO b (x) VALUES (?)', rows)\n"
    )
    first = [(site.line, site.identity_hint) for site in _writes(source)]
    second = [(site.line, site.identity_hint) for site in _writes(source)]
    assert first == second == [(1, "a"), (3, "b")]


def test_the_context_is_accepted_and_unused() -> None:
    """B.3b-user_upload is the first family with a context to read."""
    tree = ast.parse("cursor.execute('INSERT INTO documents (id) VALUES (1)')")
    assert len(DbFamily().detect_writes(tree, HANDLER, context=None)) == 1
    assert len(
        DbFamily().detect_reads(
            ast.parse("cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM documents')"),
            HANDLER, context=object(),
        )
    ) == 1


def test_the_family_declares_its_name() -> None:
    """The name is the registry key and half of a store's identity (§1)."""
    assert DbFamily.name == "db"


def test_the_family_is_a_family() -> None:
    assert isinstance(DbFamily(), Family)


def test_importing_the_store_package_registers_the_family() -> None:
    """No caller names `db`; the import of the package is the registration.

    `tests/test_store_core/test_db_resolver.py` builds the resolver with
    an explicit family, so the registry is what this pins: the family
    the pipeline will find is the one this module imports.
    """
    assert registry.FAMILIES["db"] is DbFamily
    assert registry.FAMILIES["fs"] is FsFamily
    assert registry.FAMILIES["s3"] is S3Family
    assert registry.all_names() == ["db", "fs", "s3"]


def test_the_registry_resolves_the_family() -> None:
    """The resolver's default input, in the order it was asked for."""
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.resolve(["db"])] == [DbFamily]
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.resolve(["fs", "s3", "db"])] == [
        FsFamily, S3Family, DbFamily,
    ]
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.registered_families()] == [
        FsFamily, S3Family, DbFamily,
    ]

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_families/test_fs.py
==============================================================================
"""The `fs` family — call shapes, literals, and what it ignores.

ADR-0021 §12 gives a family one job: read a module's AST once, report the
call sites that write into and read from a store it recognizes, and say
what literal each site names the store with. Everything else — identity,
confidence, nodes, edges — is `StoreResolver`'s and is pinned in
`tests/test_store_core/`. What is here is the family's half:

  - **the shapes** (S1–S4): `open` by mode, `Path(...).write_*` /
    `read_*`, `aiofiles.open` by mode, and `'r+'` as *both* roles;
  - **the literals** (L1–L4): a constant, the left side of a `+` or `/`,
    the part of an f-string before its first `{...}`, and `None` for
    everything else;
  - **the non-sites**: the ADR-0009 sinks (`os.remove`, `shutil.copy`,
    `shutil.move`, `os.listdir`, `Path.unlink`, ...), which are a
    different fact about a call and not this family's;
  - **the registration**: importing `aicorellator.store` is enough for
    the resolver to see `fs`.

The prefix signal itself (`confidence.literal_match`) is pinned where it
lives, in `tests/test_store_core/test_confidence.py`; this file pins
what the family *feeds* it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.store import registry
from aicorellator.store.families.base import Family, ReadSite, WriteSite
from aicorellator.store.families.db import DbFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.fs import FsFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.s3 import S3Family

HANDLER = "app/handler.py"


def _writes(source: str) -> list[WriteSite]:
    return FsFamily().detect_writes(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _reads(source: str) -> list[ReadSite]:
    return FsFamily().detect_reads(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _hints(sites: list) -> list[str | None]:
    return [site.identity_hint for site in sites]


# ============================================================
# The shapes (S1–S4)
# ============================================================

def test_open_in_a_write_mode_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """S1 — `open(path, 'wb')` is the canonical write."""
    sites = _writes("open('/uploads/x', 'wb')")
    assert _hints(sites) == ["/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.file_path for site in sites] == [HANDLER]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]


def test_open_in_a_read_mode_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """S1 — and `'rb'` is the same call pointing the other way."""
    sites = _reads("open('/uploads/x', 'rb')")
    assert _hints(sites) == ["/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]
    # A read's role is the context's business, and this family has none.
    assert [site.source_type for site in sites] == [None]


def test_the_mode_decides_the_direction() -> None:
    """S1 — the mode characters, one by one, on both sides.

    `w`, `a` and `x` make a write and nothing else — and they keep that
    direction when a `+` joins them (`'w+'` writes, it does not read).
    A mode with none of `w`, `a`, `x` makes a read and nothing else.
    Each mode is checked in *both* lists, because a site in the wrong
    one would pair a writer with a writer. A bare `+` and the `r+`
    family are the exception and have their own test.
    """
    for mode in ("w", "wb", "a", "ab", "x", "xb", "w+", "a+", "x+"):
        assert _writes(f"open('/uploads/x', '{mode}')"), mode
        assert _reads(f"open('/uploads/x', '{mode}')") == [], mode
    for mode in ("r", "rb", "rt", "br"):
        assert _reads(f"open('/uploads/x', '{mode}')"), mode
        assert _writes(f"open('/uploads/x', '{mode}')") == [], mode


def test_a_plus_mode_is_both_a_write_and_a_read() -> None:
    """S4 — `'r+'` asks for the other half, so one call site is two roles.

    The two roles are one call site, and a group is two components: the
    resolver pairs *sites*, so this site pairs with another one or not
    at all. The `r+` family is the case that matters — the `+` asks for
    the other half of an otherwise-read mode — and a bare `'+'` is both
    for the same reason. `'w+'` is not: `w` already decides it.
    """
    for mode in ("r+", "rb+", "r+b", "+"):
        source = f"open('/uploads/x', '{mode}')"
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["/uploads/x"], mode
        assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["/uploads/x"], mode


def test_an_absent_mode_is_a_read() -> None:
    """`'r'` is `open`'s default, so `open(path)` reads."""
    assert _hints(_reads("open('/uploads/x')")) == ["/uploads/x"]
    assert _writes("open('/uploads/x')") == []


def test_the_mode_may_be_a_keyword() -> None:
    """`mode=` is the argument's name; the rule does not read positions."""
    assert _writes("open('/uploads/x', mode='wb')")
    assert _reads("open('/uploads/x', mode='rb')")


def test_the_path_may_be_a_keyword() -> None:
    """`file=` too, and the hint is the same."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open(file='/uploads/x', mode='wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]


def test_a_mode_the_ast_cannot_read_is_no_site() -> None:
    """A variable mode is neither direction: the AST cannot say (§5).

    The same rule the sink extractor follows: a `writes_filesystem`
    capability needs a mode string, and a direction invented from a name
    would be a guess.
    """
    assert _writes("open('/uploads/x', mode)") == []
    assert _reads("open('/uploads/x', mode)") == []
    assert _writes("open('/uploads/x', f'{mode}')") == []


def test_path_write_methods_are_write_sites() -> None:
    """S2 — the name states the direction; the receiver holds the path."""
    sites = _writes("Path('/uploads/x').write_text(data)")
    assert _hints(sites) == ["/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]
    assert _hints(_writes("Path('/uploads/x').write_bytes(data)")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]


def test_path_read_methods_are_read_sites() -> None:
    """S2 — and the other two read."""
    assert _hints(_reads("Path('/uploads/x').read_text()")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]
    assert _hints(_reads("Path('/uploads/x').read_bytes()")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]


def test_pathlib_path_is_the_same_class() -> None:
    """`pathlib.Path('/x')` is `Path('/x')`, spelled out."""
    assert _writes("pathlib.Path('/uploads/x').write_text(data)")
    assert _reads("pathlib.Path('/uploads/x').read_text()")


def test_path_open_takes_its_mode_first() -> None:
    """`Path.open`'s path is the receiver's, its mode the first argument.

    The argument layout is the reason `_classify` has a branch per shape:
    `open`'s mode is its *second* argument and `Path.open`'s is its
    first, because the receiver already holds the path.
    """
    assert _writes("Path('/uploads/x').open('wb')")
    assert _reads("Path('/uploads/x').open('rb')")
    assert _reads("Path('/uploads/x').open()")
    assert _writes("Path('/uploads/x').open(mode='wb')")


def test_a_receiver_that_is_not_a_path_call_is_not_matched() -> None:
    """The receiver must be built from `Path(...)` — the stated limit.

    `p` is a `Name` and `client` is some other class entirely; neither
    is `pathlib.Path`, so neither is a site. The hint would be `None`
    for `p` and the call would be a false positive for `client`, and §5
    prefers the missing site to the invented one.
    """
    assert _writes("p.write_text(data)") == []
    assert _reads("p.read_text()") == []
    assert _writes("client.write_text(data)") == []
    assert _reads("client.read_text()") == []


def test_builtins_open_is_the_same_call() -> None:
    """`builtins.open` is `open`, spelled out; `os.open` is not (above)."""
    assert _hints(_writes("builtins.open('/uploads/x', 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]
    assert _hints(_reads("builtins.open('/uploads/x', 'rb')")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]


def test_a_path_division_names_the_directory_it_started_from() -> None:
    """`/` adds a segment to a directory; the directory is the hint."""
    assert _hints(_writes("(Path('/uploads') / 'x').write_text(data)")) == [
        "/uploads"
    ]
    assert _hints(
        _reads("(Path('/uploads') / name).read_text()")
    ) == ["/uploads"]


def test_aiofiles_open_is_matched_by_its_module() -> None:
    """S3 — `aiofiles.open(path, mode)`, the same mode rule."""
    assert _hints(_writes("aiofiles.open('/uploads/x', 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]
    assert _hints(_reads("aiofiles.open('/uploads/x', 'rb')")) == [
        "/uploads/x"
    ]


def test_an_aliased_aiofiles_is_a_known_false_negative() -> None:
    """`import aiofiles as aio` — the family follows dotted names only."""
    assert _writes("aio.open('/uploads/x', 'wb')") == []
    assert _reads("aio.open('/uploads/x', 'rb')") == []


# ============================================================
# The literals (L1–L4)
# ============================================================

def test_a_constant_is_the_whole_hint() -> None:
    """L1 — the file, exactly as written."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open('/uploads/report.txt', 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/report.txt"
    ]


def test_a_concatenation_names_its_prefix() -> None:
    """L2 — `'/uploads/' + name` names the directory, not the file.

    The right side is runtime data; the left side is the bucket the call
    writes into, and that is the identity a reader can be paired with.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("open('/uploads/' + name, 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/"
    ]
    assert _hints(_reads("open('/uploads/' + name, 'rb')")) == [
        "/uploads/"
    ]


def test_a_chain_of_concatenations_names_the_first_literal() -> None:
    """L2 — the left side is taken again, so the prefix is the head."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open('/uploads/' + kind + '/' + name, 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/"
    ]


def test_an_fstring_names_the_part_before_the_braces() -> None:
    """L3 — `f'/uploads/{name}'` names `'/uploads/'`."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open(f'/uploads/{name}', 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/"
    ]


def test_an_fstring_that_starts_with_a_brace_names_nothing() -> None:
    """L4 — there is no leading constant to take.

    The site is still a read or a write; it just names no store, and §5
    is what makes that "no store" rather than "any store".
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("open(f'{base}/{name}', 'wb')")) == [None]
    assert _hints(_reads("open(f'{base}/{name}', 'rb')")) == [None]


def test_a_name_names_nothing() -> None:
    """L4 — a parameter is a value the AST does not hold (§5).

    `open(path, 'wb')` is a write site with no hint; the resolver keeps
    it and lets the literal side decide the store.
    """
    sites = _writes("open(path, 'wb')")
    assert _hints(sites) == [None]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]


def test_an_attribute_names_nothing() -> None:
    """L4 — `settings.upload_dir` is resolved at runtime.

    The site is still a write — the call is `open` in a write mode — and
    the hint is `None`, which is §5's answer and not the absence of a
    site.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("open(settings.upload_dir, 'wb')")) == [None]


def test_a_call_names_nothing() -> None:
    """L4 — `os.path.join(...)` is a call, not a literal."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open(os.path.join(base, name), 'wb')")) == [None]


def test_a_percent_format_names_its_template() -> None:
    """Any expression built from a literal takes its left side.

    `'/uploads/%s' % name` is a `BinOp` like `+` and `/` are, so the
    template is the hint. It is not normalised into `'/uploads/'`: the
    family reports what the code says.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("open('/uploads/%s' % name, 'wb')")) == [
        "/uploads/%s"
    ]


def test_a_non_string_constant_names_nothing() -> None:
    """A bytes path is not a store identity this family can state."""
    assert _hints(_writes("open(b'/uploads/x', 'wb')")) == [None]


# ============================================================
# The non-sites — ADR-0009's sinks, and `os.open`
# ============================================================

def test_os_remove_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """A sink (`writes_filesystem`), and no data moves into a store."""
    assert _writes("os.remove('/uploads/x')") == []
    assert _reads("os.remove('/uploads/x')") == []


def test_shutil_copy_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """A sink on both sides: it reads a file and writes one."""
    assert _writes("shutil.copy(src, '/uploads/x')") == []
    assert _reads("shutil.copy(src, '/uploads/x')") == []


def test_shutil_move_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    assert _writes("shutil.move(src, '/uploads/x')") == []
    assert _reads("shutil.move(src, '/uploads/x')") == []


def test_os_listdir_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """Names, not content: a listing carries no data to pair."""
    assert _writes("os.listdir('/uploads')") == []
    assert _reads("os.listdir('/uploads')") == []


def test_path_unlink_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """`Path.unlink` deletes; nothing is written and nothing is read."""
    assert _writes("Path('/uploads/x').unlink()") == []
    assert _reads("Path('/uploads/x').unlink()") == []


def test_os_open_is_not_the_builtin() -> None:
    """`os.open` returns a file descriptor, and it is not `open`.

    The sink rules list it separately (`os.write`), and the store model
    has nothing to pair: the descriptor is not a path literal.
    """
    assert _writes("os.open('/uploads/x', os.O_WRONLY)") == []
    assert _reads("os.open('/uploads/x', os.O_RDONLY)") == []


def test_the_rest_of_the_sink_set_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """The other calls the brief names, in one place.

    `os.unlink`, `os.rmdir`, `os.rename`, `Path.rename`, `Path.iterdir`,
    `os.scandir`, `shutil.rmtree` and `shutil.copytree`: each is a sink
    or names no content, and none of them is a store operation.
    """
    calls = (
        "os.unlink('/uploads/x')",
        "os.rmdir('/uploads')",
        "os.rename(a, b)",
        "Path('/uploads').iterdir()",
        "os.scandir('/uploads')",
        "shutil.rmtree('/uploads')",
        "shutil.copytree(a, b)",
    )
    for call in calls:
        assert _writes(call) == [], call
        assert _reads(call) == [], call
    assert _writes("Path('/uploads/x').rename('/uploads/y')") == []


# ============================================================
# Order, and the interface
# ============================================================

def test_the_sites_come_back_in_source_order() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` is breadth-first; the family reports source order.

    The nested write is first in the file and *second* in the walk, so
    this pins the sort rather than the traversal.
    """
    source = "if flag:\n    open('/a', 'wb')\nopen('/b', 'wb')\n"
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["/a", "/b"]


def test_the_context_is_accepted_and_unused() -> None:
    """B.3b-user_upload is the first family with a context to read."""
    tree = ast.parse("open('/uploads/x', 'wb')")
    assert len(FsFamily().detect_writes(tree, HANDLER, context=None)) == 1
    assert len(
        FsFamily().detect_reads(ast.parse("open('/uploads/x', 'rb')"),
                                HANDLER, context=object())
    ) == 1


def test_the_family_declares_its_name() -> None:
    """The name is the registry key and half of a store's identity (§1)."""
    assert FsFamily.name == "fs"


def test_the_family_is_a_family() -> None:
    assert isinstance(FsFamily(), Family)


def test_importing_the_store_package_registers_the_family() -> None:
    """P1 — no caller names `fs`; the import is the registration.

    `tests/test_store_core/test_resolver.py` builds the resolver with an
    explicit family, so the registry is what this pins: the family the
    pipeline will find is the one this module defines.
    """
    assert registry.FAMILIES["fs"] is FsFamily
    # `s3` joined the tree in B.3b-s3 and `db` in B.3b-db; the three are
    # the families it ships.
    assert registry.all_names() == ["db", "fs", "s3"]


def test_the_registry_resolves_the_family() -> None:
    """The resolver's default input, in the order it was asked for."""
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.resolve(["fs"])] == [FsFamily]
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.registered_families()] == [
        FsFamily, S3Family, DbFamily,
    ]

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_families/test_s3.py
==============================================================================
"""The `s3` family — call shapes, literals, and what it ignores.

ADR-0021 §12 gives a family one job: read a module's AST once, report the
call sites that write into and read from a store it recognizes, and say
what literal each site names the store with. Everything else — identity,
confidence, nodes, edges — is `StoreResolver`'s and is pinned in
`tests/test_store_core/test_s3_resolver.py`. What is here is the family's
half:

  - **the shapes** (W1–W5, R1–R3): the three writers, the three readers,
    the receiver spellings that match, and the calls that are not sites;
  - **the handles** (H1–H6, B.3b-s3-followup): a receiver the file bound
    to `boto3.client` / `boto3.resource` / `S3FileSystem` / `Minio` is a
    site wherever the literal set would not have matched, resolved
    per scope, last assignment wins, no value followed;
  - **`s3fs`** (F1–F4): `handle.open('s3://<bucket>/<key>', mode)`, the
    mode deciding the direction the way the `fs` family's `open` does,
    the scheme stripped for the hint;
  - **MinIO** (M1–M5): `handle.put_object(bucket, key)` and the lowercase
    keyword spelling, told apart from boto3's by the argument layout and
    not by the receiver's name;
  - **the literals** (L1–L5): `Bucket` plus `Key`, a bucket with no key,
    `None` for an unresolved bucket, and the f-string prefix;
  - **the non-sites**: `head_object`, the enumeration and delete calls,
    the bucket-configuration calls and the constructor — different facts
    about a call, and not this family's;
  - **the registration**: importing `aicorellator.store` is enough for
    the resolver to see `s3`.

The prefix signal itself (`confidence.literal_match`) is pinned where it
lives, in `tests/test_store_core/test_confidence.py`; this file pins what
the family *feeds* it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast

from aicorellator.store import registry
from aicorellator.store.families.base import Family, ReadSite, WriteSite
from aicorellator.store.families.db import DbFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.fs import FsFamily
from aicorellator.store.families.s3 import S3Family

HANDLER = "app/handler.py"
BUCKET = "docs"
KEY = "uploads/x"


def _writes(source: str) -> list[WriteSite]:
    return S3Family().detect_writes(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _reads(source: str) -> list[ReadSite]:
    return S3Family().detect_reads(ast.parse(source), HANDLER)


def _hints(sites: list) -> list[str | None]:
    return [site.identity_hint for site in sites]


# ============================================================
# The write shapes (W1–W3)
# ============================================================

def test_put_object_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W1 — `Bucket` and `Key` by keyword, and `Body` ignored."""
    sites = _writes(
        f's3.put_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}", Body=payload)'
    )
    assert _hints(sites) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.file_path for site in sites] == [HANDLER]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]


def test_upload_file_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W2 — `Filename` is the local path, not the S3 key.

    The same store is named with either `Filename`, and with the
    positional spelling of the shape (`Filename, Bucket, Key`): the
    family reads `Bucket` and `Key` and nothing else.
    """
    for source in (
        's3.upload_file(Filename="local.bin", Bucket="docs", '
        'Key="uploads/x")',
        's3.upload_file(Filename="/tmp/other.bin", Bucket="docs", '
        'Key="uploads/x")',
        's3.upload_file("local.bin", "docs", "uploads/x")',
    ):
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"], source


def test_upload_fileobj_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """W3 — `(fileobj, bucket, key)`, positional or mixed."""
    for source in (
        "s3.upload_fileobj(fileobj, 'docs', 'uploads/x')",
        "s3.upload_fileobj(fileobj, Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


# ============================================================
# The read shapes (R1–R3)
# ============================================================

def test_get_object_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R1 — the read half of the `put_object` / `get_object` pair."""
    sites = _reads(f's3.get_object(Bucket="{BUCKET}", Key="{KEY}")')
    assert _hints(sites) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [1]
    # A read's role is the context's business, and this family has none.
    assert [site.source_type for site in sites] == [None]


def test_download_file_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R2 — the third positional is the local path, and it is ignored."""
    for source in (
        "s3.download_file('docs', 'uploads/x', '/tmp/local')",
        "s3.download_file('docs', 'uploads/x', '/tmp/other')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"], source
        assert _writes(source) == [], source


def test_download_fileobj_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """R3 — `(bucket, key, fileobj)`; the file object is not the store."""
    source = "s3.download_fileobj('docs', 'uploads/x', fileobj)"
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert _writes(source) == []


# ============================================================
# The direction comes from the name, and the receiver from the name
# ============================================================

def test_each_name_states_its_own_direction() -> None:
    """There is no mode argument: the method name *is* the direction.

    Each shape is checked in *both* lists, because a site in the wrong
    one would pair a writer with a writer. The arguments are the same
    on both sides, so only the name can decide.
    """
    writes = (
        "s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.upload_file(Filename='local', Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.upload_fileobj(fileobj, 'docs', 'uploads/x')",
    )
    reads = (
        "s3.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.download_file('docs', 'uploads/x', '/tmp/local')",
        "s3.download_fileobj('docs', 'uploads/x', fileobj)",
    )
    for source in writes:
        assert _writes(source), source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source
    for source in reads:
        assert _reads(source), source
        assert _writes(source) == [], source


def test_a_bare_call_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """W4 — no receiver, no store: the AST does not know the object.

    `put_object(...)` is a method on a name the family cannot resolve,
    and §5 prefers "no store" to a guessed one. `boto3.client('s3')` is
    where the handle comes from, and the handle is a variable: tracking
    it is dataflow and a separate step.
    """
    for source in (
        "put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_receiver_that_is_not_an_s3_name_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """W5 — the receiver set is the whole of what the AST can say.

    `obj.put_object(...)` is some other object's method, and a receiver
    that is an expression — `boto3.client('s3').put_object(...)` — is
    not a name at all. Both are the false negatives the module
    docstring lists.
    """
    for source in (
        "obj.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "store_client.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "boto3.client('s3').put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "session.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_receiver_spellings_that_match() -> None:
    """The conventional bindings for an `s3` handle, by last segment.

    The last segment is what counts, so `aws.s3` and `self.s3_client`
    match as well as the bare names: the receiver is read as a name,
    and the name's tail is the qualifier.
    """
    for receiver in (
        "s3", "s3_client", "client", "s3_resource", "resource",
        "self.s3_client", "aws.s3",
    ):
        source = f"{receiver}.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"], source


# ============================================================
# The literals (L1–L5)
# ============================================================

def test_the_bucket_and_the_key_are_one_hint() -> None:
    """L1 — `'docs'` and `'uploads/x'` name `'docs/uploads/x'`.

    Both sides of the store name it the same way, so a write and a read
    of one object carry one hint each and the resolver can pair them.
    """
    write = "s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    read = "s3.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    assert _hints(_writes(write)) == _hints(_reads(read)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_key_with_a_trailing_slash_keeps_it() -> None:
    """L2 — the key is spelled as written, and so is the hint.

    `'uploads/'` is the directory the call names, and the hint is the
    bucket plus it: nothing is appended beyond the one separator.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/')")) == [
        "docs/uploads/"
    ]


def test_a_bucket_with_no_key_names_the_bucket() -> None:
    """L3 — a call that names the bucket is a fact about that store.

    The key is the half that may be missing — the bucket is not — and
    the hint ends at the bucket plus the separator.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Body=payload)")) == [
        "docs/"
    ]
    assert _hints(_reads("s3.get_object(Bucket='docs')")) == ["docs/"]
    # A `Key` with no `Bucket` names nothing at all (§5).
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Key='uploads/x')")) == [None]


def test_an_unresolved_bucket_names_nothing() -> None:
    """L4 — a parameter, an attribute or a call is `None`, not a guess.

    §5 turns the `None` into "no store": the resolver has no literal to
    build one from, and a store invented from a variable would be a
    store nobody named.
    """
    for source in (
        "s3.put_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)",
        "s3.put_object(Bucket=bucket)",
        "s3.put_object(Bucket=settings.bucket, Key='uploads/x')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_writes(source)) == [None], source
    # The same on the read side: an unresolved half is `None` there too.
    for source in (
        "s3.get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.get_object(Bucket=get_bucket(), Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.download_file(bucket, 'uploads/x', '/tmp/local')",
    ):
        assert _hints(_reads(source)) == [None], source
        assert _writes(source) == [], source


def test_an_fstring_key_contributes_its_prefix() -> None:
    """L5 — the constant part before the first `{...}` is the hint.

    `f'uploads/{name}'` names the `'uploads/'` prefix, so the store is
    the bucket plus it; `f'{base}/x'` starts with the placeholder and
    names nothing, which leaves the bucket alone (`'docs/'`).
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key=f'uploads/{n}')")
    ) == ["docs/uploads/"]
    assert _hints(
        _writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key=f'{base}/x')")
    ) == ["docs/"]
    # The left side of a `+` is the same rule, as for `fs`.
    assert _hints(
        _writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/' + n)")
    ) == ["docs/uploads/"]


def test_a_bucket_trailing_slash_is_not_normalised() -> None:
    """The two spellings of a bucket stay two hints.

    S3 bucket names carry no trailing slash in the API, and the family
    invents none and removes none: `'docs/'` and `'docs'` are compared
    as written, so `Bucket='docs/', Key='uploads/'` names
    `'docs//uploads/'` and `Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/'` names
    `'docs/uploads/'`. `confidence.literal_match` would relate them on
    containment; the resolver attaches only on equality (B.3b-fs-
    followup), and that is pinned in `tests/test_store_core/
    test_s3_resolver.py`.
    """
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs/', Key='uploads/')")) \
        == ["docs//uploads/"]
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/')")) \
        == ["docs/uploads/"]
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs/')")) == ["docs//"]


# ============================================================
# Not in `s3` (N1–N5)
# ============================================================

def test_head_object_is_not_a_store_site() -> None:
    """N1 — metadata is not content, and there is nothing to pair."""
    source = "s3.head_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_the_enumeration_calls_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """N2 — a listing carries names, not data."""
    for source in (
        "s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket='docs', Prefix='uploads/')",
        "s3.list_objects(Bucket='docs')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_delete_calls_are_not_store_writes() -> None:
    """N3 — a deletion is destructive; nothing is written into a store."""
    for source in (
        "s3.delete_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')",
        "s3.delete_objects(Bucket='docs', Delete=payload)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_bucket_configuration_calls_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """N4 — a bucket's policy, ACL and versioning are not data."""
    for source in (
        "s3.put_bucket_policy(Bucket='docs', Policy=policy)",
        "s3.put_bucket_acl(Bucket='docs', ACL='private')",
        "s3.put_bucket_versioning(Bucket='docs', VersioningConfiguration=c)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_constructor_is_not_a_call_site() -> None:
    """N5 — a handle is a variable, and the family reads names only."""
    for source in (
        "boto3.client('s3')",
        "boto3.resource('s3')",
        "s3 = boto3.client('s3')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_the_other_s3_spellings_are_not_this_family() -> None:
    """`s3fs`, MinIO and `open('s3://...')` name no store *unbound*.

    Before B.3b-s3-followup this was "not this family at all"; the three
    are shapes here now, and the pins stay because each of these three
    calls still names nothing, for the followup's reason rather than
    this step's:

      - `s3fs.S3FileSystem().open(...)` has a *call* for a receiver, and
        the handle rule resolves a name a constructor bound;
      - `minio_client.put_object(...)` has no handle and is not a literal
        receiver, so the receiver names nothing;
      - `open('s3://docs/x')` is the `fs` family's site — it names a
        path, and it is `fs` that reports it.

    The three near-misses are pinned below, one per shape:
    `test_a_direct_s3fs_handle_is_not_resolved`,
    `test_a_minio_call_with_no_handle_is_not_a_site` and
    `test_a_bare_open_is_not_an_s3fs_site`.
    """
    for source in (
        "s3fs.S3FileSystem().open('docs/uploads/x')",
        "minio_client.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x', fileobj)",
        "open('s3://docs/uploads/x', 'wb')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


# ============================================================
# Handle tracking (B.3b-s3-followup, H1–H6)
#
# Dataflow-lite, not dataflow: **one assignment per name per scope**
# whose value is a constructor call, resolved by name. ADR-0001 forbids
# following values through calls, and nothing here does — the family
# never asks what the handle holds, only whether the receiver name is
# one a constructor in the file bound.
# ============================================================

def test_a_client_handle_is_tracked() -> None:
    """H1 — `s3_client = boto3.client('s3')` names a handle.

    The receiver is a name the literal set does not carry, so before
    this step the call was invisible. The handle is the constructor's
    return value, and the assignment is the whole of what the family
    reads: no value is followed, one `Name = Call` is resolved.
    """
    source = (
        "s3_client = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "s3_client.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x', Body=payload)"
    )
    sites = _writes(source)
    assert _hints(sites) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [2]
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_resource_handle_is_tracked() -> None:
    """H2 — `boto3.resource` binds a handle the same way."""
    source = (
        "s3_resource = boto3.resource('s3')\n"
        "s3_resource.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_a_handle_in_another_function_is_not_followed() -> None:
    """H3 — the scope rule: same file is not same scope.

    The handle is assigned in `make` and used in `handle`. Resolving
    that is a call graph (which function runs first, whether `make` ran
    at all), and the family does not build one — the assignment is
    resolved per *scope*, and `c` is not in `handle`'s. A false
    negative, stated and pinned.
    """
    source = (
        "def make():\n"
        "    c = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "def handle():\n"
        "    c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')\n"
    )
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_module_level_handle_is_followed_from_a_function() -> None:
    """And the other half of the scope rule: module level is visible.

    A module-level handle is bound for the whole file, so a call site
    inside any function of that file may use it.
    """
    source = (
        "c = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "def handle():\n"
        "    c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')\n"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_handle_in_the_same_function_is_followed() -> None:
    """A function-local handle used in its own function is a site."""
    source = (
        "def handle(payload):\n"
        "    c = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "    c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x', Body=payload)\n"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_reassigned_handle_takes_the_last_assignment() -> None:
    """H4 — two assignments to one name: the last in source order wins.

    Both directions, because the rule is about the assignment's
    *position* and not about which constructor appeared. `last` is the
    honest answer — the AST cannot know which branch ran, and the last
    statement is the one the reader would see the call follow.
    """
    rebuilt = (
        "c = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "c = get_client()\n"
        "c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')\n"
    )
    assert _writes(rebuilt) == []

    bound = (
        "c = get_client()\n"
        "c = boto3.client('s3')\n"
        "c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')\n"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(bound)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_handle_from_a_factory_is_not_tracked() -> None:
    """H5 — `client = get_client()` is not a handle: no value following.

    The value is a call, and the call's target is `get_client`, not a
    constructor. Following what it *returns* is dataflow, which
    ADR-0001 forbids; the handle rule reads the assignment, not the
    value. A false negative, stated and pinned.
    """
    for source in (
        "c = get_client()\nc.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='x')",
        "c = session.client('s3')\nc.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='x')",
        "c = boto3.client\nc.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='x')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source


def test_the_service_argument_is_not_checked() -> None:
    """The `('s3')` literal is not read — a documented false positive.

    `boto3.client('ec2')` binds a handle the same way `boto3.client
    ('s3')` does, and the family accepts it: the receiver is a handle,
    and which service it talks to is a future step's business. Nothing
    in the call is read but the target of the constructor.
    """
    source = (
        "c = boto3.client('ec2')\n"
        "c.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_the_literal_receiver_rule_still_stands() -> None:
    """The two receiver rules coexist: the sets are additive.

    `client` is a literal receiver whatever it holds (B.3b-s3), so a
    `client` bound to something that is not a constructor is still a
    site. The handle set only *adds* names the literal set does not
    carry; it never subtracts one.
    """
    source = (
        "client = some_factory()\n"
        "client.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_the_boto3_layout_is_keyword_only() -> None:
    """H6 — positional arguments are not boto3's shape.

    Every boto3 method takes `**kwargs`; `put_object('docs', 'x')` is
    not a call that names a store, on a handle or on a literal receiver
    alike. The shapes with a documented positional layout
    (`upload_fileobj(fileobj, bucket, key)`) keep it — that is a
    different shape, and the table says so.
    """
    for receiver in ("c", "s3_client", "s3"):
        source = f"{receiver}.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x')"
        if receiver == "c":
            source = "c = boto3.client('s3')\n" + source
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source
    # The positional shapes are unaffected.
    assert _hints(_writes("s3.upload_fileobj(fileobj, 'docs', 'uploads/x')")) \
        == ["docs/uploads/x"]




# ============================================================
# `s3fs` (F1–F4)
# ============================================================

def test_an_s3fs_handle_open_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """F1 — the handle is the `S3FileSystem` call's return value.

    The mode decides the direction the way the `fs` family's `open`
    does, and the path names the store: `s3://<bucket>/<key>`, with the
    scheme stripped, is the same hint a boto3 `Bucket` / `Key` pair
    gives.
    """
    source = (
        "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\n"
        "fs.open('s3://docs/uploads/x', 'wb')"
    )
    sites = _writes(source)
    assert _hints(sites) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [2]
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_an_s3fs_handle_open_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """F2 — `'rb'` is the read half of the same shape."""
    source = (
        "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\n"
        "fs.open('s3://docs/uploads/x', 'rb')"
    )
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_an_s3fs_open_reads_by_default() -> None:
    """No mode is `open`'s default, which is a read — the `fs` rule.

    `'r+'` is **both**, one call site claiming both roles; `'wb'` is a
    write only. The `'s3://'` path names the same store either way.
    """
