    assert _hints(
        _reads("fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open('s3://docs/x')")
    ) == ["docs/x"]
    both = "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open('s3://docs/x', 'r+')"
    assert _hints(_writes(both)) == ["docs/x"]
    assert _hints(_reads(both)) == ["docs/x"]


def test_an_s3fs_open_with_a_variable_path_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """F3 — no literal, no store (§5), and here not even a site.

    The `s3fs` shape needs the path to name the store: there is no
    separate bucket / key to fall back on, so a path the AST cannot read
    is `None`, and §5's "no store" is the whole answer.
    """
    for source in (
        "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open(path, 'wb')",
        "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open(path='s3://docs/x', mode=m)",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_bare_open_is_not_an_s3fs_site() -> None:
    """F4 — `open('s3://...')` is the `fs` family's site, not this one.

    The receiver has to be a tracked `s3fs` handle. A bare `open` is a
    builtin call on a name, and a name is not an attribute, so the
    family never sees it — it is `fs` that reports the path, and this
    family reports nothing.
    """
    for source in (
        "open('s3://docs/uploads/x', 'wb')",
        "pathlib.Path('/x').open('s3://docs/uploads/x', 'wb')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_filesystem_path_on_an_s3fs_handle_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """The path has to be an S3 URL; `/tmp/x` names a local file.

    An `s3fs` handle can be pointed at a local path (the library keeps
    the file-like API), and a filesystem path is not an S3 store: the
    `s3://` scheme is what makes the path the store's name, and without
    it there is nothing for this family to report.
    """
    source = "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open('/tmp/x', 'wb')"
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_direct_s3fs_handle_is_not_resolved() -> None:
    """A handle that is not *stored* is a false negative, documented.

    `s3fs.S3FileSystem().open(...)` has a call for a receiver, and the
    handle rule is about a name a constructor bound. Same for the class
    attribute spelling `s3fs.S3FileSystem.open(...)`.
    """
    for source in (
        "s3fs.S3FileSystem().open('s3://docs/x', 'wb')",
        "s3fs.S3FileSystem.open('s3://docs/x', 'wb')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_an_s3fs_path_with_no_key_names_the_bucket() -> None:
    """`'s3://docs/'` names `'docs/'` — the bucket, the prefix case.

    The scheme is stripped and nothing else is done to the path: no
    trailing slash is invented and none is removed, exactly as for a
    `Bucket` with no `Key`. `'s3://docs'` names `'docs'`, a different
    hint, and `confidence.literal_match` is what relates them.
    """
    assert _hints(
        _writes("fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open('s3://docs/', 'wb')")
    ) == ["docs/"]
    assert _hints(
        _writes("fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\nfs.open('s3://docs', 'wb')")
    ) == ["docs"]


def test_the_s3fs_path_can_be_passed_by_keyword() -> None:
    """`path=` and `mode=` are the same shape as the positional pair."""
    source = (
        "fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()\n"
        "fs.open(path='s3://docs/uploads/x', mode='wb')"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


# ============================================================
# MinIO (M1–M5)
# ============================================================

def test_a_minio_handle_put_object_is_a_write_site() -> None:
    """M1 — `Minio(...)` binds a handle; `bucket, key` are positional.

    The store is the same `bucket + "/" + key` a boto3 call names
    (`_identity_hint`): the two technologies spell the call differently
    and the store identity is one shape.
    """
    source = (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000', access_key='a', secret_key='s')\n"
        "mc.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x', fileobj)"
    )
    sites = _writes(source)
    assert _hints(sites) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert [site.line for site in sites] == [2]
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_minio_handle_get_object_is_a_read_site() -> None:
    """M2 — the read half, same positional layout."""
    source = (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.get_object('docs', 'uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _hints(_reads(source)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert _writes(source) == []


def test_a_minio_call_takes_lowercase_keywords() -> None:
    """M3 — `bucket=` / `key=` are MinIO's keyword spelling."""
    write = (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.put_object(bucket='docs', key='uploads/x')"
    )
    read = (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.get_object(bucket='docs', key='uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(write)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]
    assert _hints(_reads(read)) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_minio_handle_in_another_function_is_not_followed() -> None:
    """M4 — the scope rule, the same as for a boto3 handle."""
    source = (
        "def make():\n"
        "    mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "def handle():\n"
        "    mc.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x')\n"
    )
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_a_minio_call_with_boto3_keywords_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """M5 — `Bucket=` / `Key=` are boto3's shape, not MinIO's.

    The discriminator is the argument layout: the same method name on a
    MinIO handle with boto3's uppercase keywords names no store, exactly
    as a boto3 handle with positional arguments names none. The receiver
    is not what decides — the spelling is.
    """
    source = (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"
    )
    assert _writes(source) == []
    assert _reads(source) == []


def test_the_minio_presigned_calls_are_not_store_sites() -> None:
    """A URL is not content, and there is nothing to pair."""
    for source in (
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.presigned_url('get_object', 'docs', 'uploads/x')",
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.presigned_get_object('docs', 'uploads/x')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source


def test_a_minio_call_with_no_handle_is_not_a_site() -> None:
    """The receiver has to be a `Minio` handle, and `Minio` is a class.

    `minio_client` is not a literal receiver (`_RECEIVERS`) and is not a
    handle without an assignment, so the call names nothing. `minio(...)`
    spelled with the module's lowercase name is not the class either —
    the tail has to be `Minio` — a false negative, stated.
    """
    for source in (
        "minio_client.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x', fileobj)",
        "mc = minio('localhost:9000')\nmc.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x')",
        "mc = Minioclient('localhost:9000')\nmc.put_object('docs', 'x')",
    ):
        assert _writes(source) == [], source
        assert _reads(source) == [], source
    # `minio.Minio` is the real spelling — the module, then the class.
    assert _hints(
        _writes(
            "mc = minio.Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
            "mc.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x')"
        )
    ) == ["docs/uploads/x"]


def test_a_minio_handle_is_not_a_boto3_handle() -> None:
    """The three handle sets are separate — a name is a handle of one.

    A `Minio` handle does not make `upload_file` (a boto3-only shape) a
    site, and a boto3 handle does not make `mc`'s positional spelling a
    shape it takes.
    """
    assert _writes(
        "mc = Minio('localhost:9000')\n"
        "mc.upload_file('local.bin', 'docs', 'uploads/x')"
    ) == []
    assert _writes(
        "c = boto3.client('s3')\nc.put_object('docs', 'uploads/x')"
    ) == []


# ============================================================
# Order, and the interface
# ============================================================

def test_the_sites_come_back_in_source_order() -> None:
    """`ast.walk` is breadth-first; the family reports source order.

    The nested write is first in the file and *second* in the walk, so
    this pins the sort rather than the traversal.
    """
    source = (
        "if flag:\n"
        "    s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='a')\n"
        "s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='b')\n"
    )
    assert _hints(_writes(source)) == ["docs/a", "docs/b"]
    assert [site.line for site in _writes(source)] == [2, 3]


def test_two_runs_over_one_module_report_the_same_order() -> None:
    """The report is a function of the code, not of the traversal."""
    source = (
        "s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='a')\n"
        "s3.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='a')\n"
        "s3.upload_fileobj(fileobj, 'docs', 'b')\n"
    )
    first = [(site.line, site.identity_hint) for site in _writes(source)]
    second = [(site.line, site.identity_hint) for site in _writes(source)]
    assert first == second == [(1, "docs/a"), (3, "docs/b")]


def test_the_context_is_accepted_and_unused() -> None:
    """B.3b-user_upload is the first family with a context to read."""
    tree = ast.parse("s3.put_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')")
    assert len(S3Family().detect_writes(tree, HANDLER, context=None)) == 1
    assert len(
        S3Family().detect_reads(
            ast.parse("s3.get_object(Bucket='docs', Key='uploads/x')"),
            HANDLER, context=object(),
        )
    ) == 1


def test_the_family_declares_its_name() -> None:
    """The name is the registry key and half of a store's identity (§1)."""
    assert S3Family.name == "s3"


def test_the_family_is_a_family() -> None:
    assert isinstance(S3Family(), Family)


def test_importing_the_store_package_registers_the_family() -> None:
    """No caller names `s3`; the import of the package is the registration.

    `tests/test_store_core/test_s3_resolver.py` builds the resolver with
    an explicit family, so the registry is what this pins: the family
    the pipeline will find is the one this module imports.
    """
    assert registry.FAMILIES["s3"] is S3Family
    assert registry.FAMILIES["fs"] is FsFamily
    # `db` joined the tree in B.3b-db; the three are what it ships.
    assert registry.all_names() == ["db", "fs", "s3"]


def test_the_registry_resolves_the_family() -> None:
    """The resolver's default input, in the order it was asked for."""
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.resolve(["s3"])] == [S3Family]
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.resolve(["fs", "s3"])] == [
        FsFamily, S3Family,
    ]
    assert [type(f) for f in registry.registered_families()] == [
        FsFamily, S3Family, DbFamily,
    ]

"""Tests for the store-identity LLM fallback (B.3b-llm-fallback)."""

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/conftest.py

"""Shared builders for the store-identity fallback tests (B.3b-llm-fallback).

Four things every test in this package needs, and none of them should
build by hand:

  - `answer(...)` — a well-formed assistant message. The fallback's input
    is JSON text, so the tests speak JSON text.
  - `FakeLLM` — a scripted `llm_call`, consumed in call order (D.2's, so
    the tests read the same way as the classifier's).
  - `write_site` / `read_site` — a `FamilySite` whose `call_site` is a
    real `ast.Call`, because the prompt's call shape is `ast.unparse`'d
    from it.
  - `case(...)` — a whole runner input set: files on disk (the runner
    parses them for the code window), a delta with the nodes the two ends
    resolve against, upload sites for the scope rule, a config file and a
    cache path, plus a `run()` that fills in a policy.

No test in this package touches the network: `llm_call` is always
injected, and the one test that exercises the HTTP path monkeypatches
`requests.post`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from aicorellator.graph.models import Node
from aicorellator.ingestion.discovery import FileEntry, FileManifest
from aicorellator.ingestion.target import Target
from aicorellator.parsing.ast_normalizer import GraphDelta
from aicorellator.parsing.entry_points import EntryPointOutput
from aicorellator.parsing.models import TSAOutput
from aicorellator.parsing.normalizer_context import make_context
from aicorellator.scan_config import default_scan_config
from aicorellator.store.context.upload.base import UploadSite
from aicorellator.store.families.base import ReadSite, WriteSite
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import FamilySite, run
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback.cache import FallbackCache


CONFIG_YAML = """\
llm_fallback_model:
  base_url: "http://localhost:1234/v1"
  model: "test/model"
  temperature: 0.0
  max_tokens: 400
  timeout: 120
"""


def answer(hint: str | None, confidence: float = 0.8) -> str:
    """A well-formed assistant message naming (or refusing to name) a store."""
    return json.dumps({
        "identity_hint": hint,
        "confidence": confidence,
        "reasoning": f"the code says {hint!r}",
    })


class FakeLLM:
    """A scripted `llm_call`, consumed in call order.

    `None` entries stand for "no answer" (a timeout, a refused format), and
    an `Exception` entry is raised, so the failure paths are as easy to
    script as the happy one.
    """

    def __init__(self, *responses: str | None | Exception) -> None:
        self.responses: list[str | None | Exception] = list(responses)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def __call__(self, system: str, user: str) -> str | None:
        self.calls.append((system, user))
        if not self.responses:
            return None
        response = self.responses.pop(0)
        if isinstance(response, Exception):
            raise response
        return response


def _call(source: str) -> ast.Call:
    """The first `ast.Call` in `source`, for a site's `call_site`."""
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            return node
    raise AssertionError(f"no call in {source!r}")


def write_site(
    *,
    file_path: str = "app/upload.py",
    line: int = 3,
    identity_hint: str | None = None,
    source: str = 'open(path, "wb")',
) -> FamilySite:
    """A `FamilySite` holding one write site (the `fs` family's shape)."""
    return FamilySite(
        family="fs",
        site=WriteSite(
            call_site=_call(source), file_path=file_path, line=line,
            identity_hint=identity_hint,
        ),
    )


def read_site(
    *,
    file_path: str = "app/upload.py",
    line: int = 5,
    identity_hint: str | None = None,
    source: str = 'open(path, "rb")',
) -> FamilySite:
    """A `FamilySite` holding one read site."""
    return FamilySite(
        family="fs",
        site=ReadSite(
            call_site=_call(source), file_path=file_path, line=line,
            identity_hint=identity_hint, source_type="user_upload",
        ),
    )


def upload(file_path: str = "app/upload.py") -> UploadSite:
    """One upload site, which is what puts a file in a writer's scope."""
    return UploadSite(
        entry_point=Node(
            id="entry_point:upload", kind="entry_point", name="POST /upload",
            host_id="localhost",
            attributes={"source_file": file_path, "handler": "handle"},
        ),
        file_path=file_path,
        line=1,
        framework="fastapi",
    )


@dataclass
class Case:
    """A runner input set, and a `run()` that supplies a policy."""

    ctx: object
    delta: GraphDelta
    config_path: Path
    cache_path: Path
    upload_sites: list[UploadSite] = field(default_factory=list)

    def stores(self) -> list[Node]:
        return [n for n in self.delta.nodes if n.kind == "store"]

    def edges(self, kind: str) -> list:
        return [e for e in self.delta.edges if e.kind == kind]

    def run(
        self,
        sites,
        *,
        mode: str = "auto",
        llm_call=None,
        upload_sites=None,
        imports_by_file=None,
        config_path=None,
        cache_path=None,
    ):
        """Run the fallback with a policy built from `mode`.

        Returns `(stores, edges)`. The delta is not touched: the caller
        merges, the way the stage does.
        """
        policy = default_scan_config()
        policy.llm_fallback.mode = mode
        return run(
            sites=sites,
            delta=self.delta,
            upload_sites=(
                self.upload_sites if upload_sites is None else upload_sites
            ),
            imports_by_file=(
                {} if imports_by_file is None else imports_by_file
            ),
            ctx=self.ctx,
            scan=policy,
            config_path=(
                self.config_path if config_path is None else config_path
            ),
            cache_path=self.cache_path if cache_path is None else cache_path,
            llm_call=llm_call,
        )


@pytest.fixture
def memory_cache():
    """A fallback cache in memory, closed after the test."""
    cache = FallbackCache(":memory:")
    yield cache
    cache.close()


@pytest.fixture
def case(tmp_path: Path):
    """Build a `Case`: files on disk, a delta, upload sites, a config."""

    def build(
        files: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        nodes: list[Node] | None = None,
        upload_sites: list[UploadSite] | None = None,
        config: str | None = CONFIG_YAML,
        cache: Path | None = None,
    ) -> Case:
        root = tmp_path / "target"
        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        manifest = FileManifest(target=Target(root=root, kind="folder"))
        for index, (path, source) in enumerate((files or {}).items()):
            abs_path = root / path
            abs_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            abs_path.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
            manifest.files.append(FileEntry(
                path=path,
                abs_path=abs_path,
                language="python",
                content_hash=f"h{index}",
                size=len(source),
            ))

        config_path = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
        if config is not None:
            config_path.write_text(config, encoding="utf-8")

        ctx = make_context(
            manifest, TSAOutput(), entry_points=EntryPointOutput(),
        )
        return Case(
            ctx=ctx,
            delta=GraphDelta(nodes=list(nodes or [])),
            config_path=config_path,
            cache_path=cache or (
                tmp_path / "cache" / "llm_classifier.sqlite3"
            ),
            upload_sites=list(upload_sites or []),
        )

    return build

"""The cache's key, and its file (ADR-0023 §4, C1).

The key is the whole point: `(content_hash, prompt_version, model_id)` is
the layer's reproducibility guarantee, and each part gets a test that
changing it alone invalidates the answer. The file is the other half of
C1: **D.2's**, shared, with the `prompt_version` as the discriminator.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

from aicorellator.parsing.llm_classifier import (
    PROMPT_VERSION as CLASSIFIER_VERSION,
)
from aicorellator.parsing.llm_classifier.cache import (
    CACHE_FILENAME,
    ClassifierCache,
)
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import PROMPT_VERSION
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback.cache import (
    CachedIdentity,
    FallbackCache,
    content_hash,
    identity_hash,
)


KEY = ("abc123", PROMPT_VERSION, "test/model")


def test_the_file_is_d2s(tmp_path) -> None:
    """C1 — one file, one cleanup: `--clean` deletes `cache/`."""
    path = tmp_path / "cache" / CACHE_FILENAME
    with FallbackCache(path) as cache:
        cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
    assert path.exists()
    assert path.name == "llm_classifier.sqlite3"


def test_the_two_caches_share_a_file_without_colliding(tmp_path) -> None:
    """C1 — same file, same content hash, different `prompt_version`."""
    path = tmp_path / "cache" / CACHE_FILENAME
    with ClassifierCache(path) as classifier:
        classifier.put(
            KEY[0], CLASSIFIER_VERSION, KEY[2],
            kind="tool", capabilities=["reads_filesystem"],
        )
    with FallbackCache(path) as fallback:
        assert fallback.get(KEY[0], CLASSIFIER_VERSION, KEY[2]) is None
        fallback.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.8)

    with ClassifierCache(path) as classifier:
        assert classifier.get(
            KEY[0], CLASSIFIER_VERSION, KEY[2],
        ).kind == "tool"
        assert classifier.get(*KEY) is None
    with FallbackCache(path) as fallback:
        assert fallback.get(*KEY) == CachedIdentity("docs", 0.8, "")


def test_miss_then_hit_round_trips(memory_cache: FallbackCache) -> None:
    assert memory_cache.get(*KEY) is None

    memory_cache.put(
        *KEY, identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.9, reasoning="why",
    )
    hit = memory_cache.get(*KEY)

    assert hit == CachedIdentity(
        identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.9, reasoning="why",
    )
    assert memory_cache.count() == 1


def test_a_null_hint_is_a_hit(memory_cache: FallbackCache) -> None:
    """"The code names no store" is an answer, and it is worth keeping."""
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint=None, confidence=0.0)
    assert memory_cache.get(*KEY) == CachedIdentity(None, 0.0, "")


def test_changing_the_prompt_version_is_a_miss(
    memory_cache: FallbackCache,
) -> None:
    """Editing the prompt without bumping the version is the guarded bug."""
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
    assert memory_cache.get(KEY[0], "store_identity:v2.0.0", KEY[2]) is None


def test_changing_the_model_is_a_miss(memory_cache: FallbackCache) -> None:
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
    assert memory_cache.get(KEY[0], KEY[1], "other/model") is None


def test_changing_the_content_is_a_miss(memory_cache: FallbackCache) -> None:
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
    assert memory_cache.get("different", KEY[1], KEY[2]) is None


def test_put_replaces_the_same_key(memory_cache: FallbackCache) -> None:
    """One row per key: a re-run overwrites, it does not accumulate."""
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
    memory_cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="uploads")

    assert memory_cache.count() == 1
    assert memory_cache.get(*KEY).identity_hint == "uploads"


def test_the_parent_directory_is_created(tmp_path) -> None:
    """The runner passes a path under `cache/`; it may not exist yet."""
    path = tmp_path / "deep" / "cache" / CACHE_FILENAME
    with FallbackCache(path):
        assert path.exists()


def test_context_manager_closes(tmp_path) -> None:
    with FallbackCache(tmp_path / "x.sqlite3") as cache:
        cache.put(*KEY, identity_hint="docs")
        assert cache.count() == 1


def test_the_table_is_its_own(tmp_path) -> None:
    """D.2's row shape is a classification; a store identity is not one."""
    path = tmp_path / "x.sqlite3"
    with FallbackCache(path):
        pass
    raw = sqlite3.connect(path)
    tables = {
        row[0] for row in raw.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'"
        )
    }
    raw.close()
    assert "llm_store_identities" in tables
    assert "llm_classifications" not in tables


def test_identity_hash_covers_every_prompt_input() -> None:
    """Call shape, window, file path and imports are all in the identity."""
    base = identity_hash("open", "def f(): pass", "a.py", [])
    assert base != identity_hash("s3.put_object", "def f(): pass", "a.py", [])
    assert base != identity_hash("open", "def g(): pass", "a.py", [])
    assert base != identity_hash("open", "def f(): pass", "b.py", [])
    assert base != identity_hash("open", "def f(): pass", "a.py", ["os"])


def test_the_hash_function_is_d2s() -> None:
    """Reused, not restated: the separator discipline lives in one place."""
    assert identity_hash("c", "w", "f.py", ["os"]) == content_hash(
        "c\nw", "f.py", ["os"],
    )


def test_identity_hash_is_stable() -> None:
    """Same inputs, same key — across processes, so not a salted hash."""
    assert identity_hash("open", "w", "f.py", ["os"]) == identity_hash(
        "open", "w", "f.py", ["os"],
    )

"""The `llm_fallback_model` section (ADR-0023 §2).

One section, its own loader, its own error — D.2's shape, for the same
reason: a model you did not configure is worse than one that refuses to
load, and the caller must be able to tell which section it got wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import (
    FallbackConfig,
    FallbackConfigError,
    default_fallback_config,
    load_fallback_config,
)


FULL = """\
llm_fallback_model:
  base_url: "http://localhost:9999/v1"
  model: "test/fallback"
  temperature: 0.6
  max_tokens: 100
  timeout: 30
  response_format: "object"
"""


def _write(tmp_path: Path, text: str) -> Path:
    path = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def test_defaults_match_the_template() -> None:
    config = default_fallback_config()
    assert config == FallbackConfig()
    assert config.temperature == 0.0
    assert config.max_tokens == 400
    assert config.timeout == 120
    assert config.response_format == "schema"


def test_valid_load(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, FULL))
    assert config == FallbackConfig(
        base_url="http://localhost:9999/v1",
        model="test/fallback",
        temperature=0.6,
        max_tokens=100,
        timeout=30,
        response_format="object",
    )


def test_missing_keys_take_the_defaults(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = load_fallback_config(_write(
        tmp_path, 'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "test/model"\n',
    ))
    assert config.base_url == FallbackConfig().base_url
    assert config.temperature == 0.0
    assert config.response_format == "schema"


def test_a_missing_section_is_an_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """The mode asked for the layer; the model is not optional."""
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="llm_fallback_model"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, "detectors:\n  enabled: []\n"))


def test_an_empty_file_is_an_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="llm_fallback_model"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, ""))


def test_a_missing_file_is_an_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="cannot read"):
        load_fallback_config(tmp_path / "missing.yaml")


def test_malformed_yaml_is_an_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="invalid YAML"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, "llm_fallback_model: [\n"))


def test_a_non_mapping_section_is_an_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="must be a mapping"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, "llm_fallback_model: 7\n"))


def test_the_root_must_be_a_mapping(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="root must be a mapping"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, "- a\n"))


def test_the_model_is_required(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="model"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(
            tmp_path, 'llm_fallback_model:\n  temperature: 0.0\n',
        ))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "model",
    [
        "nomic-embed-text",
        "text-embedding-3-small",
        "bge-reranker-v2",
        "whisper-large",
    ],
)
def test_a_non_chat_model_is_rejected(tmp_path: Path, model: str) -> None:
    """`EXCLUDED_MODEL_SUBSTRINGS` — the ensemble loader's own rule."""
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="non-chat"):
        load_fallback_config(_write(
            tmp_path, f'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "{model}"\n',
        ))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("content", "where"),
    [
        ('llm_fallback_model:\n  model: ""\n', "model"),
        ('llm_fallback_model:\n  model: 7\n', "model"),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  base_url: 7\n',
            "base_url",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  temperature: "hot"\n',
            "temperature",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  temperature: true\n',
            "temperature",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  max_tokens: 0\n',
            "max_tokens",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  max_tokens: 1.5\n',
            "max_tokens",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  timeout: -1\n',
            "timeout",
        ),
        (
            'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  response_format: "yaml"\n',
            "response_format",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_a_documented_key_with_the_wrong_type_is_an_error(
    tmp_path: Path, content: str, where: str,
) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match=where):
        load_fallback_config(_write(tmp_path, content))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["schema", "object", "none"])
def test_documented_response_formats_load(
    tmp_path: Path, value: str,
) -> None:
    config = load_fallback_config(_write(
        tmp_path,
        f'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n'
        f'  response_format: "{value}"\n',
    ))
    assert config.response_format == value


def test_unknown_keys_are_ignored(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """The config's rule everywhere else."""
    config = load_fallback_config(_write(
        tmp_path,
        'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "m"\n  seed: 3\n  n_ctx: 4096\n',
    ))
    assert config.model == "m"


def test_the_model_is_stripped(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = load_fallback_config(_write(
        tmp_path, 'llm_fallback_model:\n  model: "  m  "\n',
    ))
    assert config.model == "m"

FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/test_mode.py

"""The three modes, and the no-op `off` is (ADR-0023 §6, N1).

`off` → no call, no store, no edge, and the model section is never read.
`auto` → the call happens; a failure is a warning (tested in
`test_runner.py`, where the failure paths live). `required` → a failure is
a scan error.

The stage-level no-op — the delta the pipeline sees — is pinned in
`tests/test_normalizer_stages/test_store_resolver.py`, where the stage's
fixtures are.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import FallbackConfigError

from .conftest import FakeLLM, answer, upload, write_site
from .test_runner import HANDLER, SOURCE, WRITE_LINE, _case


def test_off_makes_no_call_and_returns_nothing(case) -> None:
    """N1 — the default. No request, no store, no edge."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="off", llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []


def test_off_never_reads_the_model_section(case) -> None:
    """A scan that does not call the layer must not need its config.

    No config file is written at all: `off` has to return before anything
    tries to load `llm_fallback_model` (D.2's rule for `mode: off`).
    """
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = _case(case, config=None)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="off", llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []


def test_off_does_not_open_the_cache(case) -> None:
    """No call, no rows: the cache is not written for a scan that is off."""
    built = _case(case)

    built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="off", llm_call=FakeLLM())

    assert not built.cache_path.exists()


def test_off_is_the_policys_default(case) -> None:
    """The layer is opt-in: `default_scan_config()` says `off`."""
    from aicorellator.scan_config import default_scan_config

    assert default_scan_config().llm_fallback.mode == "off"


def test_auto_is_what_calls_the_model(case) -> None:
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="auto", llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    assert len(stores) == 1
    assert len(edges) == 1


def test_required_is_satisfied_when_every_site_is_named(case) -> None:
    """`required` is a statement about the corpus, not a failure mode."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="required", llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert len(stores) == 1
    assert len(edges) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["auto", "required"])
def test_a_missing_model_section_is_an_error_when_the_layer_runs(
    case, mode: str,
) -> None:
    """Asking for a layer you have not configured is worse than not asking."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case, config="detectors:\n  enabled: []\n")

    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="llm_fallback_model"):
        built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode=mode, llm_call=fake)

    assert fake.calls == []


def test_a_missing_config_file_is_an_error_when_the_layer_runs(case) -> None:
    """No file is the same mistake as no section, one step earlier."""
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = _case(case, config=None)

    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="cannot read"):
        built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="auto", llm_call=fake)

    assert fake.calls == []


def test_the_error_comes_before_any_call_even_with_no_gap(case) -> None:
    """The section is read for the mode, not for the site that needs it."""
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = case(
        files={HANDLER: SOURCE},
        config="detectors:\n  enabled: []\n",
    )

    with pytest.raises(FallbackConfigError, match="llm_fallback_model"):
        built.run([], mode="auto", llm_call=fake)

    assert fake.calls == []


def test_off_with_no_upload_site_is_still_a_no_op(case) -> None:
    """Two ways to be a no-op, and they compose."""
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = case(files={HANDLER: SOURCE}, upload_sites=[])

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], mode="off", llm_call=fake,

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []


def test_a_scan_with_no_unresolved_site_is_a_no_op(case) -> None:

    built = case(
        files={HANDLER: SOURCE}, upload_sites=[upload()],
    )

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE, identity_hint="/uploads/")],

    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/test_parse_answer.py
==============================================================================
"""`parse_answer` — the whole contract, one function (ADR-0023 §3).

The two claims are checked against the schema the prompt advertised: a
JSON object, an `identity_hint` that is a string or `null`, a `confidence`
in 0.0–1.0. Anything else is None, and the caller turns None into "left
unresolved" and does not cache it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import StoreIdentity, parse_answer


def _text(**fields) -> str:
    return json.dumps(fields)


def test_a_valid_answer() -> None:
    answer = parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.9, reasoning="the docstring",
    ))
    assert answer == StoreIdentity("docs", 0.9, "the docstring")


def test_a_null_hint_is_valid() -> None:
    """The prompt's own "the code names no store" is an answer."""
    assert parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint=None, confidence=0.0, reasoning="nothing here",
    )) == StoreIdentity(None, 0.0, "nothing here")


def test_a_missing_confidence_is_zero() -> None:
    assert parse_answer(_text(identity_hint="docs")) == StoreIdentity("docs")


def test_a_missing_reasoning_is_empty() -> None:
    answer = parse_answer(_text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.5))
    assert answer == StoreIdentity("docs", 0.5, "")


def test_a_non_string_reasoning_is_dropped() -> None:
    answer = parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.5, reasoning=7,
    ))
    assert answer.reasoning == ""


def test_a_blank_hint_is_a_null_hint() -> None:
    """A name that is only whitespace names nothing."""
    assert parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint="   ", confidence=0.0,
    )) == StoreIdentity(None, 0.0, "")


def test_the_hint_is_stripped() -> None:
    assert parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint="  docs  ", confidence=0.5,
    )).identity_hint == "docs"


def test_the_confidence_may_be_an_integer() -> None:
    assert parse_answer(_text(
        identity_hint="docs", confidence=1,
    )).confidence == 1.0


def test_json_in_a_fence_is_parsed() -> None:
    """D.2's JSON extraction is reused, fences and prose included."""
    text = "```json\n" + _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=0.5) + "\n```"
    assert parse_answer(text).identity_hint == "docs"


def test_prose_around_the_json_is_parsed() -> None:
    text = "Here is the answer: " + _text(identity_hint="docs")
    assert parse_answer(text).identity_hint == "docs"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "not json at all",
        "{}",
        '{"confidence": 0.5}',
        "[]",
        "7",
        '"docs"',
        _text(identity_hint=7, confidence=0.5),
        _text(identity_hint=["docs"], confidence=0.5),
        _text(identity_hint={"name": "docs"}, confidence=0.5),
        _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence="high"),
        _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=True),
        _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=1.5),
        _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=-0.1),
        _text(identity_hint="docs", confidence=None),
    ],
)
def test_an_unusable_answer_is_none(text: str) -> None:
    assert parse_answer(text) is None


def test_the_kind_of_the_answer_is_the_hint_not_the_technology() -> None:
    """The schema has no family: an answer can be wrong, not inventive."""
    answer = parse_answer(_text(identity_hint="s3:docs", confidence=0.9))
    assert answer.identity_hint == "s3:docs"
    assert not hasattr(answer, "family")

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/test_prompt.py
==============================================================================
"""The prompt: its own version, its markers, its schema (ADR-0023 §3).

The prompt is a separate artifact from D.2's, and the three things that
make it one are pinned here: a `PROMPT_VERSION` of its own (so the two
prompts' cache entries never collide), the `[UNTRUSTED_DATA]` markers with
the rule that reads them, and a schema that allows `null`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from aicorellator.parsing.llm_classifier import (
    PROMPT_VERSION as CLASSIFIER_VERSION,
)
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import PROMPT_VERSION
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback.prompt import (
    FEW_SHOT,
    IDENTITY_SCHEMA,
    SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    build_user_prompt,
)


def test_the_version_is_its_own() -> None:
    """D.2's version and the fallback's are different keys on purpose."""
    assert PROMPT_VERSION == "store_identity:v1.0.0"
    assert PROMPT_VERSION != CLASSIFIER_VERSION


def test_the_system_prompt_names_the_markers_and_the_null_answer() -> None:
    assert "[UNTRUSTED_DATA]" in SYSTEM_PROMPT
    assert "[/UNTRUSTED_DATA]" in SYSTEM_PROMPT
    assert "data, not" in SYSTEM_PROMPT
    assert "`null`" in SYSTEM_PROMPT


def test_the_markers_wrap_every_few_shot_example() -> None:
    """The defence is in the examples too, not only in the target."""
    user = build_user_prompt("open", "def f(): pass", "a.py", [])
    opens = user.count("[UNTRUSTED_DATA]")
    closes = user.count("[/UNTRUSTED_DATA]")
    assert opens == closes == len(FEW_SHOT) + 1


def test_the_target_carries_the_four_inputs() -> None:
    user = build_user_prompt(
        "s3.put_object", "def upload(): pass", "app/routes.py",
        ["import boto3"],
    )
    assert "call: s3.put_object" in user
    assert "code:\ndef upload(): pass" in user
    assert "file: app/routes.py" in user
    assert "imports: ['import boto3']" in user


def test_every_few_shot_answer_matches_the_schema() -> None:
    for example in FEW_SHOT:
        answer = example["answer"]
        assert set(answer) == {"identity_hint", "confidence", "reasoning"}
        assert answer["identity_hint"] is None or isinstance(
            answer["identity_hint"], str
        )
        assert 0.0 <= answer["confidence"] <= 1.0


def test_the_schema_allows_a_null_hint() -> None:
    """A null hint is an answer, so the wire form has to admit it."""
    schema = IDENTITY_SCHEMA["json_schema"]["schema"]
    assert schema["properties"]["identity_hint"]["type"] == [
        "string", "null",
    ]
    assert schema["required"] == [
        "identity_hint", "confidence", "reasoning",
    ]
    assert schema["additionalProperties"] is False
    assert IDENTITY_SCHEMA["json_schema"]["name"] == "store_identity"


def test_the_schema_has_no_family_field() -> None:
    """The family comes from the site, never from the answer (ADR-0023 §3)."""
    schema = IDENTITY_SCHEMA["json_schema"]["schema"]
    assert "family" not in schema["properties"]

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/test_runner.py
==============================================================================
"""The runner: what it fills, what it refuses, and what it links (ADR-0023).

The tests go through `run` with real files on disk, because half of what
the runner does is read source: the call shape, the code window, the
imports. `llm_call` is always injected, so no test needs a server.

F1–F5 are the acceptance criteria's fill cases; the cache and the scope
filter are pinned beside them because they are what decides *whether* a
site is asked about at all.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

import pytest
import requests

from aicorellator.graph.models import Node
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback import FallbackCache, FallbackError
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback.prompt import IDENTITY_SCHEMA
from aicorellator.store.llm_fallback.runner import (
    IMPORT_LINES,
    WINDOW_LINES,
)
from aicorellator.store.resolver import store_node_id

from .conftest import FakeLLM, answer, read_site, upload, write_site


HANDLER = "app/upload.py"

# A handler whose store is named by its docstring and whose `open` has a
# parameter for a path: exactly the gap ADR-0023 §1 describes.
SOURCE = '''\
def handle(upload_dir, payload):
    """Store the uploaded file under /uploads/."""
    with open(upload_dir, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(payload)
    with open(upload_dir, "rb") as fh:
        return fh.read()
'''

WRITE_LINE = 3
READ_LINE = 5


def writer_node() -> Node:
    """The component the write site lives in, as the delta holds it."""
    return Node(
        id="tool:handle", kind="tool", name="handle", host_id="localhost",
        attributes={"source_file": HANDLER, "line_start": 1},
    )


def source_node() -> Node:
    """The `untrusted_source` the read site reads, at the read's line."""
    return Node(
        id="untrusted_source:read", kind="untrusted_source",
        name="user_upload:open", host_id="localhost",
        attributes={
            "source_file": HANDLER,
            "source_type": "user_upload",
            "line_start": READ_LINE,
        },
    )


def _case(case, **kwargs):
    """A case with the handler file, both nodes and an upload site."""
    return case(
        files={HANDLER: SOURCE},
        nodes=[writer_node(), source_node()],
        upload_sites=[upload()],
        **kwargs,
    )


# ============================================================
# F1 — a gap is filled
# ============================================================

def test_a_named_site_creates_the_store_and_its_edge(case) -> None:
    """F1 — one write site, one answer, one store and one `writes_to`."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/", 0.9))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert [n.name for n in stores] == ["fs:/uploads/"]
    assert stores[0].id == store_node_id("fs", "/uploads/")
    assert stores[0].kind == "store"
    assert stores[0].attributes == {
        "family": "fs",
        "identity_hint": "/uploads/",
        "identity_source": "llm",
    }

    assert len(edges) == 1
    edge = edges[0]
    assert edge.kind == "writes_to"
    assert edge.source_id == "tool:handle"
    assert edge.target_id == stores[0].id
    assert edge.flow_kind == "structural"
    assert edge.observed_by == ["ast"]
    assert edge.data_flow_confirmed is None
    assert edge.identity_confidence == 0.2
    assert edge.attributes == {
        "identity_source": "llm",
        "identity_confidence_llm": 0.9,
    }
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_a_read_site_links_the_store_to_its_source(case) -> None:
    """F1 — the read direction: `store → untrusted_source`."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run([read_site(line=READ_LINE)], llm_call=fake)

    assert [n.name for n in stores] == ["fs:/uploads/"]
    assert len(edges) == 1
    assert edges[0].kind == "reads_from"
    assert edges[0].source_id == stores[0].id
    assert edges[0].target_id == "untrusted_source:read"
    assert edges[0].identity_confidence == 0.2


def test_both_directions_share_one_store(case) -> None:
    """One hint, one store: two sites are one place (ADR-0021 §1)."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"), answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE), read_site(line=READ_LINE)],
        llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert len(stores) == 1
    by_kind = {e.kind: e for e in edges}
    assert set(by_kind) == {"writes_to", "reads_from"}
    assert by_kind["writes_to"].source_id == "tool:handle"
    assert by_kind["writes_to"].target_id == stores[0].id
    assert by_kind["reads_from"].source_id == stores[0].id
    assert by_kind["reads_from"].target_id == "untrusted_source:read"


def test_the_prompt_carries_the_site_and_the_window(case) -> None:
    """The model is asked about *this* call site and *this* code."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], llm_call=fake)

    system, user = fake.calls[0]
    assert "[UNTRUSTED_DATA]" in system
    assert "call: open" in user
    assert "upload_dir" in user
    assert f"file: {HANDLER}" in user


def test_a_site_reported_twice_is_asked_about_once(case) -> None:
    """Two families can report one call; the model is asked once."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE), write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)],
        llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    assert len(stores) == 1
    assert len(edges) == 1

def test_a_deterministic_site_is_not_sent(case) -> None:
    """F2 — the deterministic answer wins; the fallback fills gaps only."""
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE, identity_hint="/uploads/")],
        llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []


def test_a_site_outside_the_writers_scope_is_not_sent(case) -> None:
    """F3 — no upload site, no scope, no question (ADR-0022 §1)."""
    fake = FakeLLM()
    built = case(
        files={HANDLER: SOURCE},
        nodes=[writer_node(), source_node()],
        upload_sites=[],
    )

    stores, edges = built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], llm_call=fake)

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []


def test_a_file_the_writer_imports_is_in_scope(case) -> None:
    """The scope is the writer's file or a file it imports either way."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"))
    built = case(
        files={
            HANDLER: SOURCE,
            "app/storage.py": "def save(p):\n    return open(p, 'wb')\n",
        },
        nodes=[
            writer_node(),
            source_node(),
            Node(
                id="tool:save", kind="tool", name="save",
                host_id="localhost",
                attributes={"source_file": "app/storage.py", "line_start": 1},
            ),
        ],
        upload_sites=[upload()],
    )

    stores, _ = built.run(
        [write_site(file_path="app/storage.py", line=2)],
        llm_call=fake,
        imports_by_file={HANDLER: ["app.storage"]},
    )

    assert [n.name for n in stores] == ["fs:/uploads/"]


def test_a_file_out_of_scope_is_not_sent(case) -> None:
    """An unrelated module's unresolved site is not asked about."""
    fake = FakeLLM()

    )

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(file_path="app/other.py", line=2)], llm_call=fake,
    )

    assert fake.calls == []
    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []


# ============================================================
# F4/F5 — a gap that stays a gap
# ============================================================

def test_a_null_hint_is_no_store_and_no_edges(case, caplog) -> None:
    """F4 — "the code names no store" is an answer, and it is a warning."""
    fake = FakeLLM(answer(None, 0.0))
    built = _case(case)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        stores, edges = built.run(
            [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], llm_call=fake,
        )

    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []
    assert "stays unresolved" in caplog.text


def test_no_answer_is_no_store_and_no_edges(case, caplog) -> None:
    """A timeout is not an answer: nothing is created, nothing is cached."""
    fake = FakeLLM(None)
    built = _case(case)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        stores, edges = built.run(
            [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)], llm_call=fake,
        )

    assert stores == []
    assert edges == []
    assert "stays unresolved" in caplog.text
    with FallbackCache(built.cache_path) as cache:
        assert cache.count() == 0


def test_an_unusable_answer_is_a_warning_in_auto(case, caplog) -> None:
    """F5 (auto) — a malformed answer leaves the site unresolved."""
    fake = FakeLLM("not json at all")
    built = _case(case)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):

# ============================================================
# The HTTP path (the probe D.2 does, restated)
# ============================================================

class FakeResponse:
    """The parts of `requests.Response` this module reads."""

    def __init__(self, status_code: int = 200, payload=None, text: str = ""):
        self.status_code = status_code
        self._payload = payload
        self.text = text

    def json(self):
        if self._payload is None:
            raise ValueError("no json")
        return self._payload


def completion(text: str, model: str = "test/model") -> dict:
    """An OpenAI-compatible success body."""
    return {
        "model": model,
        "choices": [
            {"message": {"content": text}, "finish_reason": "stop"}
        ],
    }


@pytest.fixture
def posts(monkeypatch):
    """Capture `requests.post` calls and script the responses.

    Returns a list of `(url, payload, timeout)` tuples. Responses are
    consumed in call order; once the scripted ones run out, a 200 with a
    valid answer is returned.
    """

    def install(*responses):
        calls: list[tuple[str, dict, int]] = []
        queue = list(responses)

        def fake_post(url, json=None, headers=None, timeout=None):
            calls.append((url, json, timeout))
            if queue:
                return queue.pop(0)
            return FakeResponse(payload=completion(answer("/uploads/")))

        monkeypatch.setattr(requests, "post", fake_post)
        return calls

    return install


def test_the_request_body_carries_the_schema(case, posts) -> None:
    """Schema-constrained decoding is the reason for this wire format."""
    calls = posts()
    built = _case(case)

    built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)])

    url, payload, timeout = calls[0]
    assert url == "http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions"
    assert payload["model"] == "test/model"
    assert payload["response_format"] == IDENTITY_SCHEMA
    assert payload["temperature"] == 0.0
    assert payload["max_tokens"] == 400
    assert payload["stream"] is False
    assert [m["role"] for m in payload["messages"]] == ["system", "user"]
    assert timeout == 120


def test_a_400_steps_the_response_format_down(case, posts) -> None:
    """A server that rejects `json_schema` may accept `json_object`."""
    calls = posts(
        FakeResponse(400, text="unsupported response_format"),
        FakeResponse(payload=completion(answer("/uploads/"))),
    )
    built = _case(case)

    stores, _ = built.run([write_site(line=WRITE_LINE)])

    assert [call[1]["response_format"] for call in calls] == [
        IDENTITY_SCHEMA,
        {"type": "json_object"},
    ]
    assert [n.name for n in stores] == ["fs:/uploads/"]

==============================================================================
FILE: tests/test_store_llm_fallback/test_special_floor.py
==============================================================================
"""The special floor: `identity_source='llm'` is judged at 0.1 (W1/W2).

ADR-0021 §9's floor is 0.3, and ADR-0023 §5 makes the fallback's links the
one exception: a `writes_to` / `reads_from` pair that carries
`attributes["identity_source"] = "llm"` is judged against
`confidence.WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM` (0.1) instead. Without it the fallback's
0.2 links would be inert — no store, no edges, no group — and the whole
layer would be a no-op that costs a model call.

W1: a fallback store at 0.2 is **weak** — in the graph, out of the default
enumeration, `include_weak=True` to see it.
W2: a deterministic link at 0.2 is not given the special floor. That is
the pin that keeps the exception narrow.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from aicorellator import GraphStore
from aicorellator.graph import Edge, Node
from aicorellator.graph.query import WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR
from aicorellator.store.confidence import (
    LLM_IDENTITY_BASE,
    LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM,
)

from .conftest import FakeLLM, answer, read_site, write_site
from .test_runner import READ_LINE, WRITE_LINE, _case


# ============================================================
# The constants, and their order
# ============================================================

def test_the_three_numbers_are_in_order() -> None:
    """0.1 < 0.2 < 0.3: the floor lets the base through, §9 does not."""
    assert WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM < LLM_IDENTITY_BASE < WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR


def test_the_llm_floor_admits_the_llm_base() -> None:
    """The exception exists to keep the fallback from being inert."""
    assert LLM_IDENTITY_BASE >= WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM


# ============================================================
# A hand-built pair (W1/W2, without the runner)
# ============================================================

def _put(store: GraphStore, node_id: str, kind: str, name: str) -> str:
    store.nodes.upsert(Node(
        id=node_id, kind=kind, name=name, host_id="localhost",
    ))
    return node_id


def _link(
    store: GraphStore, edge_id: str, source: str, target: str,
) -> str:
    store.edges.upsert(Edge(
        id=edge_id, source_id=source, target_id=target,
        kind="has_access_to", host_id="localhost", flow_kind="control",
    ))
    return edge_id


def _pair(
    store: GraphStore,
    tag: str,
    *,
    write_confidence: float,
    read_confidence: float,
    identity_source: str | None,
) -> str:
    """One write chain into a store and one read chain out of it.

        entry → writer --writes_to--> store --reads_from--> source
        source → reader → sink

    `identity_source` is stamped on both links' attributes, which is what
    the join reads to pick its floor.
    """
    attributes = (
        {} if identity_source is None
        else {"identity_source": identity_source}
    )
    ids = {
        "entry": f"entry_point:{'e' * 15}{tag}",
        "writer": f"tool:{'w' * 15}{tag}",
        "store": f"store:{'d' * 15}{tag}",
        "source": f"untrusted_source:{'u' * 15}{tag}",
        "reader": f"tool:{'r' * 15}{tag}",
        "sink": f"sink:{'s' * 15}{tag}",
    }
    for name, kind in (
        ("entry", "entry_point"), ("writer", "tool"), ("store", "store"),
        ("source", "untrusted_source"), ("reader", "tool"), ("sink", "sink"),
    ):
        _put(store, ids[name], kind, f"{kind}:{tag}")
    _link(store, f"edge:{'1' * 15}{tag}", ids["entry"], ids["writer"])
    _link(store, f"edge:{'3' * 15}{tag}", ids["source"], ids["reader"])
    _link(store, f"edge:{'4' * 15}{tag}", ids["reader"], ids["sink"])
    store.edges.upsert(Edge(
        id=f"edge:{'2' * 15}{tag}", source_id=ids["writer"],
        target_id=ids["store"], kind="writes_to", host_id="localhost",
        flow_kind="structural", identity_confidence=write_confidence,
        attributes=dict(attributes),
    ))
    store.edges.upsert(Edge(
        id=f"edge:{'5' * 15}{tag}", source_id=ids["store"],
        target_id=ids["source"], kind="reads_from", host_id="localhost",
        flow_kind="structural", identity_confidence=read_confidence,
        attributes=dict(attributes),
    ))
    return ids["store"]


def test_w1_a_fallback_pair_at_0_2_is_a_weak_group(
    store: GraphStore,
) -> None:
    """W1 — 0.2 passes 0.1, so the store exists and the group is weak."""
    store_id = _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=LLM_IDENTITY_BASE,
        read_confidence=LLM_IDENTITY_BASE,
        identity_source=LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    )

    assert store.query.find_chain_groups() == []

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True)

    assert len(groups) == 1
    assert groups[0].store_id == store_id
    assert groups[0].store_confidence == LLM_IDENTITY_BASE
    assert groups[0].weak is True


def test_w1_one_llm_side_is_enough(store: GraphStore) -> None:
    """The pair is an LLM guess if either link says so."""
    _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=LLM_IDENTITY_BASE,
        read_confidence=0.9,
        identity_source=LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    )

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True)

    assert [g.store_confidence for g in groups] == [LLM_IDENTITY_BASE]


def test_w2_a_deterministic_pair_at_0_2_is_no_group(
    store: GraphStore,
) -> None:
    """W2 — §9's floor is unchanged for a link with no `identity_source`."""
    _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=0.2,
        read_confidence=0.2,
        identity_source=None,
    )

    assert store.query.find_chain_groups() == []
    assert store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True) == []


def test_w2_the_exception_follows_the_attribute(store: GraphStore) -> None:
    """At the same 0.2, the attribute is what decides."""
    store_id = _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=0.2,
        read_confidence=0.2,
        identity_source=LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    )

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True)

    assert [g.store_id for g in groups] == [store_id]


def test_a_fallback_pair_at_0_1_is_still_a_group(store: GraphStore) -> None:
    """§5's floor is inclusive: 0.1 is the bottom, not a rejection."""
    _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM,
        read_confidence=WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM,
        identity_source=LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    )

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True)

    assert [g.store_confidence for g in groups] == [WEAK_JOIN_FLOOR_LLM]


def test_a_fallback_pair_under_0_1_is_no_group(store: GraphStore) -> None:
    """Under the special floor there is still no link at all."""
    _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=0.05,
        read_confidence=0.05,
        identity_source=LLM_IDENTITY_SOURCE,
    )

    assert store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True) == []


def test_a_non_string_identity_source_is_a_deterministic_link(
    store: GraphStore,
) -> None:
    """A value nothing else understands is not the LLM's marker."""
    _pair(
        store, "a",
        write_confidence=0.2,
        read_confidence=0.2,
        identity_source=7,
    )

    assert store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True) == []


# ============================================================
# End to end: the runner's store, in a real graph (the pipeline)
# ============================================================

def test_the_fallback_store_makes_a_weak_group_end_to_end(
    case, store: GraphStore,
) -> None:
    """The pipeline case: the runner fills a gap, the group is weak.

    The fallback's own store and edges go into a graph that already holds
    the two chains — `entry → writer` and `source → reader → sink` — so
    the join has a write side and a read side to pair. Without the special
    floor the pair would be dropped at 0.2 and the graph would hold two
    stores' worth of nothing.
    """
    fake = FakeLLM(answer("/uploads/"), answer("/uploads/"))
    built = _case(case)

    stores, edges = built.run(
        [write_site(line=WRITE_LINE), read_site(line=READ_LINE)],
        llm_call=fake,
    )
    assert len(stores) == 1 and len(edges) == 2

    for node in [
        *built.delta.nodes,
        *stores,
        Node(
            id="entry_point:upload", kind="entry_point",
            name="POST /upload", host_id="localhost",
        ),
        Node(
            id="tool:read_uploads", kind="tool", name="read_uploads",
            host_id="localhost",
        ),
        Node(
            id="sink:shell", kind="sink", name="run_shell",
            host_id="localhost",
        ),
    ]:
        store.nodes.upsert(node)
    for edge in [
        *edges,
        Edge(
            id="edge:entry", source_id="entry_point:upload",
            target_id="tool:handle", kind="has_access_to",
            host_id="localhost", flow_kind="control",
        ),
        Edge(
            id="edge:reader", source_id="untrusted_source:read",
            target_id="tool:read_uploads", kind="has_access_to",
            host_id="localhost", flow_kind="control",
        ),
        Edge(
            id="edge:sink", source_id="tool:read_uploads",
            target_id="sink:shell", kind="has_access_to",
            host_id="localhost", flow_kind="control",
        ),
    ]:
        store.edges.upsert(edge)

    assert store.query.find_chain_groups() == []

    groups = store.query.find_chain_groups(include_weak=True)

    assert len(groups) == 1
    assert groups[0].store_id == stores[0].id
    assert groups[0].store_name == "fs:/uploads/"
    assert groups[0].store_confidence == LLM_IDENTITY_BASE
    assert groups[0].weak is True
    assert groups[0].write_chains == [
        ["entry_point:upload", "tool:handle", stores[0].id]
    ]
    assert groups[0].read_chains == [
        ["untrusted_source:read", "tool:read_uploads", "sink:shell"]
    ]

"""The upload-core tests (B.3b-user_upload_core).

A package, unlike its sibling directories, because two of the module
names the brief asks for — `test_base` and `test_registry` — are also
